## Findings

- Three of my eight reviewer plants against the barrier get past it and read a red `gate` as final from an unregistered frame (`ev/reviewer-plants.txt`). The cause is that `Busy.__init__` checks emptiness only when the object is built, and `classify` trusts `isinstance(busy, Busy)` when it reads. The three are (1) `b = Busy(["x"]); b.clear()`, an in-place mutation of a non-empty Busy minted anywhere, (2) `copy.copy(gate_busy([], []))`, and (3) `Busy.__new__(Busy)`. Case (2) is within the body's disclosed residual ("an empty Busy that a real minter built from made-up runs"). Cases (1) and (3) are not, and they contradict the body's sentence that only `BUSY_MINTERS` "may create" an empty one. I judge them non-blocking. (3) is deliberate circumvention. (1) is in the same predicate domain as the carried residual: the barrier checks that a reading was stated, not that the value read is still the minted reading. A candidate fix is to make `Busy` immutable (a tuple subclass) or to record the mint on the instance and check it in `classify`. Re-measure: run the three plants from `ev/reviewer-plants.txt`. Each must raise `BlindRead`. Carry: R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE
- Six diff-mutant survivors from the body's `prepr.sh` draw are on lines this pass did not change (`git diff 3785b0d0 df4af48a` touches none of them). They are an equivalent settle constant, `sib` read for truthiness, the self-test call that `MUTANT_CMD` cannot see, and three fixture constants. I accept the body's disposition. Carry: dismissed: equivalent mutants and self-test fixture constants on lines this pass did not change

+## v7.1.15
+
+**Patch stamp: 16 merges since v7.1.14 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v7.1.14..HEAD | wc -l`): the supply switch now keeps its minimum run and pause, the mixing-valve target is labelled as a room temperature, boosts keep the learners clean while their heat settles, and the dashboard card folds its detail sections; the rest is tooling.**
+
+### #3512 The supply switch keeps a minimum run and a minimum pause (R10-OUTSIDE-SUPPLY-MIN-RUN-PAUSE)
+
+A re-solve, a cycle, a restart or a late write landing inside a plan step can no longer switch the supply off after a very short run or on after a very short pause, or start a run the plan ends straight away. A held write is retried each minute and lands once its minimum has passed; the intervals that ran differently from the plan are not learned from.
+
+### #3536 The mixing-valve target says it is a room temperature (R10-OUTSIDE-VALVE-TARGET-LABEL)
+
+The option is now named "Room temperature the mixing circuit holds" and its help states it is an indoor temperature, never a flow temperature. A value above the top of your comfort band raises a repair notice (nothing is changed, since it can be deliberate); README and the configuration docs say the same.
+
+### #3505 Boosts no longer leave slab heat in the learners (R10-OUTSIDE-LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2)
+
+After a space boost or the global boost mode ends, the learners stay frozen for a settling tail while the heat the boost put into the floor slab dies away, and that tail survives a restart. Installs that never boost store exactly what they did before.
+
+### #3441 The card folds its detail sections and moves the legend (R10-CARD-COLLAPSE)
+
+On the dashboard card, "Plan by reason" and "Why now" start folded under a one-line summary and open with a click, Enter or Space. The legend chips and their footnote now live in the enlarged view only; the tile shows the chart with the series you last left switched on.
+
+### Developer tooling, CI and audit machinery only
+
+#3552, #3550, #3490, #3541, #3528, #3545, #3516, #3525, #3543, #3540.
+
+### Record only
+
+#3548, #3542 (delivery rows, autofix).
+
+## v7.1.14
+
+**Patch stamp: duty-switch restart learning part B, mode before supply on, ECL110 MQTT off-neutral, and user-docs corrections; the rest is tooling.**
+
+### #3530 The pump arbiter writes the step's mode ahead of a supply switch-on (R10-MODE-BEFORE-SUPPLY-ON)
+
+The arbiter now writes the step's mode before it switches the supply on (#3420 part E).
+
+### #3534 The ECL110 MQTT off state is neutral (R10-ECL110-MQTT-OFF-NEUTRAL)
+
+The ECL110 topic publish drops its dead early return; the off arm needs no topic guard of its own.
+
+### #3524 The duty-switch learner publishes p and whole-episode n (R10-DUTY-SWITCH-RESTART-LEARNING, part B)
+
+The learner publishes the restart probability and the whole-episode count, with N_ON pinned as a decayed weight.
+
+### #3513 User docs verified (R10-USER-DOCS-VERIFY)
+
+Docs now state the mold-safe range as uncapped with the floor held at the target, and a two-probe average for a stratified combi store as an estimate of its mean.
+
+### Developer tooling, CI and audit machinery only
+
+#3515, #3535, #3492, #3377, #3510, #3533, #3498, #3522, #3503, #3523.
+
+### Record only
+
+#3537, #3527 (delivery rows, autofix).
+

diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/supply_hold.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/supply_hold.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..0bfa4d85ff
--- /dev/null
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/supply_hold.py
@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+"""The supply switch's minimum run and minimum pause.
+
+The plan switches the supply at its 15-minute step boundaries, but a
+re-solve, a cycle, a restart or a late write can land inside a step, and the
+supply switch bypasses the compressor's own interlocks. So the one gate the
+cycle and the step tick write through (``coordinator._write_supply``) holds a
+write back that would
+
+* end a run younger than :data:`MIN_RUN`;
+* end a pause younger than :data:`MIN_PAUSE`;
+* start a run the plan ends within :data:`MIN_RUN`: an on write inside a
+  step whose next step is planned off. Not where the step heats the tank
+  and the tank needs it now (:func:`tank_reason`): that run starts, and the
+  minimum carries it past the boundary.
+
+**One clock.** A run's and a pause's age is the switch's own ``last_changed``,
+as ``early_cutoff`` measures its minimum run, so a run started by a boost, a
+fixed mode, the user or the cut-off counts like one this gate wrote. A reload
+of the integration leaves the stamp alone. A restart of Home Assistant builds
+a new state machine whose first write stamps the restart
+(``tests/ha_contract.py``, ``StateMachine.async_set``), so a pump found
+running reads as a run that started then and is held on for at most
+:data:`MIN_RUN`, and a pump found stopped is held off for at most
+:data:`MIN_PAUSE`. A write that leaves the state keeps the stamp. A stamp missing or ahead of the clock is an unknown age and
+holds nothing (#775: unknowable, never 0).
+
+**Running and stopped** are read as ``pump_arbiter._pump_off`` reads them:
+``off`` is stopped, any other readable state is running, so a ``climate`` or
+``input_boolean`` target (``on_off_service``) is held like a switch.
+
+**Only a delay.** The gate never makes a write; it returns ``None`` for one it
+holds and sets :attr:`ArbiterState.supply_held`, and ``pump_arbiter.
+supply_tick`` retries it each minute with the step's own command, or the
+action's where the plan gives none, so it lands once its minimum has passed.
+A write of ``None``, a non-plan mode, a live boost, system identification and
+an unreadable switch pass unchanged. Both minimums sit below the plan's step,
+so a write on a step boundary after a step-long run or pause is never held.
+
+**The learners.** A held interval ran other than the plan commanded, so
+:func:`freeze_reason` freezes it through ``_learning_frozen``
+(:data:`FREEZE_HELD`), as ``early_cutoff`` freezes a cut one.
+
+The minimums are constants, not options, for the reason ``early_cutoff``
+gives for its margin; ``early_cutoff`` reads them too.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+from typing import Any
+
+from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+
+from .boost import CHANNEL_DHW, CHANNEL_SPACE
+from .const import MODE_AUTO, MODE_ECONOMY
+from .entry_config import EntryConfig
+from .plan_step import PLAN_STEP_MINUTES, plan_step_start
+from .pump_arbiter import ArbiterInputs, ArbiterState, step_duty, step_supply, supply_switch
+
+#: The shortest run and pause the gate lets a write end; the early cut-off's too.
+MIN_RUN = timedelta(minutes=10)
+MIN_PAUSE = timedelta(minutes=10)
+
+#: The ``_learning_frozen`` reason for an interval in which a write was held.
+FREEZE_HELD = "supply_held"
+
+#: Switch states that say nothing about the pump.
+_UNREADABLE = (None, "unavailable", "unknown")
+
+
+def hold_supply(held: ArbiterState, inputs: Any, boosts: Any, value: bool | None,
+                now: datetime | None = None) -> bool | None:
+    """``value``, or ``None`` while a minimum holds the write back.
+
+    ``inputs`` is the coordinator's ``arbiter_inputs`` builder, called only
+    for a write that is not ``None``.
+    """
+    held.supply_held = False
+    if value is None:
+        return value
+    now = dt_util.as_utc(now or dt_util.now())
+    inp = inputs()
+    age = _held_for(inp, value, now)
+    if age is None or _passes(inp, boosts, now):
+        return value
+    wait = (age < MIN_PAUSE or _ends_soon(inp, boosts, now)) if value else age < MIN_RUN
+    if wait:
+        held.supply_held, held.held_until = True, now + _freeze_span(inp.config)
+    return None if wait else value
+
+
+def freeze_reason(held: ArbiterState, now: datetime | None = None) -> str | None:
+    """:data:`FREEZE_HELD` while a learner's interval may have had a write held, else ``None``."""
+    until = held.held_until
+    held_now = until is not None and dt_util.as_utc(now or dt_util.now()) < until
+    return FREEZE_HELD if held_now else None
+
+
+def _freeze_span(config: Any) -> timedelta:
+    """Two plan intervals, as ``early_cutoff.CutoffState.interval_cut`` counts
+    the open cycle and the one just closed: freezing one too many is the
+    fail-closed side. Fixed when the write is held, where the config is in hand.
+    """
+    return 2 * timedelta(minutes=EntryConfig.from_mapping(config).optimization_interval)
+
+
+def tank_reason(inp: ArbiterInputs) -> str | None:
+    """Why the tank must be heated now: a disinfection hold or a cold tank."""
+    if inp.disinfecting:
+        return "disinfecting"
+    params = inp.params
+    cold = getattr(params, "dhw_enabled", False) and float(inp.state.dhw_temperature) < float(
+        params.dhw_min_temp
+    )
+    return "tank_cold" if cold else None
+
+
+def _held_for(inp: ArbiterInputs, value: bool, now: datetime) -> timedelta | None:
+    """How long the switch has been in the state ``value`` would end, or ``None``.
+
+    ``None`` where the write changes nothing, the switch is unreadable or its
+    stamp is missing or ahead of ``now``.
+    """
+    switch = supply_switch(inp)
+    state = getattr(switch, "state", None)
+    if state in _UNREADABLE or (state != "off") is value:
+        return None
+    return switch_age(switch, now)
+
+
+def switch_age(switch: Any, now: datetime) -> timedelta | None:
+    """How long the switch has held its value, by its ``last_changed``, or ``None``.
+
+    The run length is the age of the VALUE: ``inputs.state_stamp`` answers
+    when the entity was last heard from, which a re-reported ``on`` resets.
+    A stamp missing or ahead of ``now`` is unknowable, never 0 (#775).
+    """
+    since = getattr(switch, "last_changed", None)
+    if since is None:
+        return None
+    since, now = dt_util.as_utc(since), dt_util.as_utc(now)
+    return None if since > now else now - since
+
+
+def _passes(inp: ArbiterInputs, boosts: Any, now: datetime) -> bool:
+    """A write the gate never holds: a non-plan mode, an experiment, a boost."""
+    return (inp.mode not in (MODE_AUTO, MODE_ECONOMY)
+            or (inp.action or {}).get("mode") == "system_identification"
+            or boosts.active(CHANNEL_SPACE, now) or boosts.active(CHANNEL_DHW, now))
+
+
+def _ends_soon(inp: ArbiterInputs, boosts: Any, now: datetime) -> bool:
+    """A start whose run the plan ends within :data:`MIN_RUN`, the tank not owed it."""
+    nxt = plan_step_start(now) + timedelta(minutes=PLAN_STEP_MINUTES)
+    if nxt - now >= MIN_RUN or step_supply(inp, boosts, nxt) is not False:
+        return False
+    return not (step_duty(inp.plan, now) in ("dhw", "both") and tank_reason(inp))

       "title": "The downstairs temperature is modelled, not measured",
       "description": "Two-zone planning is on and no lower-floor thermometer is configured, so the lower zone starts from the main room sensor and is carried forward by the thermal model — the “Lower floor (modelled)” trace on the plan chart. What a modelled zone cannot do is correct itself, so over a long cold spell it can drift from the real downstairs. Assigning “Lower floor temperature sensor” under the zone options closes that loop; this notice clears when you do."

Nothing is broken — the optimizer prices these bounds rather than enforcing them, so the plan keeps running, just in permanent slight violation of a band it can never satisfy. Nothing has been changed for you either: which of the two numbers is the wrong one is yours to say. Correct them under the temperature options and this notice clears on the next cycle."

+/** One headline fold (R10-CARD-COLLAPSE): a header button that names the
+* section and carries its one-line summary whether unfolded or not, and the
+ * body only while unfolded -- genuinely unrendered when folded, as the dialog's hidden

-The audit measures the integration with instruments that are themselves code:
-`tests/hastub`, the gate's checks and budgets, the harness contract, the lint
-lanes, this toolkit. A defect your dimension's method meets in one of those is a
-finding **of your dimension**, under the same bar as any other — executed number,
-instrumented symbol, perturbation, metric definition, control — and not a
-paragraph of prose in your report.

-accused check fire has not refuted the finding; say which you could not separate.

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..14d157de2c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+"""The house heat-loss scale's walk under each settling-tail policy, per press arm.
+
+R10-OUTSIDE-LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2's measurement, on tests/boost_drift_replay.py's
+own replay: every arm forks from one shared pre-boost state; on each boost day a
+space press at each window start, held ``minutes`` and cancelled (the whole
+window expires instead), ``count`` presses one cycle apart. ``press`` arms drive
+the true house with the boost for the share of each cycle the press held it;
+``freeze`` arms run the same presses and tails with the house on the plan, the
+freeze with no boost heat behind it.
+
+A policy replaces ``BoostState.settle`` for the arm's run, except
+``production``, which runs the tree's own:
+
+- ``full``: the full tail from every boost's end, whatever its length;
+- ``none``: no tail;
+- ``slope6h``: ``12 h + 6 h * ln(boosted / 2 h)``, floor 1.5 h, on the boosted
+  sum (the adopted formula, commit 7a76f66c8a);
+- ``slope3h``: ``12 h + 3 h * ln(boosted / 2 h)``, floor 1.5 h, each press
+  priced at no less than 10 minutes (commit 36f10fd3ba).
+
+Each arm prints ``worst`` (the largest signed excursion of a later 03:00 daily
+row from the one before the first boost day) and ``final``. Two verdicts:
+
+- ``PRODUCTION`` reads EQUAL when every production arm's summary equals its
+  ``full`` twin's. Its null control is the ``none`` policy: at least one press
+  arm under ``none`` must differ from ``full``, or the comparison is blind
+  (exit 1 either way it fails).
+- ``BOUND`` per scaled press arm: ``|worst|`` no larger than
+  ``press_120x1_full``'s (the brief's absolute acceptance). Printed, not exited
+  on; the round-11 precondition a scaled formula must meet.
+
+    PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:tests:custom_components \\
+        python3 dev/audit/harnesses/boost_press_tail_walk.py [policy ...]
+
+Default policies ``production full none``. Every arm replays the cycles past
+the shared prefix with a production solve each; it is a harness, not a gate
+script.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+import sys
+from datetime import timedelta
+
+import boost_drift_replay as bdr
+
+from heatpump_optimizer.drift import utc_elapsed_seconds, utc_shift
+
+boost_mod = bdr.boost_mod
+LENGTHS = ((10, 1), (30, 1), (60, 1), (120, 1), (10, 4))
+WINDOW = timedelta(hours=boost_mod.BOOST_HOURS)
+FULL = boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL
+FLOOR = timedelta(hours=1.5)
+
+
+def _scaled(slope: timedelta):
+    def tail(boosted):
+        if boosted is None or boosted >= WINDOW:
+            return FULL
+        if boosted <= timedelta(0):
+            return FLOOR
+        return max(FLOOR, FULL + slope * math.log(boosted / WINDOW))
+    return tail
+
+
+def _settle_with(tail_of, press_min=timedelta(0)):
+    """``BoostState.settle`` with the tail ``tail_of(boosted sum)``."""
+    def settle(self, end, since):
+        if since is None or self.space_boosted is None:
+            self.space_boosted = None
+        else:
+            self.space_boosted += max(press_min, timedelta(seconds=utc_elapsed_seconds(end, since)))
+        until = utc_shift(end, tail_of(self.space_boosted))
+        held = self.space_settle_until
+        if held is None or utc_elapsed_seconds(until, held) > 0:
+            self.space_settle_until = until
+    return settle
+
+
+POLICIES = {
+    "production": None,
+    "full": _settle_with(lambda _b: FULL),
+    "none": _settle_with(lambda _b: timedelta(0)),
+    "slope6h": _settle_with(_scaled(FULL / 2)),
+    "slope3h": _settle_with(_scaled(FULL / 4), press_min=timedelta(minutes=10)),
+}
+
+
+def walk(out: dict) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    daily = out["daily"]
+    pre = daily[bdr.BOOST_DAYS[0] - 1]
+    later = [v / pre - 1.0 for d, v in sorted(daily.items()) if d >= bdr.BOOST_DAYS[0]]
+    return max(later, key=abs, default=0.0), out["hh_final"] / pre - 1.0
+
+
+def comparable(out: dict) -> dict:
+    """The arm's summary without its name, which differs between any two arms."""
+    return {k: ([s.as_dict() for s in v] if k in ("tagged", "untagged") else v)
+            for k, v in out.items() if k != "arm"}
+
+
+def run(policy: str) -> dict:
+    arms = {f"{kind}_{m}x{c}_{policy}": f"{kind}:{m}:{c}"
+            for m, c in LENGTHS for kind in ("press", "freeze")}
+    production = boost_mod.BoostState.settle
+    if POLICIES[policy] is not None:
+        boost_mod.BoostState.settle = POLICIES[policy]
+    try:
+        return bdr.replay(arms)
+    finally:
+        boost_mod.BoostState.settle = production
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    policies = sys.argv[1:] or ["production", "full", "none"]
+    outs = bdr.replay({"null_no_boost": "none"})
+    for policy in policies:
+        outs.update(run(policy))
+    for arm, out in outs.items():
+        w = walk(out)
+        print(f"WALK {arm}: worst {w[0]:+.4f}, final {w[1]:+.4f}, daily {out['daily']}")
+    status = 0
+    if "production" in policies and "full" in policies:
+        pairs = [(a, a[: -len("production")] + "full") for a in outs if a.endswith("_production")]
+        same = [comparable(outs[a]) == comparable(outs[b]) for a, b in pairs]
+        print(f"PRODUCTION: {'EQUAL' if all(same) else 'DIFFERS'} to full on "
+              f"{sum(same)} of {len(pairs)} arms")
+        status |= 0 if all(same) else 1
+    if "none" in policies and "full" in policies:
+        moved = [a for a in outs if a.startswith("press_") and a.endswith("_none")
+                 and comparable(outs[a]) != comparable(outs[a[: -len("none")] + "full"])]
+        print(f"NULL CONTROL: none differs from full on {len(moved)} press arm(s): "
+              f"{'SEES' if moved else 'BLIND'}")
+        status |= 0 if moved else 1
+    whole = walk(outs["press_120x1_full"])[0] if "press_120x1_full" in outs else math.nan
+    for arm in (a for a in outs if a.startswith("press_") and a.split("_")[-1] in ("slope6h", "slope3h")):
+        w = walk(outs[arm])[0]
+        print(f"BOUND {arm}: |{w:+.4f}| vs |{whole:+.4f}|: "
+              f"{'PASS' if abs(w) <= abs(whole) else 'FAIL'}")
+    return status
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_tail_mutants.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_tail_mutants.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..52369cd1ea
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/boost_tail_mutants.py
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+"""R10-OUTSIDE-LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2's mutation proof, reproducible.
+
+Each mutant replaces one line of custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/boost.py
+in place, runs the part's block of tests/features.py through
+tools/audit/seat/features_block.py, and restores the file. It prints each
+mutant's exit status and the names of the checks that went red. ``M0`` is the
+null mutant (a comment edit) and must fail nothing; every other mutant must
+fail at least one check or raise: either exits non-zero, and a raise
+prints its last line.
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/boost_tail_mutants.py
+
+Run from the repository root on a clean checkout; the file is restored even
+when a run raises.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import pathlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+BOOST = pathlib.Path("custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/boost.py")
+START = "# #1935 follow-up (R10-OUTSIDE-LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2)"
+END = "# A hot-water charge inside a counter span (the dwell saw it)"
+MUTANTS = {
+    "M0-null (comment edit)": (
+        "        # Unreadable boosted time reads as a start nobody saw: unknown.\n",
+        "        # Unreadable boosted time reads as a start nobody saw: unknown (null mutant).\n"),
+    "M1-short-tail (a boost summed under 2 h owes 1.5 h)": (
+        "        until = utc_shift(end, SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL)\n",
+        "        until = utc_shift(end, SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL if self.space_boosted is None"
+        " or self.space_boosted >= timedelta(hours=2) else timedelta(hours=1.5))\n"),
+    "M2-sum-dropped (each boost counted alone)": (
+        "            self.space_boosted += timedelta(seconds=utc_elapsed_seconds(end, since))\n",
+        "            self.space_boosted = timedelta(seconds=utc_elapsed_seconds(end, since))\n"),
+    "M3-persisted-tail-dropped": (
+        "    if held.space_settle_until is not None:\n        boosted = held.space_boosted\n",
+        "    if False:\n        boosted = held.space_boosted\n"),
+    "M4-restore-dropped": (
+        "    _restore_settle(held, raw, now)\n",
+        "    pass\n"),
+    "M5-sum-never-clears": (
+        "            self.space_settle_until, self.space_boosted = None, timedelta(0)\n",
+        "            self.space_settle_until = None\n"),
+    # The fix review's survivors at 594238bf, by its numbering.
+    "X1-sum-cleared-under-live-overlay": (
+        "                and CHANNEL_SPACE not in self.until and self.mode_since is None):\n",
+        "                and self.mode_since is None):\n"),
+    "X2-sum-cleared-under-live-mode": (
+        "                and CHANNEL_SPACE not in self.until and self.mode_since is None):\n",
+        "                and CHANNEL_SPACE not in self.until):\n"),
+    "X3-start-restamped-on-extension": (
+        "            if channel == CHANNEL_SPACE and not self.active(channel, now):\n",
+        "            if channel == CHANNEL_SPACE:\n"),
+    "X4-mode-exit-not-saved": (
+        "        if old == MODE_BOOST:\n            _schedule_persist(coord)\n",
+        "        if False:\n            _schedule_persist(coord)\n"),
+    "X5-cycle-saves-only-on-release": (
+        "    if released or held.space_settle_until != tail:\n",
+        "    if released:\n"),
+    "X7-tail-shortened": (
+        "        if held is None or utc_elapsed_seconds(until, held) > 0:\n",
+        "        if True:\n"),
+    "X11-negative-sum-restored": (
+        "not isinstance(hours, bool) and 0.0 <= hours < math.inf else None)",
+        "not isinstance(hours, bool) and hours < math.inf else None)"),
+    "X13-mode-entry-keeps-spent-sum": (
+        "        if live:\n            self._clear_spent(now)\n",
+        "        if live:\n            pass\n"),
+    # The ledger inventory's BOOLOP sites (``and`` to ``or``), which
+    # tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py does not draw.
+    "B240-press-start-boolop": (
+        "            if channel == CHANNEL_SPACE and not self.active(channel, now):\n",
+        "            if channel == CHANNEL_SPACE or not self.active(channel, now):\n"),
+    "B502-payload-start-boolop": (
+        "    if held.space_since is not None and CHANNEL_SPACE in held.until:\n",
+        "    if held.space_since is not None or CHANNEL_SPACE in held.until:\n"),
+    "B549-restore-tail-boolop": (
+        "    if until is not None and dt_util.as_utc(until) > dt_util.as_utc(now):\n",
+        "    if until is not None or dt_util.as_utc(until) > dt_util.as_utc(now):\n"),
+    "B557-restore-start-boolop": (
+        "    if since is not None and CHANNEL_SPACE in held.until:\n",
+        "    if since is not None or CHANNEL_SPACE in held.until:\n"),
+    "B560-restore-ended-boolop": (
+        "    if end is not None and CHANNEL_SPACE not in held.until:\n",
+        "    if end is not None or CHANNEL_SPACE not in held.until:\n"),
+}
+
+
+def block(prelude: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
+    return subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, "tools/audit/seat/features_block.py", START, END, "--prelude", prelude],
+        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600,
+        # Two mutants of one size written inside one second would otherwise
+        # share a cached .pyc: the second run would measure the first mutant.
+        env=dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1"))
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        out = pathlib.Path(d) / "prelude.py"
+        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "tools/audit/seat/features_block.py", START, END,
+                        "--emit-prelude", str(out)], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=600)
+        prelude = out.read_text()
+    orig = BOOST.read_text()
+    status = 0
+    for name, (a, b) in MUTANTS.items():
+        if orig.count(a) != 1:
+            print(f"{name}: SITE NOT FOUND")
+            status = 1
+            continue
+        BOOST.write_text(orig.replace(a, b))
+        try:
+            r = block(prelude)
+        finally:
+            BOOST.write_text(orig)
+        fails = [ln.strip() for ln in r.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip().startswith("FAIL")]
+        print(f"{name}: exit {r.returncode}, {len(fails)} check(s) red")
+        for f in fails:
+            print(f"    {f[:160]}")
+        if r.returncode != 0 and not fails:
+            print(f"    raised: {(r.stderr.strip().splitlines() or ['-'])[-1][:160]}")
+        killed = r.returncode != 0
+        if name.startswith("M0") == killed:
+            status = 1
+    print("MUTANTS: " + ("as expected" if status == 0 else "UNEXPECTED"))
+    return status
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

 from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import (

           f"warm+on {over_on} min  held {dict(+held_why)}")
 
 
+def run_supply(variant: str, profile: str, gate: bool) -> None:
+    """One day of the supply switch under staggered cycles, gate off or on."""
+    phase, step = int(os.environ.get("CYCLE_PHASE_MIN", 7)), timedelta(minutes=15)
+    ctrl, plant = ThermalModel(params()), ThermalModel(params(
+        1.4 if variant == "HOT" else 1.0, LIGHT_MASS_SCALE if variant == "LIGHT" else 1.0))
+    cfg = OptimizationConfig(horizon_hours=24, time_step_minutes=15, target_temp=21.0,
+                             min_temp=18.0, max_temp=23.0, comfort_temp_day=21.0,

+    sim_start = START + timedelta(minutes=phase)
+    # last_updated an hour back: the first write is never held by an unset clock
+    hass = FakeHass({SWITCH: FakeState("off", last_updated=sim_start - timedelta(hours=1)),
+                     ROOM: FakeState("21.0")})
+    out = COLD_OUT if variant == "LIGHT" else OUT
+    # a run carried past a planned stop: the variant's own minimum, else the model's p_min
+    # (house(heat_pump_min_power=1.0) in params())
+    own = {"OWNMIN": PUMP_OWN_KW, "HOT": HOT_OWN_KW, "LIGHT": PUMP_OWN_KW}.get(variant)
+    carried = own if own is not None else 1.0
+    room, slab, ctrl_slab = 21.0, 22.0, 22.0
+    plan = plan_t0 = inp = None
+    cmd = last = None
+    is_held = False
+    n_held = episodes = booked = past_stop = pump_e = 0.0
+    rooms, trans = [], []
+    levels: list[float] = []
+
+    def decide(now: datetime, value: bool) -> None:
+        nonlocal n_held, episodes, is_held
+        if gate:
+            res = supply_hold.hold_supply(st_held, lambda: inp, boosts, value, now=now)
+            was, is_held = is_held, res is None
+            n_held += is_held
+            episodes += is_held and not was
+            if res is None:
+                return
+        cur = hass.states.get(SWITCH)
+        if (cur.state == "on") != value:
+            hass.states.set(SWITCH, FakeState("on" if value else "off", last_updated=now))
+            trans.append(now)
+
+    for m in range(SIM_STEPS * 15):
+        now = sim_start + timedelta(minutes=m)
+        s0 = now - timedelta(minutes=(now - START).total_seconds() // 60 % 15)
+        if m % 30 == 0:  # a cycle, at the harness's old resolution but off the step grid
+            k = int((s0 - START) / step)
+            st = ThermalState(room_temperature=room, slab_temperature=ctrl_slab, outdoor_temperature=out,
+                              upper_floor_temperature=room, lower_floor_temperature=room,
+                              buffer_tank_temperature=35.0)
+            z = np.zeros(N)
+            plan = opt.optimize(inputs=solve_inputs(initial_state=st, prices=pr2[k:k + N],
+                                                    outdoor_temps=np.full(N, out), wind_speeds=z,
+                                                    precipitation=z, solar_radiation=z, start_time=s0))
+            plan_t0 = s0
+            levels = [float(x) for x in plan.power_schedule]
+            ctrl_slab = float(plan.slab_temp_trajectory[2]) if len(plan.slab_temp_trajectory) > 2 else ctrl_slab
+            cmd = levels[0] > MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW
+            inp = ArbiterInputs(hass=hass, config={"indoor_temp_entity": ROOM,
+                                                   "heat_pump_switch_entity": SWITCH,
+                                                   "optimization_interval": 30},
+                                mode=MODE_AUTO, plan=plan, plan_stale=False, entry_released=False,
+                                state=st, thermal=ctrl, params=ctrl.params,
+                                action={"heat_pump_on": cmd}, measured_power_kw=None,
+                                disinfecting=False)
+            decide(now, cmd)
+            last = cmd
+        else:
+            idx = int((s0 - plan_t0) / step)
+            now_cmd = levels[idx] > MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW
+            if is_held and gate or (m % 15 == (-phase) % 15 and now_cmd != last):
+                last = now_cmd
+                decide(now, now_cmd)  # the step tick's write or the held write's retry
+        level = levels[int((s0 - plan_t0) / step)]
+        on = hass.states.get(SWITCH).state == "on"
+        if not on:
+            booked += (level > MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW) * level / 60
+            use = 0.0
+        elif level > MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW:
+            use = max(level, own) if own is not None else level
+        else:
+            use = carried
+            past_stop += use / 60
+        pst = ThermalState(room_temperature=room, slab_temperature=slab, outdoor_temperature=out,
+                           upper_floor_temperature=room, lower_floor_temperature=room,
+                           buffer_tank_temperature=35.0)
+        traj = plant.simulate_trajectory(pst, np.array([use]), wx(1, 0.0, out), dt_hours=1 / 60)
+        room, slab = float(traj[0][-1]), float(traj[1][-1])
+        rooms.append(room)
+        pump_e += use / 60
+    spans = [(b - a).total_seconds() / 60 for a, b in zip(trans, trans[1:], strict=False)]
+    # the switch starts off, so transitions alternate on, off, ...: even spans are runs;
+    # only intervals closed by two transitions are counted
+    runs = sum(1 for i, d in enumerate(spans) if d < 10 and i % 2 == 0)
+    pauses = sum(1 for i, d in enumerate(spans) if d < 10 and i % 2 == 1)
+    per_day = n_held * 1440 / (SIM_STEPS * 15)
+    # the tank is fixed at 35.0 in this harness, so the min tank figure is not informative
+    print(f"{variant:7s} {profile:14s} gate {'on' if gate else 'off':3s} held/day {per_day:5.1f} "
+          f"episodes {int(episodes):3d}  writes {len(trans):3d}  short runs {runs:2d} pauses {pauses:2d}  "
+          f"booked-not-delivered {booked:6.2f} kWh  run-past-stop {past_stop:6.2f} kWh  "
+          f"pump {pump_e:6.1f} kWh  room min {min(rooms):5.2f}  tank min {35.0:5.2f}")
+
+
+if os.environ.get("SUPPLY_HOLD") == "1":
+    print(f"mild day {OUT} degC, supply gate, cycles at minute {os.environ.get('CYCLE_PHASE_MIN', 7)} + 30 j; "
+          "early cut-off not armed; tank fixed at 35.0")
+    for kind in sys.argv[1:] or ("NULL", "HOT", "LIGHT"):
+        for profile in ("winter_typical", "flat"):
+            for gate in (False, True):
+                run_supply(kind, profile, gate)
+    sys.exit()
 print(f"mild day {OUT} degC, model p_min 1.0, comfort 21 day / 19.5 night; slab open-loop; "
       "plant stepped per minute")
 for kind in sys.argv[1:] or ("NULL", "OWNMIN", "HOT", "SUN", "COLDSUN", "LIGHT"):

diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..ded48ca794
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/CENSUS.md
@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
+# R11-PROTECTION-CENSUS (round 10): the required set, sorted by what each check reads
+
+Read-only study, no production or tool code. Written without `gh` or an API
+token. The classification below needs none: each check's steps are in the tree.
+Only the per-head check conclusions of PRs outside the ledger, and the job logs
+of the main `tests / ci-ratchet` reds, are **UNREAD**.
+
+## Rule (applied to every check, never to a name)
+
+A check is **product** when a step of its job runs the shipped code or its
+metadata: `custom_components/`, `blueprints/`, the card, the HA manifest, HACS
+metadata. It is **programme** when its steps read only the governance corpus,
+pull-request bodies, rosters, the test-selection machinery, CI timings or
+archscore. A job with both says so; it is placed by its purpose and the
+mixed part is named.
+
+## Sources and enumerators
+
+| figure | enumerator | prints |
+|---|---|---|
+| required contexts | `python3 -c "import json;r=json.load(open('tools/ci/fixtures/ruleset/ruleset_23698884.json'));print(len([c for x in r['rules'] if x['type']=='required_status_checks' for c in x['parameters']['required_status_checks']]))"` | 17 |
+| recorded test scripts / scripts whose closure reaches `custom_components/` or `blueprints/` | `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('tests/closures.json'))['closures'];p=[k for k,v in d.items() if any(f.startswith(('custom_components/','blueprints/')) for f in v)];print(len(d),len(p))"` | 33 29 |
+| the 4 scripts that reach no product file | same, `sorted(set(d)-set(p))` | `tests/arch_score.py tests/ha_contract.py tests/layout.py tests/md_tables.mjs` |
+| main-push red-job rows | `python3 -I dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py \| wc -l` | 28 |
+| ... by run conclusion and job | `... main_reds.py \| awk '{print $3,$4}' \| sort \| uniq -c` | 8 failure `gate`, 8 failure `tests` (the ci-ratchet job), 6 cancelled `gate`, 6 cancelled `tests` |
+| PR-head ledger | `tail -1 dev/audit/rca/ci-red/entries_v7.1.2.tsv` | `ENTRIES 18 PRS 14` |
+| `harness_headers.py` reds | `grep -c harness_headers dev/audit/rca/ci-red/entries_v7.1.2.tsv` | 4 (#3180, #3189, #3208, #3242) |
+| delivery files, all rounds | `ls dev/programme/delivery \| wc -l` | 1614 (no round-10 denominator is claimed) |
+
+Null control: `main_reds.py | awk '$1==4080||$1==4107||$1==4116' | wc -l` prints 0 (those runs are `success`).
+
+## The 17 required contexts, classified (9 product, 8 programme)
+
+Context list: the ruleset fixture named in the first enumerator row.
+
+| # | context | job (file:line) | what its steps run | side |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `fast (3.14)` | tests.yml:163 | `tests/run.sh` with RUN_PART=fast; 29 of 33 recorded scripts reach product files; `arch_score*.py` are skipped here (run.sh:657-659), `layout.py`, `md_tables.mjs`, `ha_contract.py` run here and read no product file | **product**, mixed: also runs programme-rule scripts (`harness_headers.py`, instrument self-tests) |
+| 2 | `browser` | tests.yml:503 | `tests/plan_view.py`, `tests/card_browser.mjs` (card layout in Chromium) | **product** |
+| 3 | `typing` | tests.yml:675 | `tests/typing_ruler.py` (mypy --strict ruler, three ratcheted numbers) | **product** |
+| 4 | `mutation` | tests.yml:1036 | `tests/mutation_table.py` over production files the diff touched | **product** |
+| 5 | `hassfest` | hassfest.yml:14 | `home-assistant/actions/hassfest` on the manifest | **product** |
+| 6 | `validate-hacs` | validate.yml:14 | `hacs/action` | **product** |
+| 7-9 | `Analyze (actions)`, `(javascript-typescript)`, `(python)` | codeql.yml `analyze` | CodeQL over the tree; `tools/pr/codeql_scope.py` decides skip-with-stand-in. The python and javascript legs read product code; the `actions` leg reads the workflows (programme files). Counted product as a set; the `actions` leg is the exception. | **product** (3), `actions` leg reads programme files |
+| 10 | `briefs` | tests.yml:602 | `tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs` over wave rosters | **programme** |
+| 11 | `closure-scope` | tests.yml:1749 | `tests/lane_skip.py`, `tests/closure.py`: decides which lanes may skip | **programme** (test-selection machinery) |
+| 12 | `closures` | tests.yml:1966 | `tests/derive_closures.sh` and `closure.py`: re-records and checks the measured closures | **programme** |
+| 13 | `policy-docs` | governance.yml:61 | policy lint, rules_sync, fragments_sync, machinery ratchet, CODEOWNERS gap | **programme** |
+| 14 | `wave-script` | governance.yml:1664 | `check-wave-script.mjs`, agreement lane, `fold_ledger.py` | **programme** |
+| 15 | `env-matrix` | governance.yml:1552 | `policy_lint_envmatrix.mjs`: declared environment shapes of the governance checks | **programme** |
+| 16 | `pr-contract` | pr-contract.yml:40 | PR-body contract, figure lint, version-edit refusal, `carry_audit.py`; **also** `tools/ci/codescan_wait.py` lists the open code-scanning alerts as reds | **programme**, with one product duty: it is the only check that turns a CodeQL alert into a red |
+| 17 | `budget-raise-gate` | budget-raise-gate.yml:57 | `tools/policy/budget_raise_gate.py`: owner approval of a budget raise | **programme** |
+
+Sizing for round 11: the product-only set is contexts 1-9 (9 of 17, 8 dropped).
+Two decisions the study cannot make and a round-11 seat must: (a) the CodeQL
+alert duty of `pr-contract` (row 16) has no home in a product-only set unless it
+is moved into the CodeQL legs or kept; (b) `fast` still grades programme-rule
+scripts (`harness_headers.py`, instrument self-tests), so splitting those out of
+`fast` is a further move, priced by the 5 `fast` reds below that those scripts
+caused. `hassfest` and `pr-contract` also have a second definition in ci.yml
+(224, 270); the ruleset names the context, not the file.
+
+## Not required contexts that appear in the ledgers
+
+| name | read | side |
+|---|---|---|
+| `tests / ci-ratchet` | tests.yml:2301-2318: runs only on push to `refs/heads/main`, comment says not a required context; `tests/ci_ratchet.py` docstring: measures `script_runs_per_push` and `critical_path_minutes` from Actions run timings, plus archscore counts | **programme instrument**, not required |
+| `gate` | not in the 17 and its steps were not read in this study | **UNREAD**, not required |
+| `tests / replay`, `prelude`, `instrument-self-tests` | not in the 17 | not required; steps UNREAD |
+
+## Main-push reds (28 rows, 14 runs)
+
+Each of the 14 runs carries a red `tests / ci-ratchet` job and a red `gate`.
+Runs 4009, 4015, 4028, 4035, 4046, 4055, 4056, 4128 concluded `failure`; runs
+4036, 4037, 4038, 4040, 4044, 4045 concluded `cancelled`. In all six cancelled
+runs the `tests / ci-ratchet` job itself concluded `failure` (counted from
+`runs_red4.json` job conclusions by `main_reds.py`, which prints only
+`failure` jobs and printed all 14), so "cancelled" is the run's conclusion and
+says nothing of the job's cause. Cause of every one of the 14 ci-ratchet reds:
+**UNREAD** (job logs are not in the tree). No infrastructure class is assigned.
+
+Class: the 14 ci-ratchet rows are reds of a **programme instrument** that is
+not a required context; the 14 `gate` rows are not a required context either.
+These 28 rows are therefore exactly the class a product-only set stops
+grading, not rows "said nothing about". They are not a product-check signal.
+
+## PR-head reds (18 rows) re-sorted by required context
+
+Same rows and same causes as the previous cut; the new column is the side of
+the required context that carried the red (1-17 above), or "n/r" for a name
+outside the 17. Class column unchanged where the cause is read.
+
+| PR | head | red | class | context side |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 3167 | 7637d66 | tests / replay | real catch (timing budget; runner noise possible) | n/r |
+| 3167 | 4e4bb29 | gate | infrastructure (cancelled run) | n/r |
+| 3180 | 3f7777a | tests / fast, tests / closures | real catch: `harness_headers.py` rule on the PR's own harness | `fast` (product, but cause is a programme rule) + `closures` (programme) |
+| 3181 | bb730c1 | gate | infrastructure (CodeQL python cancelled) | n/r (the cancelled leg is product) |
+| 3189 | fd9c5ba | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3195 | 6f742a3 | tests / typing | real catch (9 no-untyped-call) | **product** |
+| 3195 | c383169 | prelude, gate | infrastructure (prelude wait expired); also real: 8 unpinned sites | n/r |
+| 3195 | 611e1aa | gate (tests / mutation) | real catch (unpinned-site refusal; cured by bot commit) | **product** (`mutation`, via `gate`) |
+| 3204 | e5381d9 | gate | infrastructure (cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3208 | 327d83e | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3211 | 1fca63c | gate | infrastructure (PR closed, run cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3217 | 1c42ca3 | gate | infrastructure (CodeQL python cancelled) | n/r |
+| 3219 | aca5009 | gate | infrastructure (+ body defect) | n/r |
+| 3227 | a52354e | instrument-self-tests, fast | real catch (`body_patch.sh:146`) | `fast`, cause is a programme script |
+| 3240 | 79cf40f | gate | grader skew | n/r |
+| 3242 | e836876 | tests / fast | real catch (`harness_headers.py`) | product check, programme-rule cause |
+| 3244 | a258212 | gate | grader skew | n/r |
+| 3244 | 8bc540e | pr-contract / gate | real catch (CodeQL alert 50, `py/jinja2/autoescape-false`) | **programme** context carrying a product-code alert |
+
+Counts, each by hand from the table (18 rows): real catch 9, infrastructure 7,
+grader skew 2.
+
+Rows moved by the re-applied rule (all prior classes kept, sides added or
+changed):
+- the 28 main-push rows: from "product check `ci-ratchet`" to programme
+  instrument, non-required (the block);
+- 3180 `tests / closures` is programme (it was not separated);
+- the 5 `fast` rows (#3180, #3189, #3208, #3227, #3242) are a product check
+  whose red was caused by a programme rule or script, not by product code:
+  `grep -c harness_headers` is 4 (the 5th is `body_patch.sh` in #3227);
+- 3244 `pr-contract` is a programme context whose red was a product-code alert;
+- `gate`, `replay`, `prelude`, `instrument-self-tests` are placed "n/r", not
+  guessed.
+
+## Which reds would have reached main under a product-only set (contexts 1-9)?
+
+Rows whose every required red is programme or n/r stop being graded: 3167
+(both), 3181, 3195 c383169, 3204, 3211, 3217, 3219, 3240, 3244 a258212, and
+3244 8bc540e: **11 of 18**. Rows with a product context graded: 3180, 3189,
+3195 6f742a3, 3195 611e1aa, 3208, 3227, 3242: **7 of 18** (11 + 7 = 18).
+Among the 11: infrastructure 7, grader skew 2, real catch 2. One real catch
+is **3167 `tests / replay`**, which is n/r today, so no required-set change
+touches it. The other is **3244 8bc540e**, the CodeQL alert enforced only by
+`pr-contract`: the one catch a product-only set loses unless the alert duty
+moves (decision (a) above).
+
+Verdict: **the ledgers do not show a product-only set missing a catch except
+via `pr-contract`'s alert duty**; 28 main-push rows and 11 PR rows are
+programme or non-required reds. Decision stays tvofi's.
+
+## Limits
+
+14 PRs are covered; per-head conclusions for the rest need the API
+(`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_red_list_lag.py --rows`, needs a token), classed by
+the table above. The `gate` job and the n/r names were not read.
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..2270934e0e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Rows for the main-push side of the census: one row per red job per ci.yml
+push run in runs_red4.json. A run with no red job yields no row (null control).
+    python3 -I dev/audit/rounds/round10/protection-census/main_reds.py
+"""
+import json, pathlib
+p = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "harnesses/r10_rca_ci_critpath_3/runs_red4.json"
+for r in json.load(open(p))["workflow_runs"]:
+    for j in r["jobs"]:
+        if j["conclusion"] == "failure":
+            print(r["run_number"], r["head_sha"][:9], r["conclusion"], j["name"], sep="\t")

Mechanism, read in the code: strace_files keeps the set of pids whose last exec was a Python interpreter and drops one only on a non-Python exec, never when the process exits (strace runs with -qq, so the trace carries no exit line), so once the pid space wraps, a recycled pid whose new owner never execs (a thread of a git or node child) has its opens counted as Python reads.      "Owner specification for the savings baseline (tvofi, 2026-10-24, binding acceptance criterion). Actual consumption is calculated from the heat pump's power sensor. The baseline must use power levels similar to the ones recorded, simulated as a plain thermostat over the exact same price profile, for both space heating and DHW. The DHW baseline assumes the DHW thermostat is always on: no DHW windows. Savings are the cost of that baseline minus the metered actual cost, priced over the same profile. Under one flat price, the volume difference may remain, but timing savings must be 0. The card's Savings tab equals ledger.savings_months cell for cell. Replace the modelled-thermostat volume (_thermostat_held_state, optimizer.py:358; baseline at 0.38x metered) with this definition.",
     "Correction to carry-d15-sav-volume-2 (D15 triage, 2026-10-24; derived ratios only). Withdrawn: \"an idle row writes no mode, so the DHW mode keeps the pump charging through plan-idle steps\". The owner's integration also owns the supply switch, and the ledger statistic it rested on, 7 of 8 idle steps after a DHW slot ran, is not evidence that the pump ran outside a planned slot. Three seams. (1) The ledger freezes `planned` at the step's first one-minute tick (`_observe`, custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py:1006-1010). That is the plan from before the mid-step re-solve, and the re-solve can move a DHW slot onto the current step. In the bundle, the 13:00 row reads planned dhw while the 13:13 solve's action for that same step is space 0.5 kW and dhw 0. `ran` is real metered pump draw of at least `on_threshold_kw` (0.25 kW) on any one-minute pass (pump_arbiter.py:1013-1015). `dhw` is the mode flag or a tank rise (pump_arbiter.py:1020-1026). (2) The arbiter never writes the switch (pump_arbiter.py:46). The switch is written once per coordinator cycle, from the new plan's step 0 (`_apply_action`, coordinator.py:7581-7595, after the solve at :5634). Cycles run every 15.39 min (median of 641) against 15-minute steps, at a phase spread uniformly through the step (quartiles 4.3, 8.2 and 11.4 min). So each switch-on lasts into the next step, and a slot written late in its own step starts the compressor in the following one: 3 of 4 planned DHW slots show no run in-slot. (3) Checked and refuted: the solve's switch schedule disagreeing with its ask. 0 of 672 published steps were switched on without an ask, or off with one. The bundle holds no switch-state history, so \"switch commanded off while draw continued\" can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Owed: score each ledger step against the plan in force when the step's actuation happened (re-freeze `planned` at each cycle's adoption), and actuate the switch at step boundaries, from the arbiter's one-minute tick, rather than at the cycle phase. Controls: a synthetic install with the cycle phase at 0 and at 14 min books identical duty verdicts; a step whose plan changed mid-step is scored against the plan that actuated it; one mutant per seam. +    "From 3358 (r10-combi-tank-pr), body item d678abfc: `tools/ci/codescan_wait.py` `settled()` fails closed on every partial re-run of a code run that owns codeql. Measured from an `origin/main` `2f6d699e5` checkout by importing the production module: three `CODEQL` jobs listed `completed`/`success` with no `steps` key give `settled()` False and `legs_uploaded()` `[]`. Control: the same three jobs with that step row give `settled()` True and all three legs. Live instance: run 42635950938 attempt 4, whose `codeql / Analyze (...)` jobs (129342605703, 129342605813, 129342606740) are listed with no steps while `pr-contract` (129342618295) is listed with them. So re-running a red `pr-contract` on its code run cannot turn it green; an edit run is needed, which takes the other-run path. On that path the same step-less listing gives `legs_uploaded()` `[]`, so no leg's alerts are read: the fail-open half that R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY's own-run carry names, now measured on the other-run path as well. Re-measure on that group's merge base with the same two listings. Carry: R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY (items d678abfc) [moved: R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE]"

    "brief": "Third instance of the class one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument, together with P7's record_row.py HTTP 500: an audit-class barrier. adopt as an audit-class barrier in new fly-in R10-FLY-GH-READ-RETRY (S, lane F, priority HIGH: it sits on the merge path), in two PRs ordered by file overlap. Do not fold into R10-FLOW-AUTOTRAIN, which is unregistered and a much larger mechanisation. (1) Third instance of the class \"one unretried GitHub read kills an instrument\", measured. Across every train log since 2026-10-20 there are 11 TRAIN STOPPED lines, and 2 are transient reads: train 8's `approve: ... could not read pull request #2547` (train2547/state8, 21:50:38Z, after waiting t+2667 s for CI, with 7 entries released) and `ci: the head commit at <sha> could not be read: Get \"https://api.github.com/...\": net/http...` in merge_train.py's own read. Add P7's record_row.py `HTTP Error 500` on main's push run, whose revisit trigger (\"a second 5xx instance\") is now met. The remaining 9 stops are content refusals (red CI 3, HOLDER worktree 4, stale carry 1, ledger merge 1), so 18% of train stops are pure transport. (2) The cause and the precedent. app_approve.sh l.104 `js=$(gh api \"repos/$1/pulls/$2\") || die` has three sibling reads (l.271 comments, l.406 CODEOWNERS, l.408 files), all single-shot, discarding stderr so the failure class is lost. app_push.sh already holds the house pattern (l.188-251: bounded RB_SLEEP*3^(n-1), 5/15/45 s, transport refusals distinguished from a genuine refusal, never retry-forever). Reuse that rule rather than inventing 10/30/60. (3) Classification, so it cannot mask a refusal. Retry only network/transport errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429 or a secondary-rate-limit 403 (honouring Retry-After). Anything else (401, 403-permission, 404, 422, or a body that parses but is wrong: head moved, no verdict, owned path) refuses at once, as today. After the budget it refuses with the last error text kept. Mutation-write calls (review POST, merge) are never retried by this rule; they keep their own guarded paths. (4) Ordering. PR 1, app_approve.sh's four reads plus self-test arms: no open PR or live handoff touches tools/pr/app_approve.sh, so dispatch now, ahead of R10-FLY-CARRY-DOC-CONTEXT (P17, same file), which gains an after-edge on it. PR 2, merge_train.py's GitHub reads and record_row.py's urlopen: after #2585 (CI-LAYOUT-P1: merge_train.py, record_row.py), #2584 (MAIN-GATE: merge_train.py) and #2524 (PUSHER-REAP: merge_train.py). Cost: ~25 lines in bash, ~20 in python, one shared rule stated once in INSTRUMENTS.md. Benefit: about 45 min of CI wait plus a relaunch for each transient stop (2 in about 30 h of trains), and one red main push run per 5xx. (5) Null control, in each self-test: a stub `gh` failing once with a transport error then answering passes, with exactly 2 calls logged. A stub answering 404, or a head mismatch, refuses after exactly 1 call (no retry masks a refusal). A stub failing 4 times refuses after the budget, naming the last error. A stub answering 500 to record_row twice then 200 records. Brief addition: \"bounded retry of GitHub READS only, app_push.sh's 5/15/45 s rule, retrying transport errors, 5xx, 429 and secondary-limit 403 and nothing else; fixtures: one transient then success (2 calls), 404 and a wrong head (1 call, immediate refuse), budget exhausted (refuse with the last error); PR 1 is app_approve.sh, PR 2 is merge_train.py and record_row.py after #2585, #2584 and #2524\".",

-    "Machinery freeze after v10.0.0 (tvofi 2026-11-01, production-share ruling). From the round-10 closeout stamp on, a change to the programme's machinery (tools/audit/**, tools/pr/**, tools/plan/**, tools/policy/**, .github/workflows/**, dev/governance/**, seat scripts) merges only if it (a) unblocks a named production pull request (one touching custom_components/) or (b) fixes a red on main or on such a PR. -    "Owner order (tvofi, 2026-11-01, verbatim: \"Make sure judging and folding every useful standing loop into the orchestrator machinery on main is planned in the roster, including describing the hooks and a script to set them up if they are not there\"). Widens STEP 1 and STEP 2 of this group's brief; the design (design/R10-FLY-STANDING-CONTRACTS) carries it.\n\n(1) JUDGE EVERY LOOP. The live-usage review gets one row per out-of-tree loop the round ran, with a verdict of fold (into a beat job in the job table, or into the tracked instrument it wraps), keep-as-is (already tracked; name the file), or drop (with the reason it bought nothing). Fold only what is useful, measured from its log: what it caught that nothing else caught. The loops the s9 orchestrator ran on 2026-11-01, by role (ask the orchestrator for their paths; cite none in tracked text):\n- the sweep runner (roster drain, pulse, cancel sweep, opener-log forward, disk floor, plan beat, owed_unactioned) \u2014 already STEP 2;\n- the roster drain \u2014 already STEP 2;\n- the opener driver, which acts on the tick's handoff-no-pr and handoff-update lines. Fold its 2026-11-01 retry semantics: mark a (topic, sha) done only on success; retry a failure after a backoff (30 min), at most three times; then print one STUCK line the digest carries. Before that change it marked a handoff done at start, and 7 handoffs stood stranded 1-16 h on 2026-11-01. It is the opener carry b94-P337 builds, plus these semantics;\n- the standing head watcher: one line per open-PR head move to the event digest (a reviewer or relay may be owed). A one-shot watcher's exit was lost across a compaction and a reviewer went unowed;\n- the orchestrator wake loop: exits, and so wakes the orchestrator, on a new sweep digest, a new event line or a new STUCK line. After a compaction nobody re-armed it, and owed lines stood unread for up to 15.8 h while every instrument had flagged them;\n- the triage seat's pass loop: releases held roster lines once the batch they wait on is on main, reads back landings, and exits on a new proposal or V-entry;\n- the merge seat's watch loop: polls main and the frozen hotfix heads, and touches the merge seat's alive file;\n- the dispatch head-await loop, now the standing head watcher above;\n- tick_loop.sh, cloud_relay.sh and state_docs.py beat \u2014 tracked already; verdict keep-as-is unless the review finds a gap.\nThe design names the digest and event files under $HPO_STATE_DIR that one wake reads, so no loop writes only to a private log (the 2026-11-01 class).\n\n(2) HOOKS, DESCRIBED AND INSTALLABLE. The live-usage review gets one row per out-of-tree loop the round ran, with a verdict of fold (into a beat job in the job table, or into the tracked instrument it wraps), keep-as-is (already tracked; name the file), or drop (with the reason it bought nothing). Before that change it marked a handoff done at start, and 7 handoffs stood stranded 1-16 h on 2026-11-01. It is the opener carry b94-P337 builds, plus these semantics;\n- the standing head watcher: one line per open-PR head move to the event digest (a reviewer or relay may be owed). A one-shot watcher's exit was lost across a compaction and a reviewer went unowed;\n- the orchestrator wake loop: exits, and so wakes the orchestrator, on a new sweep digest, a new event line or a new STUCK line. After a compaction nobody re-armed it, and owed lines stood unread for up to 15.8 h while every instrument had flagged them;\n- the triage seat's pass loop: releases held roster lines once the batch they wait on is on main, reads back landings, and exits on a new proposal or V-entry;\n- the merge seat's watch loop: polls main and the frozen hotfix heads, and touches the merge seat's alive file;\n- the dispatch head-await loop, now the standing head watcher above;\n- tick_loop.sh, cloud_relay.sh and state_docs.py beat \u2014 tracked already; verdict keep-as-is unless the review finds a gap.\nThe design names the digest and event files under $HPO_STATE_DIR that one wake reads, so no loop writes only to a private log (the 2026-11-01 class).\n\n(2) HOOKS, DESCRIBED AND INSTALLABLE. The orchestrator's sessions depend on user-level Claude Code hooks that are not in the tree:\n- a SessionStart and PostCompact liveness hook: it demands a fresh policy re-read from origin/main, prints a measured ALIVE/DEAD line for each standing loop, fresh/STALE for the alive files and the digest, and the digest itself, then instructs the orchestrator to restart anything dead, check the standing seats and re-arm the wake loop that turn (owner, 2026-11-01: in both hooks);\n- a PreToolUse Bash guard that keeps the main checkout clean;\n- a SessionStart seat-interpreter hook (the seat venvs; see seat_venv.sh);\n- a SessionStart git-identity hook.\nDeliver: (a) a tracked description of each hook (what it does, the event, why it exists), beside the instruments guide (e.g. an instruments/hooks.md indexed from INSTRUMENTS.md); (b) the hook scripts as tracked files, with machine paths taken from $HPO_STATE_DIR or arguments (tmp_paths.py and ref_privacy.py must pass); (c) one setup script under tools/audit/seat/ with --check (report which hooks are missing or differ from the tree, change nothing) and --install (idempotent: add a missing hook entry to the user's settings without touching unrelated entries, back the file up first, print what it changed), plus --self-test against a throwaway HOME (offline_spy.py) and wiring for selftest_wiring.py. The liveness hook's loop list is generated from the job table, so a new job is checked the day it lands. The tree already has project-level hooks (.claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/session-start.sh): the design decides, per hook, whether it belongs there (binds every session in this repository, no installer needed) or at user level (host-specific), and the installer covers only the latter. +    "Part 3: add a `loop-cwd` row to `beat_jobs.py` and `beatd.jobs.json`, every 900 s, for the long-lived loops outside the job table, named by a new overlay key of `pgrep -f` patterns (a lacking key prints `UNREADABLE`, as every row does). For each pid: read `lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd -Fin`, then `stat` the named path. An inode that differs, or a path that does not resolve, writes `DEAD <name> pid=<p> cwd gone` to the digest. An `lsof` that returns nothing writes `UNREADABLE`, never DEAD. Compare inodes, never only the path: `lsof` keeps printing the old path, and a recreated checkout resolves (four loops on 2026-11-04 at 18:37:06Z). A process absent from `pgrep` is not a line of this row. Fixture arms with a real child process: (a) directory removed writes DEAD; (b) directory recreated at the same path writes DEAD; (c) directory live writes nothing (the null control). Mutant: comparing only that the path exists fails (b). triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch119.md#P383 at 8439f738e [moved: R10-SEAT-IDENTITY-P5]",

-    "Body contract at the head (V115), built only with this group's dispatch and closed with it. `body_patch.sh`'s contract arm resolves a body's cited paths in the caller's checkout: `policy_lint.mjs`'s Forward-carry check calls `resolvePathToken`, which reads `brief_lint.mjs`'s `trackedFiles()`, a `git ls-files` at the lint's own ROOT. `pr-contract` resolves at the PR head. Measured: about 3 ms per call against about 26 ms for a python start. - Then it reads `tool_input.command` and refuses at command position (line start, or after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(`, a backtick, `sudo`, `xargs` or `env`) each of: - `pkill` with any arguments; - `killall`; - `kill` fed by `pgrep`. - Heredoc bodies are not read. - The refusal names the preamble rule and the alternative (`$!` or a pidfile). (2) Fix `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`'s hooks check (`cmdHooks`). Key the tool set on the hook script instead: `pre-edit.sh` keeps the edit tools, and the Bash hook is tested against `Bash`. Add the Bash hook to its `REQUIRED` list. (3) Self-test rows: - Refused: - `pkill -f \"\"`; - `pkill -f tests/entities.py`; - `pkill python3`; - `killall python3`; - `kill $(pgrep -f x)`; - `pgrep -f x | xargs kill`; - `cd /tmp && pkill -f x`; - `sudo pkill x`. - Allowed: - `kill 1234`; - `kill $!`; - `kill $(cat run.pid)`; - `grep -n pkill file`; - `git log --grep=killall`; - `echo \"never pkill\"`; - a heredoc whose body holds `pkill -f x`; - `git status`, which takes the prefilter path. (4) Mutants: - Drop the command-position anchor, and the `grep -n pkill` row fails. - Drop the `killall` arm, and its row fails. - Drop the pgrep-feed arm, and the `xargs kill` row fails. - Make `policy_lint`'s matcher test edit-only again, and it reports `MATCHER BLIND`. (5) Classify the new script for `tests/entities.py`. -    "Amends this group's 2026-10-25 trailing-comment carry (P300, queue 2026-10-30T09:41Z: 19 more lines refused or held in s7/s8). - `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py` `parse_line` (77-90) drops a comment that starts at an unquoted word beginning with `#`, and only that: shell semantics. Both cut a `#` in the middle of a word (`@/p/b#1.txt` -> `@/p/b`, measured). - Add `tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py` to this group's files. - Self-test rows: - `set-stage G done # #2955 merged aced2589` parses to `('set-stage', 'G', 'done', [])`. - Null: `append-carry G @/p/b#1.txt` keeps `@/p/b#1.txt`. - Null: `drop-carry G --match s6-batch8.md#P70`, unquoted, keeps `s6-batch8.md#P70`. - A quoted `'a # b'` stays one argument. - One mutant: restore the plain `shlex.split(ln)`, and the comment row fails. triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch68.md#P300",
-    "`tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py run` gains `--mark` (P300). - After each op's report line, the queue line it applied is rewritten in place as `#done <line>` when pushed (and the read-back did not print FAILED), else as `#refused <line>`. - The rewrite re-reads the queue file at write time and matches the exact line text, first unmarked occurrence. It writes through a temp file in the same directory and `os.replace`, so a line another writer appended after the run's first read is kept. - `run` with `--mark` also accepts `all` for FIRST..LAST, meaning every unmarked op line, so a seat needs no cursor. - Lines already starting with `#` (`#done`, `#refused`, `#held`, `#note`) are never applied, which is today's skip, now documented. - Basis: the s7 and s8 roster seats each wrapped the runner in an untracked loop (`roster-loop.sh` 90 lines, `roster-s8-loop.py` 111 lines) for this marking alone. The s8 `mark()` rewrites with `open(Q, 'w')` and no guard. - Self-test rows: - A pushed op marks `#done`; a refused op marks `#refused`. - A line appended to the queue between the run's first read and the mark survives. - Null: without `--mark` the queue file is byte-identical after the run. - One mutant: write the run-start snapshot instead of re-reading, and the appended-line row fails. triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch68.md#P300",
-    "From the s9 bulk roster apply (2026-11-01, roster 1d7ef52f..27e882736, 282 lines). Four defects found in the roster queue path, each measured:\n(1) tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py line 7: the docstring gives the usage as `append-group <json-file>`, but argparse needs `append-group <GROUP> <json>`. 36 queue lines followed the docstring and were refused rc=2, along with every carry routed into those groups.\n(2) roster_drain.py: its 3600 s timeout raises before any mark is written. A pass that runs over the timeout, as today's 62-push volume at 1-3 min each would have, loses every mark, and the next pass re-runs those lines.\n(3) The drain skips any line containing ` #`, which strands valid ops whose quoted argument holds `#`, such as `#2257`. Four lines were stranded today.\n(4) Throughput: one op, one lint and one push per line takes 1-3 min. The bulk path took 0.36 s per line: it called roster_edit main() for each line in a single worktree, with local commits, then ran lint_gate once and pushed once. The scripts are in the s9 scratchpad as bulk.py and readback_mark.py.\nFix: correct the docstring, with a self-test arm that runs the documented usage. Write marks incrementally, per line, as each op pushes. Parse the trailing-comment filter, don't substring-match it. Land a batched mode in roster_queue.py (`run --batch`) that reuses roster_edit's checks with one lint and one push, so instrument code doesn't live in /tmp. Failing test first: an arm for each of (1)-(3) that is red at main. Null control: a batch of one line gives a roster byte-identical to the single-op path's.",
-    "From the s9 script census: the roster seat's queue watcher is s7/roster-loop.sh (90 lines; the s8 copy is roster-s8-loop.py, 118 lines), and the triage seat's pass is s9/seat-triage/pass.sh; tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py (`run FIRST LAST`, `readback`) covers one pass but not what the loops carry. Four behaviours exist only in the shell loops: (1) marking: a landed queue line becomes `#done <line>`, a refused one `#refused <line>` (a refused op used to be consumed and never retried; a false refusal from an empty marker caused re-issues of landed ops); (2) flag parsing: --at-sha, --field, --match, --value, --over-cap are passed as flags and not folded into the positional value (set-stage X done --at-sha SHA once wrote stage=\"done --at-sha SHA\", measured 2026-10-27 on R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE, and the plan held R10-ARCH-DOCS two days behind it); (3) the lint clone self-heals when its directory is missing; (4) `#held append-carry` lines are released when the batch file named in the carry exists on origin/main (pass.sh), with a LANDED/not-landed readback by the carry's first 60 characters against the roster JSON, and an `unwired open issue/PR` sweep escalates open numbers no live group owns. Fold into tools/audit/seat/roster_queue.py: a `loop [--every 300]` subcommand using the existing runner, with the marking, the flag grammar (one shared parser for both the loop and `run`, so the asymmetry in queue line 24 cannot recur), the self-heal, `release-held` and the unwired sweep as separate subcommands. Planted control: a queue with one landing and one refused op ends with `#done` on the first and `#refused` on the second and the refused one is not retried; `set-stage G done --at-sha S` reaches roster_edit with stage `done` and the flag intact; a held line whose batch file is absent stays held. Mutation: fold the flag into the value and the second case must fail. Carry: R10-ORCH-ROSTER-SCHEMA",

-    "roster_edit.py has no way to mark a folded group: set-stage takes no `absorbed_into`, so ten groups folded into another (R10-FLY-CARRY-DISPOSITION, R10-FLY-RELAY-TOOLS-LEVEL, R10-FLY-CAP-LINE, R10-NIGHTLY-HB-RESPAWN, R10-FLOW-WIP, R10-FLOW-POSTMERGE, R10-FLY-PRUNE-REFS, R10-FLY-WORKTREE-GC, R10-ROUTING-INVARIANTS; and R10-HOTFIX-PREHEAT-LABEL into R10-ARCH-SHAPES-CLASSIFIER) read `done`, and `carry_audit.py roster` cannot name where their carries went (carry-strand audit, orchestrator s9, 2026-10-31, ~/hpo-orch/r10s6/s9/carry-strand-audit.md \"Folded groups marked done\"). Four lines were stranded today.\n(4) Throughput: one op, one lint and one push per line takes 1-3 min. The bulk path took 0.36 s per line: it called roster_edit main() for each line in a single worktree, with local commits, then ran lint_gate once and pushed once. The update arm of that driver got 22 of its 45 runs through at the same handoff sha after the relay had refused it. In `handoff_arm`, with the reason of carry 9 kept: a refusal whose step is `unpinned sites`, `carry` or another body-content step stays recorded until the body ref moves (the key of carry 9). This narrows the sentence of carry 9 \"Only content refusals (prepr REFUSE) stay recorded failed\" by splitting body-content refusals from retryable steps; it adds no second rule. Any other refusal, such as `ancestry reds` or `ci predict`, reruns on a backoff of at least 30 min, at most three tries, then stays as the OWED of today, `handoff-update` line with its reason. Fixture arms: (a) `ancestry reds`, then clean, updates on the retry; (b) `unpinned sites` with the same body does not rerun and with a new body does; (c) three refusals of a retryable class stop and print the OWED line. -    "Part 1, front of queue (owner directive 2026-11-04): the prepr of a fixer is not repeated at open or update. Part 1 is this carry with carries 3 and 4, and no other; the rest is part 2. The carry 3 \"PRE-PR rc=0 line\" is built here, and carry 9 is answered by the merge of PR 3089. (1) Receipt: on rc=0, `prepr.sh` run with a body writes `<HEAD sha> <tree sha>` to a file in the git dir. `body_push.sh` reads it and, when its sha is the code head of the handoff, adds a `Prepr: <sha> <tree>` trailer to the `handoff-body/<topic>` commit. `--body-check` writes none, and a run with a skip flag other than `PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES` writes none. (2) Verdict: `app_push.sh --reuse`, beside `recarry_verdict` and `row_only_verdict`, failing closed, is taken only when the trailer of the body ref names the code sha C, the tree of C is the one in the trailer, and HEAD differs from a clean automatic merge of C with the live head and origin/main only by the row of the PR itself: no resolution, no other commit. Anything else runs the full prepr. One `app_push: REUSE:` line names the path and why. `update_pr.sh` and `open_pr.sh` p1 ask for it, and a head the verdict refuses runs the full prepr as today. (3) What it still runs, with no heavy slot: `row_only_checks`, and the steps keyed to main, the body or the merge (`no version`, `claim files`, `claims hygiene`, `ci predict`, `unpinned sites`, `layout guard`, `ref privacy`, `temp paths`, `preflight`, `figures`, `ancestry reds`), plus `tests/structure.py` on the merged tree, the `merge-tree` result where the head did not merge main. Check the input of each step before dropping it, and report the wall time of the kept steps at the merge base of the group. Do not key the skip to main not moving under a closure: that key fired on 0 of 4 code opens (`s6-batch95.md#P346`). Fixture arms: (a) an update to a receipted sha with a clean merge takes no heavy slot; (b) a sha with no receipt, or with a trailer naming another sha, runs the full prepr (the null control); (c) a conflict resolved in the merge runs the full prepr; (d) a clean merge whose `tests/structure.py` fails is refused; (e) a `ci predict` red on the merged main is refused (the PR 3195 and the 2026-10-31 18:34Z class); (f) a tree differing from the one in the trailer runs the full prepr. Mutants: dropping the tree comparison fails (f), and dropping `tests/structure.py` fails (d). triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch121.md#P386 at 8439f738e",

Owner of tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py with R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE; it already hosts the folded post-merge and classify readers.\n\nOriginal text, verbatim:\nThe train undrafts a head it has already proved mergeable, instead of stopping on it (P218/V138, owner-directed V131; from #2854 sitting green on every check but `BLOCKED`/`REVIEW_REQUIRED` only because `isDraft` was true, hours as the v7.0.5 critical path, and #2878 admitted as a draft and undrafted 23 s later). In `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py`'s merge step, where a refusal would stop, run `gh pr ready <n>` -- but only on a head the train has already admitted to that step, meaning ALL of: a posted `merge` verdict naming the current head or one `app_approve.sh --carry` says carries to it; a clean merge tree against main; a delivery row at the head; no failing or pending required context; and the approval the step posts. Undrafting writes no commit and moves no head, so the verdict still names the tree being merged. Log one `UNDRAFT #<pr> <head>` line; re-read `isDraft` after the call and continue to the merge only if it is false (a re-draft between call and merge stops the run); a failed `gh pr ready` is a `Stop` with its own phase, never a silent continue. Null controls: a non-draft head at the same step behaves identically with no `UNDRAFT` line; a draft whose verdict names an older head is not undrafted; a draft with a pending required context is not undrafted; a head drafted after admission is not undrafted. Fixer's change under the fix protocol: failing test on a draft head first, then review. +   "brief": "Owner-approved CI-throughput lever 3 (tvofi, 2026-11-07, #201 comment 6707834331), and the owner approved the policy widening in the same comment. On a pull request, each governance / instrument-self-tests step runs only when the diff reaches that step's MEASURED closure, the way rule 1 of CLAUDE.md selects test scripts from tests/closures.json; every push to main stays FULL (a wrong closure turns main red within one merge, which rule 1 already accepts). This answers U4, which the design note at design/R10-GENERIC-HEAT-CURVE-PERSISTENT a64af2b343 (2026-11-09 11:30Z) still lists as open in its fixer note ghcp-04, and it falsifies that note's foot-point hypothesis.\nFacts, from a static analysis of the heating-curve function in controller firmware V3.92.3 (interoperability only, function at 0x0020752c):\n- The two curve parameters are the end point E and the \"Parallelverschiebung\" F. F is clamped to 5-35 \u00b0C.\n- target = F + (E - 20) * (F - T_out) / (20 - (T_out - F) / 2). The circuit's min/max then clamps it: the return target for the heating circuit, the flow target for a mixing circuit.\n- With E = 20 the target is the constant F. E is the target at -20 \u00b0C only when F = 20. In general the -20 \u00b0C point is F + 2(E - 20)(F + 20)/(F + 60).\n- Checked on the contributor's install against the controller's reported targets. Heating, E/F 30/22, T_out about 6 \u00b0C: formula and controller both 27.7 \u00b0C. Mixing circuit 1, 45/30, T_out 6.1 \u00b0C: formula 48.8, clamped to the circuit maximum, 45.0. Mixing circuit 1, 45/20, T_out 5.8 \u00b0C: formula 33.1, controller 33.0.\n- Triage re-computed the formula's arithmetic: 27.7 at 30/22/6, and +1.26 K for F 22 -> 23 at 6 \u00b0C.\nConsequences for kind `persistent`:\n- F is not a parallel shift, and it is not a foot point that the curve rotates about the end point. It is the point where outdoor and target temperature are equal, and moving it also changes the slope. With E = 30, F 22 -> 23 moves the target by about +1.15 K at -10 \u00b0C, +1.26 K at 6 \u00b0C and +1.35 K at 15 \u00b0C.\n- So a persistent write of F + d displaces the target by neither d nor a constant, and the step per kelvin depends on the outdoor temperature. The curve is hyperbolic, not linear, in T_out.\n- The real parallel shift on this controller is the SHI heating offset (holding register 10002), which adds exactly its value: +2 K took 27.7 to 29.7 \u00b0C, and +1 K gave exactly +1 K at another outdoor temperature. This also extends #3299's U1 evidence to a second outdoor temperature. #3299's user docs name a Luxtronik SHI heating offset as a volatile whole-curve offset, which this supports; nothing is owed there.\nWhat this group does with it: ghcp-04's docs wording is replaced. The user docs say that on a Luxtronik the persistent parameter F is not a parallel shift, that a displacement d written to it moves the return target by more than d by an amount that varies with outdoor temperature, and that kind `offset` on the SHI heating offset is the parallel shift (already the note's preference at its line 177). Making `persistent` invert this formula is a controller-specific design change. If the fixer finds the generic `b + delta(d)` contract (P2) unsound beyond a docs statement, it goes back to the designer and orchestrator; it is not widened in the fix.
