+## P646: `train.sh add` with no live train batches every ready pull request
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2: correct train.sh's add text. REJECT the `--only` flag and the pre-start print.
+
+Source: triage queue line 324. When no train is live, `add` starts one through
+merge_train.py ready_batch (:3058-3068). That is carry 14 (tvofi 2026-11-01: batch by default),
+pinned by the self-test at :5942: every ready verdicted pull request from build_queue joins the
+first batch. The behaviour is the owner's ruling. What is false is train.sh's own text:
+- the header (:12-14) says `add` "with no train live, starts one over it";
+- the --queue refusal (:75) says "the started train's queue is the added entry".
+
+The instrument guide train.sh.md (:28) states it correctly ("over every ready").
+
+Instances ($HOME/.local/state/hpo/merge_train/train.log):
+- `grep -oE 'STARTED train.sh pid [0-9]+ over [^;]+; queue add-queue-202611(0[89]|1[01])' | wc -l`
+  gives 16 add-started trains from 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-11.
+- A 17th, the orchestrator's instance, has no STARTED line. That add's build_queue logged `QUEUE
+  #3355` (line 20642), `QUEUE #3431` (20655) and `QUEUE #3442` (20662), and the merge seat TERMed
+  it.
+- The seat relaunched at 18:36:24Z with the explicit queue (`train.sh: queue=.../Q.json`, then
+  `BATCH 20261111-183624 ... queue=7`), so no excluded pull request merged. The delay was about
+  4 min.
+
+The rule, run per part:
+- Measure: add-started trains that took in a pull request the orchestrator had excluded. That is
+  1 of 17 (6%) over 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-11, under 20%. (Today alone it is 1 of 3, too few to
+  bear a percentage.)
+- Severity: medium, R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2's roster severity (in progress). That group's carries
+  already route merge_train.py and train.sh work. A false statement of what a merge command will
+  merge, in the file a seat reads before running it, is a defect repair.
+- `--only` duplicates `train.sh --queue Q.json` (header :4), the documented exact-queue start
+  the seat used at 18:36. A second spelling of the same start is rejected.
+- A print of the batch before it starts gives an unattended seat nothing to act on between the
+  print and the start. The STARTED line already names the set (`over #...`), and `merge_train.py
+  queue` prints the QUEUE/LEFT lines without starting anything. Rejected.
+
+Cost: train.sh header (:12-14) and one die string (:75), about 4 lines. There is no new flag,
+file or check, and train.sh has no structure_budgets.json row.
+
+Binding: a 4-line correction of false text in a merge command's header, against a new flag that
+duplicates `--queue`.
+
+Bar: severity medium (R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2). Figure: 1 of 17 add-started trains (6%), under 20%.
+Basis: severity-exempt defect repair (medium) only. On the 20% bar alone it would be REJECTed. It
+is a carry on a group already in progress, so no new group starts.
+
+Destination: append-carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2, with this text:
+
+> TRAIN-ADD-START-TEXT (triage P646). tools/audit/seat/train.sh says `add` with no train live
+> "starts one over it" (header :12-14) and that "the started train's queue is the added entry"
+> (the --queue refusal, :75). Since carry 14 (tvofi 2026-11-01, merge_train.py ready_batch
+> :3058-3068), the started train's first batch is every ready verdicted pull request from

+- OPENER-LIVE-TIP, s6-batch183.md#P603, carries 6 and 7.

+- P581 measured STALE CHECKOUT on 8 of 25 opener attempts (32%) from 2026-11-10T09:50Z to

+should be built in, no critical path, outside or hotfix PR should wait in CI queue." A local version

+Instances:
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/sweep.md:611 (2026-11-11T20:12:02Z): 77 runs queued and 9 running, and

+- R10-FLY-CANCEL-SWEEP owns tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py. It is done (#3004), so it cannot
+  receive the carry.
+- R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE is this exact seam, from the owner's directive of 2026-10-28: pause the
+  lowest-priority PR's CI when the account's job limit binds. #3004 left it as its part 2, and it
+  already holds the tier carries (P267/P268).
+  - Its stage is `refused` by the keep test (2.7% of main CI wall, s6-batch136.md#P428). The
+    owner's ruling now overrides that keep test, so the group reopens to not-started.

+  - Its files gain tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py, and tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py, which holds
+    the beat's cancel-sweep row (:83, :522).
+- No new group is needed. The owner directs that the build starts and that priority PRs never
+  wait, so the open-PR cap does not hold it; the orchestrator dispatches it as a priority group.

+The measure the PR must report: the minutes a priority PR's first job waits in the queue, before
+and after. Before is 31 min (#3455's review run, 20:11Z, 77 queued and 9 running).
+
+Cost: one M instrument group, already sized on the roster, plus one carry.
+
+Binding: owner ruling.
+
+The carry, as queued:
+
+> CI-QUEUE-PRIORITY-BUILT-IN, owner ruling (tvofi 2026-11-11T20:13Z, verbatim: "6. Do it, it is already decided and should be built in, no critical path, outside or hotfix PR should wait in CI queue."), reopening this group from its 2026-11-08 keep-test refusal (triage P652). Build into the beat's cancel-sweep row (tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py cancel-sweep, :83 and :522) and tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py the rule the session's local seat has run since 2026-11-11T20:20Z: while any critical-path, hotfix or outside pull request (classes read from the roster through roster_lib, this group's tier mapping) has a workflow run queued, cancel the queued runs of non-priority pull requests and re-run them once no priority run is queued; never cancel a run of the pull request the merge train is waiting on, nor a run already in progress, nor a main-branch run. Print one line per cancel and per re-run naming the PR, the run and the priority PR that caused it. Self-test: a queued priority run plus a queued non-priority run cancels the non-priority one and re-runs it after; the train's PR is never cancelled; null control: no priority run queued cancels nothing; mutation proof: dropping the priority check makes the null control cancel. Measure in the body: minutes a priority PR's first job waits queued, before and after, with the before figure re-measured at the merge base (31 min was measured for #3455's review run at 2026-11-11T20:11Z, 77 queued and 9 running); carry no count.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 215
+
+Sources: triage queue lines 331 to 333, three PROPOSAL lines (orchestrator s14,
+2026-11-11T20:48:09Z), ruled as P653 to P655. Line numbers are at origin/main 61afd4f2db.
+Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster 5700990bac. All three accepted parts are carries on
+existing groups, so the open-PR cap does not bear on them.

+## P653: merge_pr.sh re-posts a verdict the bus already posted
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT part (b) as a carry on R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER; REJECT part (a), the host-path claim (refuted: the Evidence line is the sanctioned home-relative form).
+
+Source: triage queue line 331.
+
+Instances:
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/sweep.md:629, `WORKAROUND 20:40Z merge s14-7: #3355 stray verdict comment
+  6805392170 (posted by my merge_pr.sh try ...) patched via gh_comment.py patch to the body of
+  verdict comment 6783731829 ... so newest verdict matches tip aad4f556`.
+- tools/audit/seat/merge_pr.sh:272-273 copies the evidence directory's VERDICT.md, appends
+  `Evidence: <path>/` when the text does not name the directory, and posts it through
+  app_comment.sh. It runs before the merge, and nothing first reads whether the bus already
+  posted a verdict for this head. A try that then fails leaves a newer verdict comment whose text
+  differs from verdict/<pr>'s tip, which merge_train.py:3190 refuses ("the newest posted
+  verdict (comment N) is not verdict/<pr>'s tip").
+- Part (a) is refuted. The path is written by `ref_privacy.py path`, which makes it
+  `~/<rest>`, the form the tool documents for posted text (ref_privacy.py:5). body_refusal
+  passes it, and its self-test at ref_privacy.py:837 pins exactly that
+  (`evidence: ~/.zcode/bus/...`). Publishing `~/...` paths is today's policy, not a leak.
+  Changing that would be a ref_privacy policy proposal of its own.
+
+Measure: $HPO_STATE_DIR/merge_pr/v holds 8 verdict files, which is every merge_pr.sh post under
+this state dir, and one of them did harm. The owner restricted merge_pr.sh to deadlocks and the
+critical path (sweep.md:613, ruling 5), so the harm falls on the pull requests where a stall
+costs most.
+
+Basis: severity-exempt defect repair (medium) only. On the 20% bar alone it would be REJECTed:
+it is one instance in 8 uses, with a one-call workaround.
+
+Destination: append-carry on R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER (medium, not started). It is the open group
+that lists tools/audit/seat/merge_pr.sh. The seat is the verdict post, beside that group's
+gate-reader arm. Text:
+
+> MERGE-PR-NO-REPOST (triage P653). tools/audit/seat/merge_pr.sh:272-273 always posts the
+> evidence VERDICT.md (plus an `Evidence:` line) through app_comment.sh before it merges, even
+> when the bus has already posted that verdict for the head. A try that then fails leaves a newer
+> verdict comment that is not verdict/<pr>'s tip text, and `merge_train.py add` refuses the PR
+> (merge_train.py:3190). Instance: #3355, comment 6805392170, 2026-11-11T19:33Z, cured by hand
+> with a gh_comment.py patch.
+> Repair: before posting, read the PR's newest posted merge verdict with the same reading the
+> train's add check uses. When that verdict is for this head, post nothing and print
+> `ALREADY POSTED: comment <id>`. Post only when no verdict for the head is posted. Keep the
+> Evidence line's `ref_privacy.py path` form unchanged.
+> Self-test (merge_pr.sh's offline flow): with a posted verdict for the head, there is no
+> app_comment.sh call and the merge proceeds. Null control: with no posted verdict, it posts as
+> today. Mutation proof: dropping the read makes the first arm post.
+
+## P654: zombie workflow runs that refuse cancel
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT parts (1) and (3) as two carries on R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE; DEFER part (2) (the fresh-run step) until a zombie at a live PR head is shown permanent.
+
+Source: triage queue line 332.
+
+Instances:
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/digest/jobs/cancel-sweep (written 21:46Z) has 12 lines. These are six pairs of
+  `gh api .../runs/<id>/cancel rc=1: ... not in progress. (HTTP 409)` and `could not cancel
+  <id>`, for 42810088662, 42810088912, 42817922694, 42818706376, 42955031956 and 42961218591.
+  The ids match the proposal's.
+- tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py:222-228 POSTs a cancel for every planned id on every pass and
+  keeps no memory of a 409. beat_jobs.py:83 runs it every 600 s, and beat_jobs.py:518-527
+  reports each `could not cancel` line as a job failure.
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/seat/ci-priority/FINDINGS.md:3-5: the local shim ran 20:15Z to 20:42Z,
+  cancelled 21 queued non-priority runs, and `priority_queued stayed 19 to 20`. GitHub completed
+  about 2 runs per hour, so the cancels freed no runner. sweep.md:619 (20:22Z) shows 37 of the
+  queued runs were main `Gate sweep` runs, which the shim's rule never touches.
+- Part (2) is not established. FINDINGS.md:5-6 list the #3441, #3458, #3451, #3469, #3442 and
+  #3428 runs as not completed about 30 minutes after a cancel on a saturated account. It also says
+  "queued cancels did not take effect on a saturated account" and (:8) "rerun refused 'already
+  running' ... their status turned queued again, so a run existed". A cancel still pending on a
+  saturated queue is not shown to be a permanent zombie. Only the ten-day Hassfest run and the
+  six sweep ids are long-lived, and the proposal does not show those at a live PR head.
+
+Measure, part (1): one sweep pass costs 1 PR listing, 5 run listings, one commit read per PR
+with something to cancel, and one POST per cancel (cancel_superseded.py:39-42). The six refused
+POSTs, and their commit reads, are at least 6 of at most 18 calls, about 33% or more of the
+pass's REST calls. That is 864 refused POSTs a day at the 600-s cadence. It is over 20% on REST
+calls per pass, and it is a medium-plus defect repair as well.
+
+Measure, part (3): 21 cancels drained no priority run (0%), and the reruns turned 10 spooled
+verdicted pull requests red (proposal; FINDINGS.md:3 lists the cancelled PRs). Carry 4 of
+R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE specifies that cancel rule. A measured defect in an accepted carry's design,
+on a high, owner-directed group, is severity-exempt, and the measured result is the reason.
+
+Destination: two append-carries on R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE (high, not started), which lists
+tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py and tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py. Texts:
+
+> CANCEL-SWEEP-ZOMBIE-MEMORY (triage P654 (1)). tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py:222-228 POSTs a
+> cancel for every planned run on every pass. Six runs (42810088662 42810088912 42817922694
+> 42818706376 42955031956 42961218591) answer HTTP 409 "Cannot cancel a workflow run that is not
+> in progress" on every 600-s beat pass (beat_jobs.py:83). That is 12 failure lines in
+> digest/jobs/cancel-sweep and at least a third of the pass's REST calls.
+> Repair: record a run that answers 409 while it is listed active in a state file under
+> $HPO_STATE_DIR (id, first-seen time). Skip it on later passes without a POST or a commit read.
+> Print it once as `cancel_superseded: zombie <id> (409, not retried)`, and count zombies in the
+> CANCEL-SWEEP summary line. Do not count a known zombie as a failure in beat_jobs.py's
+> cancel_sweep filter (:523-524). A run that is gone from the active listings drops out of the
+> file.
+> Self-test: a 409 answer is recorded and the next pass makes no POST for it. Null control: a
+> non-409 failure (rc 1, HTTP 500) is retried on the next pass. Mutation proof: dropping the
+> record makes the second pass POST again.
+
+> CI-PRIORITY-NO-VERDICT-CANCEL (triage P654 (3)), amending carry 4 (CI-QUEUE-PRIORITY-BUILT-IN)
+> with the local shim's measured result (s14 ci-priority FINDINGS, 2026-11-11 20:15-20:42Z). 21
+> cancels of queued non-priority runs drained no priority run: priority_queued held at 19-20, and
+> GitHub completed about 2 runs per hour. The cancels and reruns also turned 10 spooled verdicted
+> pull requests red. 37 of the queued runs were main `Gate sweep` runs, which carry 4's rule
+> exempts.
+> The build must: (i) never cancel a run of a pull request that holds a posted merge verdict at
+> its head, or that is in the merge train's queue or spool, as well as the train's current PR;
+> (ii) prefer holding to cancelling, which means starting no rerun or dispatch of a non-priority
+> PR's CI (the train and merge_pr unstale reruns, rerun helpers) while a priority run is queued,
+> and cancelling a queued run only where the body's before/after measure (carry 4) shows that
+> cancelling shortens a priority PR's queued wait; (iii) report in the body which share of the
+> queue is main-branch runs, because they decided the shim's zero.
+> Self-test: a queued run of a verdicted spooled PR is never cancelled while a priority run is
+> queued. Null control: a non-verdicted, non-spooled queued run is handled as carry 4 says.
+> Mutation proof: dropping the verdict check cancels the verdicted run.
+
+Re-raise trigger for part (2): a run at a PR's live head still not completed 2 hours after its
+cancel, while the account has queued runs below its job cap, with rerun refused. Then the
+fresh-run step (workflow_dispatch of ci.yml with pr and base, as the autofix jobs do) is
+ACCEPTable as a carry on R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE. Until then, moving the head is the workaround.
+
+## P655: the merge train keeps a skipped entry's worktree on its branch
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT form (a) as a carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 (the train releases a skipped entry's recarry worktree at the skip); REJECT form (b) (update_pr.sh detaching the train's worktree).
+
+Source: triage queue line 333.
+
+Instances:
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/sweep.md:625, `#3464 handoff d9ab65e9 NOT applied: update_pr BUSY (exit 75
+  twice; branch checked out in merge_train/wt/3464)`. :628, `WORKAROUND 20:39:18Z detached the
+  train's clean worktree wt/3464 ... (train skipped #3464 on conflict)`. :632, applied at
+  20:44:25Z.
+- $HPO_STATE_DIR/train/current.log: `SKIP #3464 recarry: main does not merge without a
+  resolution`. That log has 55 `recarry:` skips in total.
+- merge_train.py:2512-2525 adds the recarry worktree on the branch (`worktree add -B`) and
+  appends it to made_wts. release_worktrees (:2895-2906) removes made_wts only before the run's
+  closing line. skip (:3681) does not touch the worktree, so a skipped entry's branch stays
+  checked out until the train ends.
+- update_pr.sh:64-67 detaches another instrument's clean worktree only under its own state
+  prefix `$P/` (:44, `$HPO_STATE_DIR/pr`). A train worktree is outside it, so :69 exits 75 BUSY.
+- Not a duplicate. --free-holders (merge_train.py:1705) frees OTHER holders for the train's own
+  recarry, the opposite direction. R10-FLOW-BODY-PATCH carry 0 and the exit-75 carry (P2/P22)
+  made the train's hold a retryable BUSY. Neither releases it at a skip.
+
+Measure: one instance, a critical-path repair blocked about 25 minutes (20:15-20:39Z), with two
+one-shot seats spent. A worktree is held after every recarry skip (55 in the log), but a block
+needs an update to arrive while the train is still running.
+
+Basis: severity-exempt defect repair (medium) only. On the 20% bar alone it would be REJECTed.
+It is one measured instance.
+
+Why (a) and not (b): the instrument that made the worktree owns its release (release_worktrees'
+own rule). If update_pr.sh detached a worktree a live train may still be using, it would act on
+another instrument's working state while that instrument is running. A skip ends the train's use
+of that entry, so releasing at the skip is sound and needs no cross-instrument rule.
+
+Destination: append-carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 (medium, in progress, files merge_train.py).
+Text:
+
+> TRAIN-SKIP-RELEASES-WORKTREE (triage P655). merge_train.py's recarry adds a worktree on the
+> entry's branch (:2512-2525, made_wts). release_worktrees (:2895) removes it only before the
+> run's closing line. So after `SKIP #N recarry` (skip, :3681) the branch stays checked out until
+> the train ends, and update_pr.sh for that PR exits 75 BUSY (update_pr.sh:69; its detach rule
+> :64-67 covers only $HPO_STATE_DIR/pr). Instance: #3464 (critical path), 2026-11-11 20:15-20:39Z,
+> two BUSY exits, cured by a hand detach.
+> Repair: when an entry is skipped, release that entry's worktree if this run made it (it is in
+> made_wts), with release_worktrees' rule: `git worktree remove`, never forced. Log
+> `released <wt>` or `NOT released <wt> (...)`, and drop it from made_wts. A queue entry's own
+> `worktree` is never touched.
+> Self-test: a recarry skip with a clean made worktree removes it and logs `released`. Null
+> control: a skip of an entry whose worktree came from the queue entry leaves it. Mutation proof:
+> dropping the release leaves the branch checked out after the skip.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 216
+
+Sources: the orchestrator's message to the triage seat (s14, 2026-11-11, after the #3481 CARRY-MISSING
+roster ops), ruled as P656. Line numbers are at origin/main 61afd4f2db. Roster read at
+handoff/audit-r10-roster 028ebe9c5d.

+## P656: an item id must survive its own landed annotation
+
+Verdict: REJECT as duplicate of s6-batch183.md#P605 (CARRY-LANDED-OWN-TOPIC, R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5 carry 4, accepted, not built); both proposed fixes REJECTed in favour of it.
+
+Source: orchestrator message, 2026-11-11, instance #3481.
+
+The proposal's cause is half right. The three body items of #3481 did get new ids (c7424eb8,
+ccc86b13 and 70e463f9 became b4048305, 128b800e and c33b6f10) once each item gained a
+`Carry N: landed at f4c4044aaa ... (items <id>)` suffix. carry_audit.py:290 hashes the whole item
+text. But a changed id is already provided for. landed() (carry_audit.py:620-660) also counts an
+item as landed when its group's carries hold the SOURCE, `#<pr>` or the handoff topic (P310: "an
+id re-minted by a reword still lands by its source"). The relay's carry-fold arm landed carries 2,
+3 and 4 as `From r10-advisor-steady-start, body item ...`, which is the topic.
+
+The refusal comes from the caller. tools/audit/seat/bus.sh:236-237 runs `carry_audit.py landed
+--body ... --pr "#$1"` with no `--topic`, so the topic-sourced carries never match.
+
+Measured on #3481's live body (head branch fix/r10-advisor-steady-start), roster at origin/main:
+- `landed --pr '#3481'`: `CARRY-LANDED: 3 missing` (the bus's refusal).
+- `landed --pr '#3481' --topic r10-advisor-steady-start`: `CARRY-LANDED: 0 missing`.
+
+This also answers the open s14-26 question of why `carry_audit landed` printed "0 missing". That
+run passed `--topic`; the bus does not.
+
+Prior instances: 66 distinct CARRY-MISSING lines across 19 refused dispatches in tick-loop.log,
+cloud-relay.daemon.log, s13/dispatch-seat/mint3299.out and the s14 dispatch seat files. For each
+item, the group's current carries show how it was later satisfied:
+- 11 items (3 PRs) were already held by a topic-sourced carry before the refusal: #3481 (3 items),
+  #3227 (5, R10-BODY-CONTRACT) and #3220 (3, R10-SAV-COMFORT). Each refusal was false, and the
+  hand-landed `From #N` / `From PR N` copy duplicated a carry. That is 11 duplicate carries;
+  R10-BODY-CONTRACT carries 10, 16 and 26 are one example.
+- 15 items were landed afterwards from `#N`. Those refusals were true.
+- 26 were never landed by text (R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE 22 and others, re-routed or
+  dismissed).
+- #3448 (P605's own instance: 23 own-group lines) is the same missing `--topic`.
+So 4 of 19 refused dispatches (21%) were false refusals from the missing `--topic`. That is over
+20% on dispatch right-first-time.
+
+Why the proposed fixes are not taken:
+- (i) Hashing the text before the landed suffix covers only this one annotation shape. A reword
+  still re-mints the id, which is the case P310's source rule was built for.
+- (ii) Moving the landed note out of the item changes the body template (policy-adjacent), and it
+  too leaves the reword case open.
+Passing the topic is the one change that makes the existing source rule work for both.
+
+Binding: duplicate. P605's carry (R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5 idx 4) is the fix, exactly as written: read
+.head.ref, map it with topic_grammar.py pr-topic, and pass --topic. To the orchestrator: the
+measure above (4 of 19 refused dispatches, 11 duplicate carries, one L-group first review held
+tonight) supports dispatching R10-CARRY-AUDIT-P5 (medium, not started) ahead of other medium
+instrument groups. Until it is built, a CARRY-MISSING refusal should first be re-run with
+`--topic <pr topic>`. If that run reports 0 missing, the refusal is false. Then deliver the
+dispatch past it by the orchestrator's ruling, and append no copy.

+## P657: the tick's RED-UNOWNED reads a carried merge verdict as no verdict
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT the orchestrator_tick.py part as a carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3; REJECT the verdict_audit.py part (refuted: its merge arm does not compare the head).
+
+Source: triage queue line 334.
+
+Instances, verified at the refs:
+- #3452: verdict/3452 (79e2d9dcba) reads `Fix review: merge e099eff6a5`; the PR head 586f8ebec5
+  is a merge of origin/main whose first parent is e099eff6a5.
+- #3428: verdict/3428 (eaa8684e75) reads `Fix review: merge 846f2dc07b`; the PR head c6b73e7a0a
+  is a merge of origin/main whose first parent is 846f2dc07b.
+
+Cause, measured in the code:
+- tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py:253-256, `verdict_kind`, returns `merge` only when the
+  verdict names exactly the head. The bucket classifier (:1013-1014) therefore never reads a
+  merge verdict on a main remerge as `verdicted`. It falls through, and a PR with a red check
+  and no seat on it prints `red ..., no verdict at head, no seat on it` (:1031-1032,
+  `red-unowned`).
+- The tick already owns the train's carry predicate: `_carries(verdict, head)` (:1067-1073)
+  runs `app_approve.sh --carry` through ledger.app_approve_carries, and REVIEW OWED uses it.
+  The bucket classifier does not.
+- The verdict_audit.py half is refuted. Its merge arm (verdict_audit.py:64-66) does not
+  compare the verdict sha with the head: it prints `UNHELD ... owed to the merge train` only
+  when the PR is absent from the train log and nobody holds it. Both instances were in the
+  train, so verdict_audit printed nothing for them, and it never prints "no verdict at head".
+  The words come only from the tick. This is not a duplicate of verdict_audit's own state.
+
+Duplicate check: no carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3, R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P2 or R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER
+names the bucket classifier's carry read; R10-ORCH-DISPATCH-REG carry 12 (REVIEW OWED's carry
+skip) is built and is a different line.
+
+Accepted change (carry): when the latest verdict is `Fix review: merge <at>` and `at` is not the
+head, the classifier asks `_carries(at, head)` before any owed arm; a carried head is
+`verdicted`. A failed fetch carries nothing (the head stays as today). The `WAIT is not red`
+half of the ask needs no separate read: a carried head returns before the red arm.
+
+Basis: severity-exempt defect repair (a false owed line, two instances in one day, each an
+orchestrator turn and a merge-seat read), reusing a predicate the tick already holds. On the
+20% bar alone it would be REJECTed.

+## P665: the roster's one string `model`
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT as a low-priority carry on R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE (the roster_lib seam), superseding P525's REJECT on new facts.
+
+Source: the orchestrator's message, 2026-11-11 about 22:15Z (no queue line).
+
+Instances:
+- At the roster ea774b53f3, R10-REPLAY-OPEN-LOG holds `"model": "sonnet"`. It is the one string
+  among 478 groups: 469 objects, 8 null.
+- tools/audit/seat/review_strength.py:251 calls `.get("fixer")` on it and crashes.
+  tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py:182 and :202 read a non-dict as `{}` and silently drop it.
+- P525 (batch 141) rejected the tool change because the datum was the cheaper cure. That cure is
+  not available. roster_edit.py has no op that writes `model` (its ops are append-carry,
+  append-group, edit-brief, mark-carry, set-after, set-files, set-resume, set-size, set-source,
+  set-stage and wire-issue). The orchestrator rules out a hand commit on the roster.
+
+Duplicate check: no carry names the model shape. R10-CI-PRIORITY-PAUSE is the only open group
+whose files include roster_lib.py.
+
+Accepted change: one reader, `roster_lib.group_model(group)`. It returns the object, maps a string
+s to `{"fixer": s}`, and maps anything else to `{}`. review_strength.py and cloud_dispatch.py read
+the model only through it. roster_edit.py append-group refuses a non-object `model` in the group
+it adds. The existing datum is never refused, because the reader tolerates it.
+
+Basis: a low-severity defect whose only cure is now a tool change. It is low priority within the
+group, behind carries 4 to 6.

+

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 219
+
+Sources: triage queue lines 346 to 349, four PROPOSAL lines of 2026-11-11, ruled as P669 to
+P672. Line numbers are at origin/main 61afd4f2db. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster
+e2623f542c. Every accepted part is a carry on an existing group, so the open-PR cap does not
+bear on them.
+
+## P669: the core quota emptied, and the shim's count covers only a third of it
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT (a) one host-wide gh call log, as a carry on R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE; DEFER (b) the cloud-share measurement and the second token.
+
+Source: triage queue line 346 (orchestrator, 2026-11-11T22:25:23Z). The core bucket read 0 of
+5000 at 22:25Z (reset 22:25:35Z). `gh_calls.py --top --since 21:26Z` counted 1180 calls, so the
+line attributes about 3800 calls to callers the shim cannot see, chiefly cloud seats.
+
+Instances, measured from the two shim logs over the bucket's hour (21:25:35Z to 22:25:35Z,
+`awk '$1>=...&&$1<...'` over each log and its `.1`):
+- `~/hpo-orch/r10s6/gh-calls.log`, the log `gh_calls.py` reads under the
+  orchestrator's `HPO_STATE_DIR`: 1188 lines. That is the line's 1180.
+- `~/.local/state/hpo/gh-calls.log`, the default home: 1833 lines in the same hour. No line
+  shares a stamp and pid with the other log, so the two are disjoint.
+- So the shim logged 3021 calls in that hour, not 1180. 1833 of them (61%) are invisible to the
+  orchestrator's `--top`.
+- Top callers in the default log: merge_train.py 1079, pass.py 331, blind_spots.py 321, `zsh -c`
+  91. Across both logs merge_train.py logged about 1176 calls, about 24% of the bucket.
+- The remainder the shim did not log is at most 5000 - 3021 = 1979 (about 40%). It also holds the
+  extra pages of each `--paginate` call (the shim logs one line per call), and record_row.py's
+  urllib read (the blind spot gh_calls.py states). The cloud share in it is not measured.
+
+Cause of (a): tools/audit/seat/shims/seat-gh:64-65 writes to `${HPO_STATE_DIR:-$HOME/.local/state/hpo}/gh-calls.log`,
+so each caller's environment chooses the log. gh_calls.py:744 reads only `state_dir()/gh-calls.log`.
+The token and its bucket are host-wide, so a per-state-dir log splits a single quantity.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE idx 5 (P588) is about the absence of the shim and the
+tick loop's PATH. Idx 6 (P591) is about the comment guard. Neither names the split log. Not a
+duplicate.
+
+Accepted change (a): the call log is host-wide. The shim writes to one log fixed at install (the
+default home's gh-calls.log) whatever the caller's HPO_STATE_DIR. `gh_calls.py --top` reads that
+log, plus any distinct `$HPO_STATE_DIR/gh-calls.log` left by an older shim, and labels each
+source's count. Self-test: a call made under HPO_STATE_DIR=X is counted by `--top` run with
+HPO_STATE_DIR unset, and the reverse. Null control: one log and one call print today's tables.
+Add a mutant that drops the second source.
+
+Basis: a medium defect repair (R10-GH-READ-RESIDUE, severity medium, carries-open) and over 20% on
+the API-call attribution measure (61% of logged calls were unread). The owner's no-API-hammering
+order (2026-11-08) needs the spenders named.
+
+Deferred (b): to measure the cloud share, by a per-seat count or a second token for cloud seats.
+Re-raise it after (a) builds, if in an hour where the bucket empties the rate_limit `used` figure,
+less the REST requests the host log accounts for (with paginated pages counted), exceeds 1000
+(20% of the bucket). Issuing a second token is a credential action for the owner, not a triage
+destination.
+
+## P670: the relay relays a probe ref that was disposed at its sha
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT as a carry on R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE (probe_arm skips a rev-/revt- ref disposed at its sha).
+
+Source: triage queue line 347 (the dispatch seat via the orchestrator, 2026-11-11T22:25:50Z).
+
+Instances:
+- ~/hpo-orch/r10s6/dispositions.tsv:164 holds `refs/heads/probe/rev-3481-c0d2fd50
+  6f2ab2974dca... 2026-11-11T22:13:16Z relay-dispose`.
+- ~/hpo-orch/r10s6/tick.txt.relay.log:29-38. At 22:23:24Z the relay relayed that
+  ref at the same sha. It pushed review/3481 a61af580 and logged `OWED verdict-unposted #3481
+  7c7f0608`. The verdict came from a reviewer below the fixer's model. The local stopgap disposed
+  review/3481 at a61af580.
+- Cause: in tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh probe_arm, a ref that is not `probe/rev-*` or
+  `probe/revt-*` checks `disposed` (:341). A rev-/revt- ref checks only cloud-relayed (:342) and the
+  refused list (:343-348), then goes onto the relay list (:349). A disposition never stops a relay.
+  The arm's own header (:38-42) says that probe/rev-* is OWED until disposed. Today a disposition
+  takes the ref off the level but not off the relay.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE idx 12 (P546) makes dispose take handoff-wip refs
+and makes the carry-fold arm and bus.sh orphans honour dispositions. Idx 20 (P575) is about
+ledger.py covered(). R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF idx 17 (P332) is about confirm_arm on closed PRs.
+None covers the probe_arm rev-/revt- relay path. Not a duplicate.
+
+Accepted change: before a rev-/revt- ref is written to the relay list, probe_arm skips it when
+`disposed "$ref" "$sha"` holds, the same check :341 makes for other probe refs. A disposed ref that
+moves is relayed again at its new sha. Self-test: a rev- ref disposed at its sha is not relayed
+and no review/<n> is pushed. Null controls: an undisposed rev- ref is relayed as today, and a
+disposed ref whose tip moved is relayed at the new sha. Add a mutant that drops the check.
+
+Basis: under 20% on cost (1 instance). The basis is severity-exempt only: it repairs observed
+wrong behaviour on a medium group, and the defect let a verdict from below the required model
+reach the post path. On the cost bar alone it would be REJECTed. The cost is about 2 lines plus
+a self-test arm, in a file the group already owns.
+
+## P671: the train's head wait never runs the stale check
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT as a carry on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 (wait_ci runs the stale re-run while a required context stays pending).
+
+Source: triage queue line 348 (orchestrator, 2026-11-11T22:27:34Z). Stopgap in
+~/hpo-orch/r10s6/s14/sweep.md:675.
+
+Instances:
+- #3455 at cbf80c6e waited from poll 1 to poll 19 (t+4370 s of 7320 s). It was waiting on gate
+  check-run 130782293389, which was queued over run 43089450993, a run that had already completed
+  (left over from the GitHub outage). Four newer gate runs at the same head were green. A hand
+  `merge_train.py unstale cbf80c6e` cleared it in one call (sweep.md:675). The line's cost figure
+  is about 73 min of a stalled critical-path train, with 21 PRs spooled.
+- Cause, at 61afd4f2db: tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py `unstale` (:3648-3672) runs only from
+  `land` (:2722), and that is after the head wait. `wait_ci` (:1905 onward) polls `latest_runs`.
+  A queued check-run over a completed run reads pending on every poll, so the wait never reaches
+  `land`. The other way out of it is the wait cap.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 idx 13 (P567) widens `unstale` to re-run red deferrals, and
+it still runs inside `land`. Idx 20 (P659) is about the wait cap during an outage. Neither moves
+the stale check into the wait. Not a duplicate.
+
+Accepted change:
+- Split the re-run half of `unstale` into its own step that returns the runs it re-ran, each run
+  once per head. `unstale` keeps that step followed by its wait.
+- `wait_ci` calls the re-run step at poll 3, and every 6th poll after that, while a required
+  context is still pending. It logs the STALE line and goes on waiting. It never calls `wait_ci`
+  recursively.
+- Cost: one `actions/runs/<id>` read per pending required check-run, at those polls only.
+
+Tests:
+- Self-test: the #3455 shape (a queued check-run over a completed run, with green gate runs
+  beside it) is re-run once by poll 3, and the wait then concludes.
+- Null control: a check-run that is pending over a run still in progress is not re-run.
+- A second pass at the same head re-runs nothing.
+- A mutant that drops the call keeps the fixture waiting to its cap.
+
+Basis: under 20% on the cost bar (1 instance). The basis is severity-exempt only: R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2
+is a medium group, and this repairs observed wrong behaviour on the critical path. On the bar
+alone it would be REJECTed.
+
+## P672: REVIEW STALLED fires on a review that came back and is held for CI
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT as a carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 (REVIEW STALLED reads the dispatch's probe ref before it flags).
+
+Source: triage queue line 349 (orchestrator, 2026-11-11T22:29:12Z).
+
+Instances:
+- #3479 at d925d867 printed `REVIEW STALLED ... 95m`. Its review had already returned as
+  probe/rev-3479-aeb68873 f36a81b9 at 20:38:46Z. At 22:23:20Z the relay held it
+  `HELD-PENDING-CI #3479 d925d867` (~/hpo-orch/r10s6/tick.txt.relay.log:27-28).
+- Cause, at 61afd4f2db: tools/audit/seat/orchestrator_tick.py `verdict_levels` (:720-729) prints
+  the line when three things hold: the head is in the dispatch record, no approver verdict names
+  it, and `_reviewer_ref_age` (:1046) is over STALL_MINUTES (90, :133). It never looks for the
+  returned probe ref.
+- owed_unactioned.py.md:7 maps the line to "re-fire the reviewer". The false line therefore
+  calls for a second reviewer seat on a review that is already finished, and it opens a race
+  between two verdicts.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-TICK-LEVELS and R10-FLY-TICK-APPROVAL-OWED built the line (P328) and are
+done. R10-REVIEW-DISPATCH-RESIDUE idx 23 (P585) is about the relay's pending-ci RED. No carry
+on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 names REVIEW STALLED. Not a duplicate.
+
+Accepted change:
+- When the stall condition holds, the tick looks for the dispatch's probe ref,
+  probe/rev-<N>-<nonce8>, with the nonce taken from the dispatch record. It uses one git read, and
+  only for a PR that has already met the condition.
+- If that ref exists, the tick prints `REVIEW RETURNED: #N <head8> probe <sha8> <m>m` instead. That
+  line is not flagged and is not on owed_unactioned's re-fire list.
+- With no probe ref, the line stays REVIEW STALLED.
+
+Tests:
+- Self-test: the #3479 shape (dispatched, no verdict, a probe ref at the nonce) prints REVIEW
+  RETURNED and no REVIEW STALLED.
+- Null control: the same case without the probe ref still prints REVIEW STALLED.
+- A probe ref at another nonce does not suppress the line.
+- A mutant that skips the probe read restores the false line.
+
+Basis: under 20% on the cost bar (1 instance; the frequency is unmeasured because the board keeps
+only its last state). The basis is severity-exempt only: R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 is a medium group, and
+this repairs observed wrong behaviour whose instructed action wastes a reviewer seat. On the bar
+alone it would be REJECTed.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 220
+
+Sources: triage queue line 350 (2026-11-11T22:43:06Z, carry-fold seat via orchestrator), ruled
+as P673. Line numbers are at origin/main 61afd4f2db. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster

+on it.

+## P673: the carry-fold arm re-prints OWED for superseded wip refs; a gate_lock.py env leak
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT (b) the gate_lock.py priority-env leak, as a carry on R10-PREPR-RESIDUE; REJECT (a) the carry-fold proposal as a duplicate of R10-RELAY-NOBODY-STALL carry idx 1 (P642).
+
+Source: triage queue line 350. (a) 10 of 12 carry-fold level lines at 22:50Z were stale:
+handoff-wip/<t> kept its BLOCKED.md after handoff-body/<t> named the handoff/<t> tip. Two
+cleanup seats ran today (5 refs at about 21Z, 10 at about 22:50Z). Proposed: body_push.sh
+deletes handoff-wip/<t> on success, or the arm skips a wip ref whose handoff-body names the
+handoff tip. (b) A lead from the archived wip tag
+archive/handoff-wip/r10-hotfix-restore-base-skew.69b3c17f3701: a local-only fix a27995c354 to
+tests/gate_lock.py, never pushed.
+
+Instances:
+- (a) `jq '.groups[]|select(.group=="R10-RELAY-NOBODY-STALL")|.carry[1]'` on the roster at
+  7443303217: CARRY-FOLD-SUPERSEDED (s6-batch211.md#P642). Its repair (a) drops the level line
+  for a wip ref whose topic has a handoff-body/<topic> committed later than the wip commit, and
+  repair (b) does the same when fix/<topic> merged. The group is `not-started`, severity medium.
+  Line 350's 9 of 10 (body newer than wip) are exactly repair (a)'s case.
+- (b) `git cat-file -t a27995c354`: not a valid object; the commit exists only as the diff in
+  the archived tag's BLOCKED.md (`git show 69b3c17f3701:BLOCKED.md`, lines 7-53). On main,
+  tests/gate_lock.py :1628 and :1738 start the `normal` waiter of the two ordering arms of
+  `_priority_cases` with no `_Env(None)`, and tools/pr/prepr.sh :4159-4161 exports
+  `HPO_GATE_PRIORITY`, so that waiter inherits the caller's priority.
+- (b) measured: main's `tests/gate_lock.py` copied to scratch; `_priority_cases(g)` run under
+  `python3 -I`:
+  - `HPO_GATE_PRIORITY` unset (null control): `0 of 14 failed`.
+  - `HPO_GATE_PRIORITY=1` (outside and critical-path branches): `0 of 14 failed`.
+  - `HPO_GATE_PRIORITY=2` (a hotfix branch, gate_priority.py :104): `2 of 14 failed`. The two
+    are "an urgent waiter takes before an older normal one" and "the heavy-slot pool orders by
+    the same rule".
+  So prepr.sh on any hotfix branch records these two failures, and the archived seat's
+  `2 of 2707 ENTITY` red is this leak. #3463 merged R10-HOTFIX-RESTORE-BASE-SKEW part 1 without
+  the fix (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 5ec2425619 origin/main` is true). That group is
+  carries-open, so it cannot receive a carry.
+
+Duplicate check: (a) is P642 / R10-RELAY-NOBODY-STALL idx 1. (b) No roster carry names
+a27995c354, `_Env(None)` or `priority_first` (grep of the roster JSON at 7443303217).
+
+Accepted change: (b) one carry on R10-PREPR-RESIDUE (in-progress, severity medium; it owns
+tests/gate_lock.py and tools/pr/prepr.sh). In `_priority_cases`, the `normal` waiter of both
+ordering arms enters under `_Env(None)`. Demonstration: the two arms fail with
+`HPO_GATE_PRIORITY=2` exported on the base and pass on the fix. Null control: unset passes on
+both.
+
+Cost: (b) about 6 changed lines in one test file. tests/gate_lock.py has no row in
+tests/structure_budgets.json. No new file, check or API call. (a) none: no new carry.
+
+Binding:
+- (b) The destination's severity is medium, which skips the 20% bar. On the bar alone it would
+  still pass: a hotfix branch's prepr is red with no override, and hotfixes are the top
+  dispatch rank.
+- (a) The fix is already carried. The body_push.sh alternative adds a second mechanism in a
+  second file for the same level line, and it would not clear refs that are already orphaned,
+  which the arm-side repair does. Line 350's cost (two cleanup seats and near re-fires today)
+  bears on when idx 1 is dispatched, which is the orchestrator's call. It does not justify a
+  second carry. The stopgap (archive-tag, then delete) stays in use until then.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 221
+
+Sources: triage queue line 351 (orchestrator, 2026-11-11T23:37:14Z), ruled as P674. Line numbers
+are at origin/main 61afd4f2db. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster fa165de969.

+## P674: Dependabot #3483 red on typing; seat-no-return fires on dispatch refs never fired
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT (a) a new group R10-DEPENDABOT-3483-COMPAT, which re-locks #3483 with homeassistant-stubs held and makes Dependabot ignore the two typing-ruler pins; REJECT (b) a fired-record ledger for the no-return arm.
+
+Source: triage queue line 351. (a) Dependabot #3483 (pip group in /tests, 8 updates, head
+08d58a81bc) is red on `tests / typing`. Does it owe a compat group, as #3323 and #3414 did, or
+should the bump be refused? (b) Four `seat-no-return` lines at 23:26Z came from continuations the
+dispatch seat rendered and published at about 21Z, which the orchestrator never fired because
+the handoffs had already succeeded. Proposed: key the arm on a FIRED record, or delete a render
+that is not fired. Stopgap: OWED-ACK ttl=12.
+
+Instances:
+- (a) Typing job 130852340607 (`gh api .../actions/jobs/130852340607/logs`, line 467):
+  `FAIL homeassistant-stubs is pinned at 2026.9.3 [found 2026.10.0]`, then `REFUSING to
+  measure`, `1 of 5 typing-ruler checks FAILED`. The pin is `ruler.homeassistant_stubs` in
+  tests/typing_budgets.json :42 (with `ruler.mypy` :41), enforced by tests/typing_ruler.py
+  :467-472. The PR's diff moves homeassistant-stubs 2026.9.3 to 2026.10.0. Its other 7 bumps are
+  minor: bleak, cronsim, httpcore2, httpx2, regex, truststore, zeroconf.
+  `tests / nightly-status` is also red. Its cause was not examined here, and this ruling
+  claims nothing about it.
+- (a) The class: this is the third compat replacement of the /tests pip group. #3323 was
+  re-applied as a555d52ae8 (R10-DEPENDABOT-3323-COMPAT, done). #3414 was re-locked as f402c1e8a9
+  (R10-DEPENDABOT-3414-COMPAT, carries-open); its brief reads "the bot moved
+  homeassistant-stubs past the deliberate hold that tests/typing_ruler.py enforces". #3483
+  repeats that cause. Neither compat commit moved the stubs pin: `git show <c> --
+  tests/requirements-typing.txt | grep '^[-+]homeassistant-stubs'` is empty for both. The hold
+  is deliberate, because only CI can measure the census against the pinned pair (#504).
+- (a) .github/dependabot.yml :26-33 (the `/tests` pip entry) has `groups: pip: patterns: ["*"]`
+  and no `ignore`, so every weekly run may move the pair again.
+- (b) `grep -h 'SEAT ENDED NO RETURN' cloud-relay.log*` gives 4 lines in the relay log. The log
+  starts 2026-10-28T01:30Z and is 4727 lines long. All 4 are the four topics on line 351, and
+  each was published but never fired. The arm (tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh :751-801) keys on
+  the dispatch ref's age. Its header (:759) already names the disposal: "Deleting the dispatch
+  ref disposes it." `cloud_dispatch.py --publish` (:1503) pushes the ref at render time. Firing
+  is the orchestrator's RemoteTrigger call, outside the tree. No fixer fire record exists; the
+  ledger opens only `reviewer-fire` (cloud_dispatch.py :672-673).
+
+Duplicate check:
+- (a) No live group owns .github/dependabot.yml. R10-DEPENDABOT-3323-COMPAT is done and
+  R10-DEPENDABOT-3414-COMPAT is carries-open, so neither can receive a carry (roster
+  fa165de969).
+- (b) P376 (s6-batch115.md) narrowed the arm to split-part topics. Nothing has ruled on unfired
+  renders.
+
+Accepted change: (a) a new group R10-DEPENDABOT-3483-COMPAT, severity medium as for its two
+predecessors. The orchestrator adds it. Brief:
+1. Re-lock tests/requirements-typing.txt through its header's compile with the 7 non-stub bumps
+   of #3483. Hold homeassistant-stubs at 2026.9.3.
+2. In .github/dependabot.yml's `/tests` pip entry, add `ignore` for `homeassistant-stubs` and
+   `mypy`, the two pins `ruler` in tests/typing_budgets.json records. Add a comment saying
+   moving either is a deliberate re-record of the typing census (#504), never a bot bump.
+3. Close #3483 as superseded after the merge.
+
+Demonstration: `tests / typing` is green at the head with the ruler printing `ok
+homeassistant-stubs is pinned at 2026.9.3`. Null control: the same compile without the hold
+reproduces this FAIL line.
+
+Cost:
+- (a) One lock file and about 6 config lines. tests/requirements-typing.txt and
+  .github/dependabot.yml have no row in tests/structure_budgets.json. One fixer plus a sonnet
+  review, as for #3414.
+- (b) Rejected design: a fixer fire record means a new ledger kind, a write on the orchestrator's
+  fire path and a read in cloud_relay.sh, a hot file, plus self-test arms. That is about 40 or
+  more lines across two files and the orchestrator's procedure.
+
+Binding:
+- (a) The destination's severity is medium, which skips the 20% bar. On the bar alone, the
+  `ignore` passes as the class barrier: it is the third compat replacement of one Dependabot
+  group (#3323, #3414, #3483), and each cost a fixer and a review seat. Refusing the bump
+  instead would leave the 7 minor bumps to recur weekly with the same stubs move. Under the
+  over-20 rule this group is not critical path, hotfix or outside, so it waits for a slot.
+  That is the orchestrator's to schedule.
+- (b) The measured harm is 4 false lines in 14 days, each cleared by deleting its dispatch ref
+  (one `git push origin --delete`). That disposal is already the arm's documented one. The
+  ledger costs more than it saves. The rule that costs nothing: a render the orchestrator
+  decides not to fire has its dispatch ref deleted at that decision. Delete the four refs above
+  now; the OWED-ACK ttl=12 stopgap is then moot.

@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 222
+
+Sources: triage queue line 352 (orchestrator, 2026-11-11T23:53:25Z), ruled as P675. Line numbers
+are at origin/main 046736a49f. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster 3c73aab046.
+
+## P675: a retired seat's clean branch worktrees hold update_pr.sh at BUSY
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT, as a new group R10-UPDATE-PR-SEAT-WORKTREE, which widens update_pr.sh's detach of a clean worktree at the origin head from $P to the whole state dir, guarded by a live-process check.
+
+Source: triage queue line 352. update_pr.sh answered BUSY three times tonight. Each time
+fix/<topic> was checked out in a worktree of the retired merge seat s14-7 (wt3442, wt3355,
+wt3458), each clean and at the origin head. The relay retried silently every pass (13 min) until
+the orchestrator detached them by hand, and #3458's repair handoff waited 40 min. Proposed:
+widen update_pr.sh's existing detach to seat scratch worktrees under the state dir, or have the
+merge seat's recycle step detach its worktrees. Stopgap: all of s14-7's are detached.
+
+Instances:
+- tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh :44 sets `P=${HPO_STATE_DIR:-...}/pr`. :64-68 detach another
+  worktree on $BR only if it is under `$P/`, clean, and its HEAD is an ancestor of origin/$BR.
+  :69 exits BUSY (75) on any other worktree holding $BR. A seat's worktree under
+  `$HPO_STATE_DIR/s14/seat/...` is clean at the origin head yet outside `$P/`, so it reaches
+  :69.
+- `grep -h -i 'checked out elsewhere' cloud-relay.log tick.txt.relay.log`: 5 logged BUSY lines.
+  2 of 5 (40%) name a seat worktree, merge/s14-7 and merge/s14-5; the other 3 name `$P` itself.
+  The relay retries without logging each pass, so tonight's three are mostly absent from the
+  logs. These counts are a floor.
+- `ls -d s14/seat/*/*/wt*`: 25 seat worktrees exist under the state dir. Merge s14-7 holds 18
+  (detached tonight), merge s14-5 holds 4, and dispatch s14-40 and s14-41 hold 3. Each recycle
+  of a standing merge seat leaves its set behind.
+- Cost seen: #3458's repair handoff waited 40 min, about 3 relay passes. Each further hold costs
+  13 min per pass until a person notices.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-UPDATE-PR-LOCK, R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS and R10-OPENPR-SILENT are done.
+R10-OPENER-REUSE and R10-RELAY-HANDOFF-ARM are absorbed. R10-CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP is carries-open.
+None names a seat worktree outside $P (roster 3c73aab046). tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh collects
+only a merged pull request's worktrees, so an open PR's branch, as here, is out of its reach.
+
+Accepted change: a new group, size S, severity medium (it holds relay repair handoffs, the
+critical path's re-entry), sonnet fixer and reviewer. File: tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh, plus
+its instruments page.
+- In the :64 loop, the candidate set is every worktree on $BR under `$HPO_STATE_DIR/`, not only
+  under `$P/`.
+- Keep both existing guards: clean, and HEAD an ancestor of origin/$BR.
+- Add a third guard, for a worktree outside $P: no live process has its cwd inside it (`lsof -a
+  -d cwd`, as worktree_gc.sh :66 reads it). An unreadable lsof keeps the worktree, so the run
+  stays BUSY as today.
+
+Demonstration, in update_pr.sh's self-test: a clean seat worktree at origin's head under the state
+dir is detached and the run proceeds. That fails on the base, where the run is BUSY, and passes on
+the fix. Null controls: with a live process cwd'd in that worktree, the run stays BUSY; with a
+commit origin lacks, the run stays BUSY.
+
+Cost: about 8 lines in update_pr.sh, plus a self-test arm of about 15 lines. No new file. No API
+call; lsof is local. update_pr.sh has no row in tests/structure_budgets.json. The rejected
+alternative, a detach step in the merge seat's recycle, costs no code. But it binds only a seat
+that ends cleanly, and a recycled seat often ends on a token or time limit, so it fails exactly
+when the worktrees are left behind.
+
+Binding: the destination's severity is medium, which skips the 20% bar. On the bar alone, the
+logged share is 2 of 5 BUSY holds, 40%, a floor, so it would pass. The live-process guard keeps
+it from detaching a seat that is using the checkout, which is what the `$P/` scope protected.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 223
+
+Sources: triage queue line 353 (orchestrator, 2026-11-12T00:01:47Z), ruled as P676. Line numbers
+are at origin/main 6d16af36c2. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster dc65b69234.
+
+## P676: prepr.sh's self-test compares padded wc output as a string and fails on Darwin
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT (a) the site fix, as a new hotfix group R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-WC-PAD on the
+orchestrator's go; DEFER (b) the raw-`wc` string-compare lint until a third instance of the shape.
+
+Source: triage queue line 353. Since #3455 (commit 003f89cf9c), main's prepr.sh self-test fails
+on macOS: one arm compares `wc -l` output as a string, and BSD wc pads it with blanks. Every
+full-prepr open or update from the orchestrator's macOS host is refused, including the
+r10-hotfix-opener-unblock handoff at 00:00Z. CI runs on Linux and never sees it. Local stopgap:
+a wc shim on the instruments' PATH strips leading blanks.
+
+Instances:
+- tools/pr/prepr.sh :2403 `st "$(mg status --porcelain | wc -l)" 0 "and the in-place run leaves
+  the work tree clean"`. `st` compares strings, so BSD's `       0` is not `0`.
+  `git log -L2403,2403:tools/pr/prepr.sh` names 003f89cf9c as the commit that added the line.
+- pr/r10-hotfix-opener-unblock/p1.log :22-23: `REFUSE self-test 536 passed, 1 failed` and
+  `FAIL and the in-place run leaves the work tree clean (got        0, wanted 0)`.
+- Sweep of the proposed scope, at 6d16af36c2: `git grep -nE 'wc -[lc]' -- '*.sh'`, minus lines
+  that pipe through `tr -d` or wrap the count in `$(( ))`, keeping string compares (`=`, `!=`, or
+  an `st`/`chk`/`ans` argument), and excluding numeric `-lt/-ge/-eq` tests (padding-safe). It
+  returns 2 lines. prepr.sh:2403 is the defect. app_push.sh:1095 pipes `wc -c` into awk `$1`,
+  which is padding-safe. No `var=$(... | wc -l)` assignment without `tr -d` exists under tools/
+  or .claude/. About 20 other sites (cloud_relay.sh, handoff_push.sh, tick_loop.sh,
+  session-start.sh) already follow the `| tr -d ' '` convention. The sweep therefore owes no
+  second site. The fixer re-runs it at its base.
+- Class: this is the second Darwin-only prepr self-test red to block local opens. The first was
+  R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-SELFTEST-DARWIN (done; the shim's HOME). The two causes differ. The raw-wc
+  string-compare shape has 1 instance.
+
+Duplicate check: R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-SELFTEST-DARWIN is done and fixed a different arm (planted HOME
+under the python3 shim). R10-PREPR-RESIDUE (in progress, 25 carries) and R10-HOTFIX-OPENER-UNBLOCK
+(not started) name no wc padding (roster dc65b69234).
+
+Accepted change (a): a new group, size XS, class hotfix, severity high (it refuses every local
+full-prepr open and update, and the hotfix lane opens through that path). The bar is exempt by
+severity. Edit prepr.sh:2403 to compare `$(( $(... | wc -l) ))` or pipe through `tr -d ' '`,
+as its siblings do. Add a test that the arm passes under a padding wc on PATH (a null control:
+it fails before the edit). Then retire the local wc shim from the instruments' PATH, so the
+macOS host again runs what main ships. Sonnet fixer and reviewer. File: tools/pr/prepr.sh.
+
+Deferred (b): a bare_array.py-style lint for raw `wc` in a string compare. 1 instance of the
+shape against about 20 compliant sites. A new check file and its self-test cost more than a
+one-site recurrence. It becomes due at the third instance (audit-class barrier). The cheaper
+class barrier, a Darwin run of prepr's self-test, is the stage that would also have caught the
+first instance. It belongs to whichever group next owns prepr's self-test host coverage, and is
+not built here.
+
+Cost: XS. One line in tools/pr/prepr.sh plus one self-test arm; no new file. prepr.sh is not
+on a capped list in tests/structure_budgets.json.
+
+Binding: the orchestrator's go for the new group. Until it lands, the local wc shim stays in
+place.

@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 224
+
+Sources: the orchestrator's message to the triage seat (2026-11-12T01:00Z), ruled as P677, P678 and
+P679. Line numbers are at origin/main 47788534da. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster 97a9e7a857.
+
+## P677: a false `mark-carry implemented` could only be cured by dropping the entry
+
+Verdict: REJECT (a) evidence-checked marks and (b) an `unmark-carry` op. The live owner of
+roster_edit.py residue is R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 (not started, L, severity medium; its `files` list
+roster_edit.py). Nothing is carried there from this proposal.
+
+Source: the orchestrator. A `mark-carry R10-STANDING-CONTRACTS-P2 ... implemented 47788534da` was
+queued without checking the merge. The #3464 merge did not touch dev/programme/HANDOVER.md, which
+carry e8e05480 asked for. The drain applied the mark (roster a3c0451c5f). The cure was to move the
+carry to R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 (append-carry, cd930f21eb) and drop the false entry (97a9e7a857).
+
+Instances:
+- False implemented marks: 1. Over the roster branch log, 11 drop-carry commits removed a line
+  carrying `[implemented:` (`git log --grep=drop-carry` plus each diff's removed lines). 10 are the
+  2026-11-10 carry-drain cleanup: queue lines 1695, 1960 and 4041-4115 are dedupe and legacy drops,
+  not corrections. The 11th, 97a9e7a857, is this one.
+- Denominator: 283 `mark-carry ... implemented` lines in the roster queue
+  (`grep -c 'mark-carry .* implemented' roster-queue-s7.txt`). That gives 1 false mark in 283
+  (0.35%).
+- roster_edit.py:138-146 states the design: `implemented` "records that the sha is on main; it is
+  not a verification".
+- roster_lib.py:498-518: carries-open is outside the carry-destination set by owner ruling
+  (R10-CARRY-SINK-BARRIER, tvofi 2026-11-10), so append-carry and `moved` refuse it on purpose.
+
+Rejected (a), an evidence-checked mark (a path the merge touched, or `--evidence <cmd>`):
+- It adds a required argument to every mark, for 283 marks so far, to catch a 0.35% error rate.
+  That is far under the 20% bar.
+- A path check is also the wrong test. Many carries are satisfied by a change in a file other than
+  the one they name, or by a text that a diff stat cannot read. Such a check would refuse true marks
+  and pass any false mark whose merge touched the named file for another reason.
+- The countermeasure that would have caught this instance is the reading itself: `git diff --stat
+  M^1 M -- <file>` plus reading the text. It is already binding in the triage seat's handoff (rules
+  learned, 2026-11-12).
+
+Rejected (b), `unmark-carry --match`:
+- On P2 it would have put the carry back on a carries-open group. By roster_lib.py:498-518 that is
+  a stage no seat builds a carry in, so it recreates the sink the barrier closed.
+- If the false mark had discharged the last pending carry, `close_discharged` (roster_edit.py:647-
+  659) would already have written `done`. An unmark would then also have to reverse a stage
+  closure: new logic in a 3074-line file, for 1 instance.
+- The cure that exists costs 2 queue ops: append-carry to the live owner, then drop-carry --match.
+  It ran correctly at cd930f21eb and 97a9e7a857. The extra cost that night was 4 refused ops
+  (queue 4636-4639, index-keyed or onto carries-open), and the seat handoff now records the route.
+
+Cost avoided: one op and its self-test arms in roster_edit.py (not on a capped list in
+tests/structure_budgets.json); none incurred.
+
+Binding: the 0.35% rate, and carry_receivable's carries-open exclusion. A second false mark that
+the seat's reading rule does not prevent reopens (a) as a check on the triage seat's own queue
+lines, not on roster_edit.py.
+
+## P678: the opener's backoff held a hotfix behind a host failure
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT (b) an `open_driver.py retry <topic>` verb, as a carry on
+R10-FLY-OPENER-STALE-ENV. REJECT (a) the 5-minute floor for hotfix, outside and critical topics.
+
+Source: the orchestrator. r10-hotfix-opener-unblock failed on Darwin's wc padding (P676), and the
+orchestrator reset open-driver/fails.json by hand.
+
+Instances (open-driver/open-driver.log, 2026-11-10T08:50Z..2026-11-12T00:25Z):
+- r10-hotfix-opener-unblock 80779d2e:
+  - RESULT rc=1 at 00:00:11Z, START again at 00:10:11Z, opened rc=0 at 00:25:11Z.
+  - n=1 backs off 1800 s (open_driver.py:78 and :146-147), so the driver alone would have retried
+    at 00:30:11Z.
+  - The hand reset cut the hold from 30 min to 10 min. The log does not support a 70-minute hold
+    attributable to the backoff.
+- All hotfix and outside topics: 12 rc≠0 results.
+  - 5 are STALE CHECKOUT. R10-FLY-OPENER-STALE-ENV already re-keys those to the tools checkout
+    HEAD.
+  - 1 is this host failure.
+  - The rest are conflicts or push refusals, whose p1.log has since been overwritten by the
+    successful run.
+  - Fail-to-restart gaps: 31, 5, 30, 73, 17, 17, 30, 28, 113 and 10 min.
+- Hand resets of fails.json: 3 in 40 h. Two left backups (fails.json.bak, 2026-11-11 08:27Z;
+  fails.json.bak-s14-1352, 13:52Z), and the third is tonight's 00:10:11Z restart, 20 min before the
+  backoff expired.
+
+Rejected (a), the floor:
+- The backoff keys on (topic, sha) (open_driver.py:247), so a new head is never held. A same-sha
+  retry fails again until something outside the branch changes: here, the wc shim on PATH.
+- At a 5-minute floor, each retry before the cure is a full prepr run. START to RESULT was 15 min
+  here.
+- The best case saves 20 min once in 40 h. The cost is a wasted 15-minute local prepr for each
+  retry made before the cure.
+- The environment-keyed retry that removes the failure class without spinning is the STALE
+  CHECKOUT rule already briefed on R10-FLY-OPENER-STALE-ENV.
+
+Accepted change (b), carry on R10-FLY-OPENER-STALE-ENV (not started, S, severity high, sonnet; it
+owns the backoff seam in open_driver.py; no overlap with R10-HOTFIX-OPENER-UNBLOCK, whose brief
+names no backoff):
+- Add `open_driver.py retry <topic> [<sha>]`. It removes that topic's fails.json entry, or the
+  (topic, sha) entry when a sha is given, and prints the removed n, next and why.
+- It refuses a topic with no entry. It writes the file the same way a pass does (open_driver.py:249)
+  and reads it back after its write.
+- The instrument doc names it as the cure once an environment failure is fixed, replacing a hand
+  edit of a file a live loop rewrites every pass.
+- Acceptance in open_driver_selftest.py:
+  - (i) After `retry`, the next pass starts the topic inside its backoff window.
+  - (ii) Null control: without `retry`, the same pass skips it as backoff.
+  - (iii) Mutation: a verb that writes nothing turns (i) red.
+  - (iv) A topic with no entry is refused and writes nothing.
+- Figure against 20%: it replaces 3 hand edits in 40 h of a state file with one verb. The basis is
+  the destination's severity (high), which skips the machinery bar, and a hand edit's lost-write
+  risk: pass() loads fails.json at :225 and rewrites it at :249.
+
+Cost: about 20 lines in open_driver.py and 4 self-test arms. Neither file is on a capped list in
+tests/structure_budgets.json. The group stays S.
+
+Binding: the sha-keyed backoff (:247), which makes a same-sha floor retry repeat a failure until a
+human acts, and the 3 hand resets.
+
+## P679: a direct merge while a train batch proof is in flight
+
+Verdict: REJECT.
+
+Source: the orchestrator. #3355 and #3464 merged directly while batch 20261111-183624-b2 was
+inside its proof, and the train re-proves.
+
+Instances:
+- The b2 proof (batch/20261111-183624-b2-1 at b6870648) is built on 046736a49f
+  (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
+- Before #3355 (68d34ce0ab) and #3464 (47788534da), main had already moved past that base by
+  #3482 (6d16af36c2) and the bot's #3480 (d8768cde3e). Neither is in the proof.
+- One move is enough to owe the batch its MAIN-MOVED re-prove (merge_train.py:2660-2691; one
+  re-prove whatever the count of moves). The marginal re-prove cost of the two direct merges is
+  therefore 0.
+- Since the first 2026-11-11 batch (train.log:19383): 6 proofs pushed, and 3 `[MAIN-MOVED] before
+  #N's merge: re-proving` events.
+- Median proof time is 1936 s (p90 2904 s) over 43 proofs (the max `t+` per `waiting proof` line).
+
+Rejected:
+- A print in merge_pr.sh appears when the merge is already executing, not when it is chosen, so
+  it changes no decision.
+- The decision point already has the information: the live train's spool and its train.log
+  `waiting proof ... t+` line.
+- The cheaper route already exists: `merge_train.py` add joins the live train after the running
+  batch (train.log: `ADDED #3485 to the live train`).
+- Measured benefit tonight: 0 re-proves avoidable.
+
+Cost avoided: about 8 lines in merge_pr.sh and a self-test arm.
+
+Binding: the zero marginal re-prove; a print at execution time cannot price a decision.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 225
+
+Source: the orchestrator's message to the triage seat (2026-11-12), ruled as P680. Line numbers
+are at origin/main 47788534da. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster 8ab8d08a00.

+## P680: main's instrument-self-tests job is red on an under-scoped prepr closure
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT as a new hotfix group, R10-HOTFIX-MAIN-IST-PREPR-SCOPE (size S, severity high,
+class hotfix). Main is red, so the 20% bar does not apply.
+
+Evidence: main's push CI at 6d16af36c2 (#3482 merge), job governance / instrument-self-tests,
+prints `UNDER-SCOPED step prepr: files misses ['dev/audit/harnesses/mutant_guard.py',
+'tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py']` and `selftest_scope check: 111 gated step(s), 1 refusal(s)`.
+The workflow requires "0 refusal(s)". Two notes also report over-scoped entries: steps
+cloud-dispatcher and prepr each name 1 file no longer read.
+
+Home: the table is `tools/ci/selftest_closures.json`, read and written by
+`tools/ci/selftest_scope.py`, whose docstring states the re-record rule (`record` on Linux with
+strace, or commit the `--write` measurement main uploads as the `selftest-closures` artifact).
+No open roster group owns this red. Every group naming selftest_scope or the closure table is
+done. R10-HOTFIX-PREPR-WC-PAD touches the same script, but its fixer was dispatched before this
+red was known, so it does not get this as a carry.
+
+Cause: the #3455 merge, 046736a49f, changed `tools/pr/prepr.sh` so that its self-test runs
+`tools/audit/seat/mutant_run.py`. The closure entry for the prepr step was not re-recorded.
+
+Cheaper detector: `prepr.sh` or ci_predict could run `selftest_scope.py check` before handoff
+whenever a gated step's script changes. That is recorded as a carry for the root-cause record.
+This ruling does not build it.

+
+Source: triage queue line 318 (PRODUCT-RULING, #3452 body items 7052beca and 9ac8c410), answered
+by the fable probe result handoff-body/r10-product-ruling-dhw-hard-max at d507c499a85c, and the

+## P681: dhw_hard_max_temp product rulings for R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT both rulings as the probe states them: "Ruling: (1) round-down (2) respect-and-surface".
+
+Orchestrator decision, verbatim: ACCEPT both rulings as the probe states them — (1) a no-cycle
+hot-water write never exceeds the charge limit (round down on the entity's step; the user-safety
+ground is the scald risk of a silent, permanent round-up); (2) respect the ceiling and surface it,
+as the probe's section (2) specifies. Outside-derived work: it is built in round 10, as part 2 of
+R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT, never deferred.
+
+Destination and severity: (1) is a carry on R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT (severity high,
+stage in-progress, PR #3452 open), shipped as part 2 in its own pull request after #3452 merges.
+(2) is already the brief of R10-DISINFECTION-STEP-NOTICE (M, high, after the parent), with
+9ac8c410 moved there; nothing further is queued for it.
+
+Figure against 20%: the bar does not apply; this is an outside-derived product ruling under the
+mandate. Basis: 104 of 780 no-cycle census rows write above the charge limit `dhw_max_temp` at
+main and at the group's head; null control 455 on-step rows, 0 over. The ceiling is the charge
+limit, not `dhw_hard_max_temp`, which counts 64 of the 104 with the cycle enabled.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 227
+
+Source: the orchestrator's brief to triage seat s14-36 (2026-11-12), four proposals A-D, ruled as
+P682-P685. Line numbers are at origin/main b737e88eee. Roster read at handoff/audit-r10-roster
+fe123f912d.
+
+## P682: HELD-REVIEW releases behind a disposed or refused verdict
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+
+Finding: twice on 2026-11-12 (#3461 dispatch edf76a05, #3479 dispatch 14c317ab) a repair handoff sat
+HELD-REVIEW in `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh` (hold described at :127) behind a dispatch whose
+verdict had been returned, refused by the relay over red CI and disposed; each waited for a hand
+listing in cloud-handoff-release (about 15 and 12 minutes).
+Ruling: the hold releases when the dispatch's probe ref exists and the relay ledger records it
+disposed or refused; until that is built the level line names the state so the tick prints the cure.

+Evidence: the part-1 fixer's body (ref handoff-wip/r10-standing-contracts-p2-body dea4c2ae8f, BODY.md
+lines 20-26) cites one `Carry: dismissed: implemented at <sha>` line per carry. Spot-checked two on
+main: tools/pr/ci_predict.py:656 BOOTSTRAP constant and :872 its use (carry 0 (c), e566f7e02);
+dev/governance/roles/standing.md:27-30 "## Autofix hold" naming mutation-, closures- and
+claims-autofix (carry 3, 1b174e9b3). e566f7e02 is an ancestor of 1b174e9b3.
+Ops: mark-carry implemented 1b174e9b3 on carries 0-4. The part-1 fixer has nothing left to cut.

+## P698: ci_predict's throwaway clone reads local heads as origin/* (P687 reopened)
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Scope: tools/pr/ci_predict.py:666-692 (`ci_tree_run`); tests/throwaway_git.py:151-159.
+Evidence: second instance. body_push/open refused because the predictor ran CI's tree against a stale
+roster: a local refs/heads/handoff/audit-r10-roster, behind the remote, was what the steps read as
+origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster. Cause, read from the code: `throwaway_git_clone` is a plain
+`git clone --shared` of the local checkout, so the clone's refs/remotes/origin/* are the checkout's
+LOCAL heads (refs/heads/*), not its origin/* refs. `ci_tree_run` overwrites only
+refs/remotes/origin/main (with `tip`); every other origin/* a step reads (HPO_LANDED_ROSTER_REF, the
+roster and handoff refs) is a local branch of whatever age, or is absent. CI fetches them fresh.
+P687's first instance (a four-day-old base) is consistent with that class but was not located.
+Destination and severity: carry on R10-PREPR-RESIDUE (in-progress, owns ci_predict.py and
+body_push.sh), normal. Figure against 20%: two refused body_push/open runs (the first cost about 12 min; the second was not timed) on
+release-path heads; a predictor that predicts falsely makes every red it prints suspect.
+Fix shape: after the clone, set every refs/remotes/origin/* in the clone from the checkout's own
+refs/remotes/origin/* (or fetch the named refs), never from its refs/heads/*. Control: a self-test with a
+local head behind its origin/ twin, where the step reads the origin/ value.
+

+- idx 8: orchestrator.md:108-109 "read state only from the plan page and the ledger's digest".
+  Implemented at 1b174e9b3.
+- idx 19: standing.md:49 names `$HPO_STATE_DIR/alive/`. Implemented at 1b174e9b3.
+- idx 20: designer.md:15 reads the verdict at `design-verdict/<group>`; cloud_dispatch.py:351 pins it.
+  Implemented at 1b174e9b3.
+- R10-COMBI-TANK-PR-B idx 5: tests/features.py:9800 "`unwired_combi` exemption is gone".
+  Implemented at c2cb6262d4, inside #3398.
+Left open (doubtful at grep level, not ruled): R10-STANDING-CONTRACTS-P2 idx 7 (orchestrator.md:106
+says "never you inline", but no line says a seat stays until its replacement job is live), 9-18
+(retirement and beat-job items folded to ORCH-LEDGER; owner orders), 21-23 (liveness-hook amendments),
+27 (the HANDOVER.md standing-seats bullet names four seats plus triage; the roster seat is retired).
+R10-COMBI-TANK-PR-B idx 0-2 (owner rulings that bind the design, spent once PR B merged: they need a
+dismissal ruling, not a mark), 3 (the MFS 600 S figures: no 504 l or MFS in custom_components/*.py),
+6 and 7 (constraints on later stages: they stay as long as a stage can still break them).

+share of the savings residual it explains is unmeasured, which is the destination's measure-first.

+with the harness's exchange arm at PR B's merge base. Control: the null arm on the same day.

+6715477401 (scope all), made by triage s14-41.

+## P704: R10-BODY-CONTRACT carry 38 (Card 7 ruling, figure blocks) is already on main
+
+Verdict: NO-OP
+Scope: R10-BODY-CONTRACT carry 38, the only carry of the group not yet marked.
+Evidence: 8124343607 is an ancestor of origin/main; tools/pr/figure_block.py and
+tools/pr/figure_registry.json are in the tree; .github/workflows/pr-contract.yml:370-375 runs
+figure_lint.mjs on the body and re-renders generated figure blocks from the base's registry;
+tools/policy/figure_lint.mjs and tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs carry the figure checks. The fixer's
+stop record names the same files.
+Disposition: mark carry 38 implemented at 8124343607cea8683983bf5e1005e4b27f55d502. With it, all 45
+carries of R10-BODY-CONTRACT are marked, so the group is set done at that SHA. No new work.
+
+## P705: a cloud fixer cannot read the owed-red text its body is refused on
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Scope: tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py (the fixer and repair text it renders) and
+tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh (the arm that relays a stop back to the seat).
+Evidence: body_push.sh:128 runs tools/pr/ci_predict.py, which predicts red while a red check is
+still owed an answer (ci_predict.py:1409). A cloud seat has no gh, so it cannot read that check's
+failure text and cannot write the answer; the body stays refused. Hotfix #3487 stalled 45 minutes
+until a local seat repaired the body (sweep log 05:01Z). Carry 0 of the destination already makes a
+body_push refusal the same seat's to repair; this one it cannot repair without the text.
+Destination and severity: carry on R10-RELAY-NOBODY-STALL (not-started; owns cloud_relay.sh,
+cloud_dispatch.py and body_push.sh), normal. Figure against 20%: one occurrence, 45 minutes on a
+critical-path hotfix plus a local seat; cloud is the fixer majority, so every owed red on a cloud
+PR repeats it. Fix cost is small: the relay, which has gh, fetches the owed check's failure summary
+and hands it to the seat in the repair message (or the dispatch embeds it), so the benefit clears.
+Fix shape: when the predictor refusal names an owed red, the relay attaches that check run's name,
+conclusion and failure excerpt to the seat's next message. Control: a refusal with no owed red adds
+no text.
+
+## P706: carry_fold and the roster drain race on the roster push
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Scope: the roster branch's write path, tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py (push loop :1174) as used by
+the roster-drain beat job (tools/audit/seat/beat_jobs.py:339) and by tools/audit/seat/carry_fold.py.
+Evidence: both write through roster_edit.py --push and share no lock; carry_fold lost the push race
+3 times in 3 tries against a 21-op drain, and the hotfix #3487 body stalled 15 minutes until the
+drain was SIGSTOPped by hand (sweep log 05:17Z). A stopped drain that is not resumed halts every
+roster op, so the workaround carries its own risk.
+Destination and severity: carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 (not-started; owns beat_jobs.py and the
+roster-drain row), normal. Figure against 20%: one occurrence, 15 minutes on a critical-path body
+and a manual signal to the drain; it recurs whenever a fold lands during a long drain. Fix cost is
+small: the drain takes a lease in HPO_STATE_DIR per op and yields between ops while an out-of-queue
+writer holds it (or carry_fold enqueues at the head of the queue and waits for its line), so the
+benefit clears. The fixer chooses between the two by which keeps one writer of record; the lease
+touches roster_edit.py, which the fixer adds to the group's files.
+Control: a drain pass with no fold pending runs unchanged.

+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Scope: R10-STANDING-CONTRACTS-P2 carries 9, 12, 13 and 14, dismissed for round 10 by P708.
+Owner ruling (tvofi, in person, 2026-11-12 about 06:55Z), verbatim: "Plan them for round 11".
+Supersedes in P708: the refusal for round 10 stands (the merge and dispatch seats stay standing
+seats for this round), but it is no longer a bare refusal. P708's reason is to be read as
+"planned for round 11 by owner ruling 2026-11-12, see P709", and the work enters round 11's
+opening plan as one intake entry covering the four carries below.
+Evidence: the measured load from P708, since session s14 began (2026-11-11T01:02Z): 48 merges to
+main and 46 reviewer fires in the session. tools/audit/seat/beatd.jobs.json has no merge, train or
+reviewer-dispatch row.
+Destination and severity: one carry on R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL (not-started), normal. That group
+writes the "Round 11's opening plan carries" list in dev/audit/README.md, and it already holds the
+earlier owner round-11 intake ruling (batch 218 P668, R11-INTAKE-SCORECARD-PARAGRAPHS), so this
+uses the same destination and form. Figure against 20%: not argued here; the owner ordered the
+planning, and round 11's P3 sizes it against the bar. Size: L, design first under decision 0014
+(designer and design review before a fixer).
+Precondition, common to all four, stated by the carries themselves: the replacement beat job is
+live and has run one real cycle beside the seat (for the merge seat, one real pitch built and
+merged by the job with the merge seat watching and agreeing) before the seat is stopped; the work
+moves to a daemon or beat job, never into the orchestrator's turns.

+Carry 9 (merge seat into a pitch job; owner-ordered), its original text:

+> tvofi 2026-10-24 card 1 (owner accepted; CARDS.json (prestudy-mech, r10s6 scratch, not in the tree)): when this group lands, the standing merge seat retires: the queue builder and the train run as a daemon or beat job (train.sh and merge_train.py), their per-pitch outcome goes to the digest, and no pitch is assembled in the orchestrator's turn. Edit dev/governance/roles/standing-merge.md in this group or in R10-ORCH-BEATD's contract edit, whichever merges later, not both. Binding constraint (owner, tvofi 2026-10-24, verbatim): 'make sure the retirement of the standing seats dont cause you to run things inline'. A seat's work moves to a daemon or beat job, never into the orchestrator's turns, and the seat stays until its replacement job is live and verified. Acceptance: one real pitch is built and merged by the job, with the merge seat watching and agreeing; only then is the seat stopped.
+
+Carry 12 (dispatch half of standing-dispatch.md into a beat job; owner-ordered), its original text:
+

It never moves into the orchestrator's turns. The standing dispatch seat stays until that job has run beside it for one full cycle.

What it needs from here exists: one writer (`bus.sh dispatch`), a registry with time and model, a reopen on a failed publish. The standing dispatch seat stays until the job has run beside it for one full cycle.
+

Control: one beat pass over a handoff with no live dispatch leaves one registry line and one `close reviewer-fire` in `events.tsv`, and a second pass adds neither. Carry: R10-ORCH-BEATD
