+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 236
+
+Source: the orchestrator's request on R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 after its pull request #3470 merged to
+main at be86e36a560fde88cc758cefcee322b9087a5deb (2026-11-12). Carry indices are 0-based on the
+group at roster a15a842375; #3470's body numbers its carries from 1, so its "Carry 17" is index 16.
+Ruling recorded by triage s14-44.
+
+## P710: mark the carries #3470 built; leave the rest open
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Evidence: #3470's body answers carries 1-18 (1-based): "Carry 17: built here
+(TRAIN-POLICY-REASON-STALE-CONTEXT, `rollup_states`)" and "Carry 18: built here
+(TRAIN-UNDRAFT-EVERY-ROUTE, `record_drafts` and the `land` draft arm)"; carries 1-16 read "left
+for a later part; it stays on the roster". Carries 19-23 (indices 18-22) were appended after the
+brief was rendered and the body does not name them. Checked on origin/main: merge_train.py
+defines `rollup_states` and `Train.record_drafts`, and `_batch` calls `self.record_drafts(queue)`;
+be86e36a56 is an ancestor of origin/main.
+Ruling: mark index 16 and index 17 implemented at be86e36a56, each by --match on its key text.
+Nothing is dismissed. Indices 0-15 and 18-22 (21 carries) stay open and buildable, so the stage
+stays carries-open and no set-stage done is queued. The group is not idle: a next part owes them.
+Destination and severity: roster ops only, normal. Figure against 20%: not applicable (record).
+
+## P711: derive a merged part's carry marks from its body at the merge
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Problem: marking the carries a merged part built is nobody's step. roster_sync.py at a merge
+writes only the stage (carries-open while any carry is unmarked; its marks are read, never
+written); no tool on main reads a body's "Carry N: built here" lines, and no policy file names
+mark-carry as a step. R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 carry 25 (POSTMERGE-STAGE-VIA-DRAIN) queues the stage
+op on a refused sync, not marks a body declares.
+Cost seen: after #3470 merged, R10-TRAIN-RESIDUE-P2 read 23 of 23 carries unmarked, so the plan
+could not tell its two built carries from its 21 owed ones, and a fixer dispatched on it would
+have rebuilt `rollup_states` and `record_drafts`. 14 groups sit at carries-open on the roster
+now; each merged part among them carries the same exposure. The body's 1-based numbering against
+the roster's 0-based indices makes a by-number derivation wrong by one, so it must key on text.
+Ruling: at a merge, postmerge derives one `mark-carry <GROUP> --match <key> implemented <merge>`
+per body line "Carry N: built here (<KEY>, ...)" and a dismissed mark per "Carry N: dismissed
+(<reason>)", keying --match on the key text the body quotes, checked to hit exactly one carry of
+the group; a body line whose key hits zero or two carries is printed as OWED, never guessed by
+index. The ops go to roster-drain.queue as the stage op does.
+Destination: one carry on R10-TICK-RESIDUE-P3 (not-started; it owns postmerge.py and
+roster_sync.py and carry 25, the neighbouring stage-op derivation). Severity: normal. Basis: one
+observed instance with a measured near-miss dispatch; 20% bar not argued, the cost is a re-built
+part per merged group with carries left. Size: S-M.

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 238
+
+Source: owner rulings (tvofi, about 2026-11-12T07:35Z), recorded, not weighed (P714-P716); one

+Owner ruling, verbatim (typos his; "baikanfan"/"bankaifan" is the contributor Bankaifan; "love"
+reads "move"): "Implement a mechanism that allow baikanfans PRs to be accepted as is as long as
+they follow all our conventions and rules and have a valid merge verdict (the reviewer may also be
+run by bankaifan). Merges with main and codeowner approvals remain in our machinery even for such
+PRs. The difference from today is that baikanfan may run the fixer-reviewer cycles themselves.
+Also, for the rest of the round, non critical outside PRs can be folded into the plan of they do
+not love the programme closure eta. If they do, that are planned for round 11. It is critical the
+catalog pr and programme closure is ready 15/11 or sooner"

+## P714: outside-contributor fixer and review cycle (the mechanism)
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, first and second sentences. Destination: a new group,
+R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE, size L, lane IN, source outside, design first under decision 0014.
+Today a fork pull request is rebuilt by our fixer as an hpo-author pull request: pr-contract
+refuses any other author (0011), verdicts post only through bus.sh confirm as hpo-approver (0013),
+and tools/pr/app_approve.sh takes a verdict only from an allowlisted account. Wanted: an
+allowlisted contributor's fork pull request is admitted unchanged when every required check and the
+body contract pass at its head and a valid "Fix review: merge <head>" verdict exists for that head,
+which the contributor's own reviewer seat may produce; merge of main, code-owner approval, the
+train and the record stay ours. The brief lists what the design must decide. No after-edges; it
+shares tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py with R10-GATE-DEFER-BARRIER (critical path) and must not
+take it ahead of that group. Severity medium. Figure against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).
+
+## P715: the fold rule for outside work, rest of round 10
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, third and fourth sentences. Rule: for the rest of round 10 a
+non-critical outside request is planned into round 10 only if it does not move the programme
+closure ETA; if it does, it is planned for round 11. A critical one (a defect a user is hitting
+now) is exempt. Applied against plan-live.json generated 2026-11-12T07:27Z (closure
+2026-11-15T05:43Z); a group finishing after about 2026-11-14T12:00Z moves closure. Planned
+finishes: SUPPLY-MIN-RUN-PAUSE 11-13T22:29, LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P2 11-13T21:51, START-COUNTER-EDGES
+and MODE-BEFORE-SUPPLY-ON 11-14T04:49, RESTART-LEARNING-PR-B 11-14T05:53, PLANNER-PRICE
+11-14T06:02, DHW-START-HYSTERESIS 11-14T11:04 (round 10); DISINFECTION-STEP-NOTICE 11-14T18:23,
+LEARNER-ROBUSTNESS-P3 11-15T00:23, OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE unplanned, L with design (round 11).
+None sits on an after-edge path into R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL or closeout; none but P714's group
+shares a file with a critical-path group. Stage changes are the orchestrator's to order.
+A round-11 group is recorded as P709 did: an append-carry on R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL adding the
+item to dev/audit/README.md's round-11 opening plan carries, then set-stage <group> deferred.
+
+## P716: closure and the catalog pull request by 2026-11-15 outrank outside work
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the owner ruling above, last sentence. Programme closure and R10-CATALOG-PR are critical
+and must be ready by 2026-11-15; they outrank every non-critical outside group. R10-CATALOG-PR's
+after-edges (USER-DOCS-VERIFY, ARCH-DOCS, ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL, CLOSEOUT-CLEANUP, CLOSEOUT-PREP,
+ARCH-DOCS-DELTA) hold every closeout predecessor; no edge is missing, so no roster op. The plan
+puts it post-closure (start 11-15T07:43Z, finish 11-16T07:27Z), past the date: the orchestrator's.
+
+## P717: R10-HOTFIX-REPLAY-CLASS-CUT discharged by #3477
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Its one carry (0-based 0; #3477 body "Carry 1"), the RCA countermeasure, is built at merge

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 239
+
+Source: owner rulings (tvofi, 2026-11-12 about 07:50Z, 08:00Z and 08:10Z), recorded, not weighed
+(P718, P719). Ruling recorded by triage s14-64.
+
+Owner rulings, verbatim:
+- ~07:50Z: "The "may not move the programme closure later" ruling should also apply to groups that
+  are self-fed from the ongoing round 10"
+- ~08:00Z: "Good. It should also apply to any new such self fed groups"
+- ~08:10Z: "The contributur cycle mechanism should be built in full, asap"
+
+## P718: the closure rule extends to self-fed groups, existing and new
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the 07:50Z and 08:00Z rulings above, extending batch 238 P715 (outside work) to work round
+10 feeds itself: residue parts, HOTFIX groups not fixing a red main, FLY and SEAT groups, and
+instruments grown by triage ACCEPTs, both those already on the roster and any appended from now on.
+Rule for the rest of round 10: such a group stays in round 10 only if the critical path or closeout
+needs it, or it is small and finishes without moving the programme closure (plan-live finish at or
+before about 2026-11-14T12:00Z); otherwise it is planned for round 11. Standing rule for this seat:
+every ACCEPT that would append a group or a carry gets that closure test at ruling time, and the
+entry says which; a round-11 outcome is recorded the P709 way (append-carry on
+R10-ROUND-PLAYBOOK-FINAL citing the ACCEPT, and a new group at stage deferred). Existing groups:
+the stage changes are the orchestrator's to order, from the self-fed table measured by s14-63; this
+entry queues no roster op. Exempt: R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE (P719). Closure and R10-CATALOG-PR
+by 2026-11-15 still outrank all non-critical work (P716). Severity high (closure date). Figure
+against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).
+
+## P719: R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE is round 10, in full, top priority above the cap
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Basis: the 08:10Z ruling above. The group (appended by P714, source outside) is round 10 by owner
+order: its design and every build part run in round 10, no part deferred, exempt from P715 and
+P718; it is dispatched at top priority above the open-PR cap. This supersedes the earlier note that
+the build's round is decided at design approval. Plan check, one read of origin/main: replan.py
+dispatch_tier returns TIER_TOP for roster_lib.is_outside (source "outside", set at 4721), and
+roster_lib.dispatch_rank returns RANK_TOP for it, so the tier needs nothing more. The plan's own
+cap exemption (scheduler pick with cap_exempt) keys on the computed critical path only; this group
+has no after-edges and is not on it, so the plan models it as a top-tier peer of the critical path
+inside the slot count, not above it. No roster field expresses "above the cap"; the cap that binds
+dispatch is the orchestrator's open-PR cap, so above-the-cap is the orchestrator's dispatch act,
+and no roster op is queued. The group's L size plus design is unmovable slot load in the date
+analysis. Severity high (owner order). Figure against 20%: not applicable (owner ruling).

+# Proposal triage, session s14, batch 245
+
+Source: orchestrator order of 2026-11-12 to triage seat s14-72 (three proposals). Standing owner
+rulings applied: the closure test on every ACCEPT (P718); R10-OUTSIDE-CONTRIBUTOR-CYCLE and outside
+work first (P719); owner-approved study decisions built now when they do not move closure (P734).
+
+## P739: open_pr.sh re-renders a body's figure blocks at the head it pushes
+
+Verdict: ACCEPT
+Source: seat s14-69's defect note and local patch (s14-69/NOTE.md and
+s14-69/open_pr-figure-refresh.diff, uncommitted, against origin/main).
+Instances: `tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh` writes the PR body once from handoff-body/<topic>:BODY.md
+and never runs `tools/pr/figure_block.py refresh`. A figure block names the head it was rendered
+at, so pr-body lint refuses p1 after a main merge and always refuses p2, whose row commit moves the
+head. Seen on R10-OUTSIDE-DISINFECTION-SETPOINT part 2: the opener was refused twice and PR #3495
+was opened and auto-closed after its p2 refusal (s14-69/NOTE.md). `open_pr.sh --self-test` runs
+only delivery_row.sh's and pr_args.sh's self-tests, so no case covers the p1/p2 body path: it
+passed before and after the patch (s14-69/NOTE.md).
+Cost: one S fixer part, about 25 changed lines in open_pr.sh (s14-69 diff: 2 hunks, 7 added
+lines) plus a self-test case. A body with a figure block then runs the full prepr at p2 instead of
+the row-only skip (the refreshed body differs past the `## Head` note); a body without a block
+keeps the skip. No capped file named; the fixer reports structure.py and `--budgets` rows.
+Binding: an outside product group's PR cannot open while its body carries a figure block; outside
+work outranks all else (P719).
+Destination: new group R10-HOTFIX-OPENPR-FIGURE-REFRESH, class hotfix, kind instrument, size S,
+severity high, sonnet fixer, opus reviewer, files tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh, after none. Overlap
+on open_pr.sh with R10-SEAT-SCRIPT-OUTPUT (in-progress, PR #3490) is admitted by seam: this group
+touches only the p1/p2 body-render points. Build: (1) refresh before p1 when the merged head
+differs from the code head, refusing with nothing pushed on failure; (2) refresh before p2 at the
+row head, always, closing the PR with the reason on failure; (3) a self-test case with a figure
+block in the body. Null control (s14-69/NOTE.md): a figure-block body opens with p1, p2 and the row;
+the mutant without the p2 refresh is refused at p2 with "figure-block scope-line names another
+head"; a body with no block still prints `ROW-ONLY: prepr SKIPPED`. (4) the rerun hazard the same
+open hit: a closed-after-p2 open leaves branch fix/<topic>-pr and a detached worktree that make
+the next `git worktree add -b` fail; the re-run removes or reuses them. Keeping row-only for a
+figure-block-only re-render is optional, not owed.
+Closure: needed by an outside group's opener (DISINFECTION-SETPOINT part 2), so it is on the
+outside path and enters round 10; size S on a non-binding lane. Not measured by replan; main runs
+the replan on dispatch if it wants a number. Machinery bar: severity high skips the 10% keep bar.
+Figure against 20%: not applicable (defect repair).
+

+yet — not a zero.* marks a part with nothing to grade. Hovering a row repeats

+share of the hour's total push in percent; hovering a line explains the
+reason. The plan weighs the whole day's hours together, so the heat pump can
+still do the opposite of the strongest push this hour. *No data* means the
+optimizer has no plan for this hour yet, before the first solve or while the
+price forecast is missing.

@@ -939,6 +939,26 @@ duration plus an hour's margin before the stated return, and the estimate is

+A change of the away indicator, the away switch or the holiday calendar
+replans at once, not at the next optimization interval.
+
+**Away and the mold guard.** With *Keep cold surfaces below mold humidity* on,
+the room is never planned below the mold-safe temperature, and that floor
+outranks the away setback by design: protecting the coldest surface comes
+before saving. The mold-safe temperature rises with indoor humidity and falls
+with outdoor temperature. The floor the plan holds is that temperature capped
+at your comfort target: the guard never heats past the target, because drying
+a house further is a dehumidifier's job. In a humid house in cold weather the
+floor can therefore sit at or near the target itself. On one recorded install,
+at 52–53 % indoor humidity and 1 to 5 °C outdoors, the mold-safe temperature
+worked out at 19.2 to 20.9 °C; with a 19.5 °C comfort target the floor in force
+was 19.2 to 19.5 °C, and the plan heats to it while you are away. The setback
+to *Temperature while away* then saves little or no space-heating energy for as
+long as the guard holds the floor above it. Hot water still drops to its away
+minimum. The setback saves again once the house is dry enough, or mild
+enough, that the mold-safe temperature falls below the away temperature; the
+**Mold Floor Breach** sensor's `floor_c` attribute shows the floor in force.

 ### COP, and the tracking-error gate
 
 With a power meter, COP becomes observable instead of derived from a nameplate
 figure and a temperature curve. The learned `cop_scale` multiplies the nameplate
 curve, bounded to [0.5, 1.6] so a mis-scaled power entity cannot destroy the
-model. A sample only counts if the pump is genuinely running (below a third of
-nameplate the reading is mostly auxiliaries), and samples are skipped while the
-immersion element is drawing, because a resistive kW is a different appliance on
-the same meter.
+model. A sample only counts if the pump is genuinely running: the draw and the
+plan's ask must both reach 80 % of the configured minimum power (with no minimum
+configured, 30 % of the maximum), and never less than 0.2 kW, because below that
+the reading is mostly auxiliaries. Samples are skipped while the immersion
+element is drawing, because a resistive kW is a different appliance on the same
+meter.
+
+**Measured COP, and the model's COP.** A COP is *measured* only where both sides
+are meters: a heat energy meter or a thermal power meter for the heat, and a
+power or energy meter for the electricity, neither of them the pump's own
+estimate (the *meter or estimate* settings on the metering page), and, for an
+interval that heated hot water, a heat reading declared to see the hot-water
+circuit. Only a measured COP is recorded and graded. Every other install still
+trains `cop_scale`, from the vendor's estimate or from the commanded-versus-
+measured power ratio below, but its efficiency is the model's own, and the
+Health page says so: *COP cannot be measured on this install*, with what it
+lacks.
+
+**Efficiency at part load.** *Heat pump COP loss at max power* (default 0, off)
+lowers the COP linearly from the minimum to the maximum power, to one minus the
+setting at max power, because larger heat flows need larger temperature
+differences across the heat exchangers. The plan then prices each step at its own
+draw, so a kWh of heat bought at high power costs more than one bought near
+the minimum. A value
+at or above *band / (band + max power)*, band being max minus min power, would
+make more power buy less heat; the setting is then ignored and treated as 0.

+  check("collapse: the folds sit after the savings figure and before the chart",
+    iSave >= 0 && iSave < iNarr && iNarr < iWhy && iWhy < iChart, `${iSave} ${iNarr} ${iWhy} ${iChart}`);
+  // The two stylesheet rules the polish states: a divider under the last fold,
+  // and a summary that wraps rather than ellipsises.
+  const sumRule = (shut.match(/\.hl-fold-sum\s*\{[^}]*\}/) || [""])[0];
+  check("collapse: a rule under the last fold closes the headline off from the chart",
+    /\.hl-fold:last-child\s*\{\s*border-bottom:\s*1px solid/.test(shut));
+  check("collapse: the fold summary wraps and never ellipsises",
+    /overflow-wrap:\s*anywhere/.test(sumRule) && !/nowrap|text-overflow|overflow:\s*hidden/.test(sumRule), sumRule);
+  // The folded card draws what the dialog's chips last saved: hiding a series
+  // in the dialog hides it on the card, and on a card built afterwards.
+  const cv = build(states({ items, lines }, why));
+  const priceOn = (c) => (collect(c.shadowRoot).join("\n").match(/data-key="price"/g) || []).length;
+  // Earlier checks share the saved legend state, so the starting visibility is
+  // read, not assumed; the check holds for whichever way the chip flips it.
+  const hidBefore = !!cv.legend.hidden.price, shownBefore = priceOn(cv);
+  cv.dialog.open();
+  const chipPrice = { currentTarget: { getAttribute: (k) => (k === "data-key" ? "price" : null) } };
+  cv.legend.onChipClick(chipPrice);
+  cv.dialog.close();
+  const hidAfter = !!cv.legend.hidden.price;
+  const shownAfter = priceOn(cv), shownFresh = priceOn(build(states({ items, lines }, why)));
+  const drawn = (n, hid) => (hid ? n === 0 : n > 0);
+  check("collapse: the folded card keeps the visibility the dialog's chips last saved",
+    hidAfter !== hidBefore && drawn(shownBefore, hidBefore) && drawn(shownAfter, hidAfter) && drawn(shownFresh, hidAfter),
+    `hidden ${hidBefore} -> ${hidAfter}; drawn ${shownBefore} -> ${shownAfter}, fresh card ${shownFresh}`);
+  cv.legend.onChipClick(chipPrice); // the saved state as the earlier checks left it
+  // A fold's summary when the rows cannot be totalled: the first published line.
+  const raw = collect(build(states({ lines }, undefined)).shadowRoot).join("\n");
+  check("collapse: unpaired lines summarise as the first line; no why_now as the no-data line",
+    /data-fold="narrative"[^>]*>[\s\S]*?hl-fold-sum">pre-heating 4\.0 kWh before colder weather \(1\.22 SEK\)</.test(raw)
+    && /data-fold="whynow"[^>]*>[\s\S]*?hl-fold-sum">No data</.test(raw));
+  // Chips and the dashed-line notes: the dialog only.
+  const plain = build(states({ items, lines }, why));
+  const closedDump = collect(plain.shadowRoot).join("\n");
+  check("collapse: the folded card renders no series chip and no legend",
+    !/class="chip/.test(closedDump) && !/class="legend"/.test(closedDump) && !/class="legend-note"/.test(closedDump));
+  plain._onCardClick({});
+  const dlg = (collect(plain.shadowRoot).join("\n").match(/<dialog[\s\S]*$/) || [""])[0];
+  check("collapse: the expanded dialog carries the chips and the legend",
+    /class="legend"/.test(dlg) && (dlg.match(/class="chip/g) || []).length >= 3);
+  // Every new string in every card language.
+  const foldKeys = (lang) => Object.keys(fn(`STRINGS.${lang}`)).filter((k) => k.startsWith("fold.")).sort();
+  check("collapse: every fold string has its twin in en, sv and de",
+    foldKeys("en").length >= 3 && ["sv", "de"].every((l) => JSON.stringify(foldKeys(l)) === JSON.stringify(foldKeys("en"))),
+    ["en", "sv", "de"].map((l) => `${l}: ${foldKeys(l)}`).join(" | "));
+  const sv = new Card();
+  sv.setConfig({ type: "custom:heatpump-optimizer-card" });
+  sv.hass = { states: states({ items, lines }, why, "sv"), language: "sv-SE" };
+  const svDump = collect(sv.shadowRoot).join("\n");
+  check("collapse: the headers speak the card language",
+    svDump.includes(fn("STRINGS.sv")["fold.narrative_title"]) && svDump.includes("Varför nu") && /totalt/.test(svDump));
+  build(mkStates(DEFAULT_SPACE, DEFAULT_DHW, true)); // back to English
+}
+
 console.log(fails ? `\n${fails} CARD CHECK(S) FAILED` : "\nALL CARD CHECKS PASSED");
 process.exit(fails?1:0);

+_THEME_STUB = """
+const saved = process.argv[1] === "none" ? null : process.argv[1];
+const src = {media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)", dataset: {}};
+const btn = {setAttribute() {}, addEventListener() {}};
+globalThis.document = {documentElement: {dataset: {}}, getElementById: () => btn,
+  querySelector: () => null, querySelectorAll: (q) => (q.includes("source") ? [src] : [])};
+globalThis.localStorage = {getItem: () => saved, setItem() {}};
+globalThis.matchMedia = () => ({matches: false});
+"""
+
+
+def theme_picture_media(html: str, saved: str | None) -> str | None:
+    """The `media` a built page's theme script leaves on a dark `<picture>` source, with `saved` in localStorage
+    (`hpo-theme`) and a light OS: the script run in node over a stub DOM. None when the page has no theme script."""
+    m = re.search(r"<script>(\(\(\)=>\{const r=document\.documentElement.*?)</script>", html, re.S)
+    if not m:
+        return None
+    js = _THEME_STUB + m.group(1) + "\nprocess.stdout.write(src.media);"
+    r = subprocess.run(["node", "-e", js, saved or "none"], capture_output=True, text=True)
+    return r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else f"node rc {r.returncode}: {r.stderr.strip()[:120]}"
+
+
+def check_theme_pictures(built: dict) -> None:
+    """A diagram's <picture> picks its dark render by <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">, the OS
+    preference; the site's own theme toggle must pick the same render, or a light picture sits on a dark page
+    (R10-USER-DOCS-VERIFY, carry from #3014). Null control: with no saved theme the OS query stands."""
+    html = next(iter(built.get("html", {}).values()), "")
+    got = {s: theme_picture_media(html, s) for s in ("light", "dark", None)}
+    R.check("the docs pages' theme toggle turns a dark <picture> source off on a light site theme",
+            got["light"] == "not all", repr(got))
+    R.check("... and on for a dark site theme on a light OS", got["dark"] == "all", repr(got))
+    R.check("null control: with no saved theme the source keeps its prefers-color-scheme query",
+            got[None] == "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)", repr(got))
+
+
 def check_docs_build_controls() -> None:
     """Null controls for docs_build itself: a planted tree turns the arm's core red, and a missing build or tree is red."""
     R.section("docs build arm fires on a planted tree (R9-WEB-3 null controls)")

+# The off rule reaches the MQTT arm (owner ruling under mandate 6715477401,
+# 2026-11-11): no actuator arm leaves the pump displaced. What stands on each
+# ECL110 topic -- its last publish, retained or not -- is displace 0 after
+# MODE_OFF and after unload, through the same restore hook as the entity arm.
+import json as _gm_json  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def _gm_standing(coord):
+    """Each topic's last displace and retain flag; the entity arm's last write."""
+    stand = {}
+    for dom, svc, d in coord.hass.services.calls:
+        if dom == "mqtt":
+            body = d["payload"] if d["topic"] == "ecl/set" else _gm_json.loads(d["payload"])["command"]["displace"]
+            stand[d["topic"]] = (int(body), d["retain"])
+        elif svc == "set_value":
+            stand["entity"] = d["value"]
+    return stand
+
+
+_gm = {}
+for _gm_retain in (False, True):
+    for _gm_path in ("mode_off", "unload"):
+        _gmc = _ghc_coord(entry_id=f"ghc_mqtt_{_gm_retain}_{_gm_path}", ecl110_displace_set_topic="ecl/set",
+                          ecl110_command_topic="ecl/cmd", ecl110_mqtt_retain=_gm_retain)
+        _ghc_pub(_gmc, -3.0)
+        if _gm_path == "mode_off":
+            _asyncio.run(_gmc.async_set_mode(_ghc_off, refresh=False))

+def _gm_cycle(late):
+    """(the switch writes, the legacy payload's heat_pump_on) of one _apply_action."""
+    coord = _ghc_coord(entity=None, entry_id=f"ghc_mqtt_cycle_{late}", ecl110_command_topic="ecl/cmd")
+    coord._mode = _gm_comfort
+    coord._current_action = {"mode": "comfort", "heat_pump_on": False, "displace_value": 2.0}
+    switch = []
+
+    async def _record(on):
+        switch.append(on)
+
+    coord._write_supply = _record
+    real = _gm_arb.cycle_supply
+    if late:
+        _gm_arb.cycle_supply = lambda _inp, _boosts, on, now=None: not on
+    try:
+        _asyncio.run(coord._apply_action())
+    finally:

+    return switch, [_gm_json.loads(p)["command"]["heat_pump_on"] for _, p in _ghc_mqtt(coord)]

+    _bt_returns == ["'external_heat_source'", "signals.freeze_reason", "'defrosting'",
+                    "f'{reading.problem}:{key}'", "'ventilation'", "boost.FREEZE_REASON",
+                    "_tail_freeze(self)"],
+    f"{_bt_returns}",
+)
+
+# Fix review (blocked 594238bf), X1: a press in the tail's last two hours keeps
+# the overlay live past the tail's end, and the sum is not cleared while it is
+# live, so that press adds to it. Null control: ``_bt_after`` above, the same
+# press after the tail ran out, sums only itself.
+_bt_x1, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)] * 3)
+_bt_x1_tail = _bt_x1.space_settle_until
+_bt_x1.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, _bt_x1_tail - timedelta(hours=1))
+_bt_x1.expire(_bt_x1_tail + timedelta(minutes=30))
+_bt_x1_mid = (_bt_x1.space_settle_until, _bt_x1.space_boosted)
+_bt_x1.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, False, _bt_x1_tail + timedelta(minutes=50))
+# X2: the same over the mode surface, a mode held past an earlier overlay's tail.
+_bt_x2 = boost_mod.BoostState()
+_bt_x2.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, NOW)
+_bt_x2.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, False, NOW + _bt_20)
+_bt_x2.note_mode(True, NOW + timedelta(minutes=21))
+_bt_x2.expire(NOW + timedelta(hours=13))
+_bt_x2.note_mode(False, NOW + timedelta(hours=14))
+R.check(
+    "the boosted sum is not cleared while an overlay or the mode is live past an earlier "
+    "boost's tail, so the live boost adds to it, over both surfaces",
+    _bt_x1_mid == (_bt_x1_tail, 3 * _bt_20)
+    and _bt_x1.space_boosted == 3 * _bt_20 + timedelta(minutes=110)
+    and _bt_x1.space_settle_until == _bt_x1_tail + timedelta(minutes=50) + boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL
+    and _bt_x2.space_boosted == _bt_20 + timedelta(hours=14) - timedelta(minutes=21)
+    and _bt_x2.space_settle_until == NOW + timedelta(hours=14) + boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL,
+    f"{_bt_x1_mid} {_bt_x1} {_bt_x2}",
+)
+
+# X3: a press that finds the overlay live extends it and keeps its start, so the
+# sum counts the whole boost. X13: entering the mode clears a spent sum, as a
+# press does. Null control: a single press sums its own length (``_bt_one``).
+_bt_x3 = boost_mod.BoostState()
+_bt_x3.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, NOW)
+_bt_x3.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, NOW + timedelta(hours=1))
+_bt_x3.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, False, NOW + timedelta(hours=2))
+_bt_x13, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)] * 3)
+_bt_x13_spent = _bt_x13.space_settle_until
+_bt_x13.note_mode(True, _bt_x13_spent + timedelta(hours=1))
+_bt_x13.note_mode(False, _bt_x13_spent + timedelta(hours=1, minutes=30))
+R.check(
+    "an extended overlay sums from its first press; the mode entered after a spent tail "
+    "sums only itself",
+    _bt_x3.space_boosted == timedelta(hours=2) and _bt_x3.space_since == NOW
+    and _bt_x13.space_boosted == timedelta(minutes=30),
+    f"{_bt_x3} {_bt_x13}",
+)
+
+# X7: ``settle`` never shortens a running tail (an end stamped before a clock
+# step back); a later end lengthens it, even by half a second (null control).
+_bt_x7 = boost_mod.BoostState(space_settle_until=NOW + boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL)
+_bt_x7.settle(NOW - timedelta(hours=1), NOW - timedelta(hours=2))
+_bt_x7_kept = _bt_x7.space_settle_until
+_bt_x7.settle(NOW + timedelta(milliseconds=500), NOW)
+R.check(
+    "a settle ending before the running tail's end leaves it; one ending later moves it",
+    _bt_x7_kept == NOW + boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL
+    and _bt_x7.space_settle_until == NOW + timedelta(milliseconds=500) + boost_mod.SPACE_SETTLE_TAIL,
+    f"{_bt_x7_kept} {_bt_x7}",
+)
+
+# X11: the store does not hold ``boosted_h`` to its domain on load, so the
+# restore does: a negative, NaN or infinite sum is unknown; zero and a sum under
+# one hour restore as stored (null controls).
+def _bt_hours(raw):
+    st = boost_mod.BoostState()
+    boost_mod._restore_settle(st, {"space_settle": {"until": (NOW + timedelta(hours=7)).isoformat(),
+                                                    "boosted_h": raw}}, NOW)
+    return st.space_boosted
+
+
+R.check(
+    "a restored boosted sum outside [0, inf) is unknown; 0 and 0.5 h restore as stored",
+    [_bt_hours(h) for h in (-1.0, float("nan"), float("inf"), True, 0.0, 0.5)]
+    == [None, None, None, None, timedelta(0), timedelta(minutes=30)],
+    f"{[_bt_hours(h) for h in (-1.0, float('nan'), float('inf'), True, 0.0, 0.5)]}",
+)
+
+# X4 and X5: the two saves of a tail. Leaving the boost mode saves the tail it
+# starts (``note_mode_change``); a cycle whose expiry starts a tail saves it
+# (``apply``). Null controls: entering the mode, a change between two other
+# modes and a cycle that changes nothing schedule no save.
+_bt_saved = []
+_bt_sched = boost_mod._schedule_persist
+boost_mod._schedule_persist = _bt_saved.append
+try:
+    _bt_mc = _BtCoord()
+    boost_mod.note_mode_change(_bt_mc, _fb_const.MODE_AUTO, boost_mod.MODE_BOOST, NOW)
+    _bt_enter = list(_bt_saved)
+    boost_mod.note_mode_change(_bt_mc, _fb_const.MODE_AUTO, _fb_const.MODE_ECONOMY, NOW)
+    _bt_other = list(_bt_saved)
+    boost_mod.note_mode_change(_bt_mc, boost_mod.MODE_BOOST, _fb_const.MODE_AUTO, NOW + timedelta(hours=1))
+    _bt_left = list(_bt_saved)
+    _bt_left_payload = boost_mod._store_payload(boost_mod.held_for(_bt_mc))
+    _bt_saved.clear()
+    _bt_ac = _BlockFloorCoord(None)
+    _bt_ac_now = dt_util.now()
+    boost_mod.held_for(_bt_ac).set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, _bt_ac_now - timedelta(hours=3))
+    boost_mod.apply(_bt_ac, boost_mod.BoostOverlay(6.0, 24.0, 8.0))

+    _bt_cycle_payload = boost_mod._store_payload(boost_mod.held_for(_bt_ac))
+    boost_mod.apply(_bt_ac, boost_mod.BoostOverlay(6.0, 24.0, 8.0))

+    and _bt_cycle == [_bt_ac] and _bt_quiet == []
+    and _bt_cycle_payload.get("space_settle", {}).get("boosted_h") == 2.0,
+    f"{_bt_enter} {_bt_other} {_bt_left} {_bt_left_payload} {_bt_cycle} {_bt_quiet} {_bt_cycle_payload}",
+)
+
+# The fixer's own pass over every added line: the tail runs out at its own
+# instant, not a second either side (a press at the instant sums only itself, a
+# press half a second before adds to the series); a spent tail is cleared by the
+# expiry itself, so a quiet install stores main's payload again; a press that
+# finds the tail spent clears the sum without an expiry first; leaving the mode
+# frees the sum to clear.
+_bt_at, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)] * 3)
+_bt_at.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, _bt_at.space_settle_until)
+_bt_before, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)] * 3)
+_bt_before.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, _bt_before.space_settle_until - timedelta(milliseconds=500))
+_bt_before.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, False, _bt_before.space_settle_until + timedelta(minutes=10))
+_bt_quiet_st, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)])
+_bt_quiet_st.expire(_bt_quiet_st.space_settle_until + timedelta(minutes=1))
+_bt_noexp, _ = _bt_series([("space", _bt_20)] * 3)
+_bt_noexp_at = _bt_noexp.space_settle_until + timedelta(minutes=1)
+_bt_noexp.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, True, _bt_noexp_at)
+_bt_noexp.set(boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE, False, _bt_noexp_at + _bt_20)

+_bt_modeleft.expire(_bt_modeleft.space_settle_until + timedelta(minutes=1))
+R.check(
+    "the tail runs out at its own instant; a spent tail clears on expiry and a quiet install "
+    "stores main's payload; a press after a spent tail sums only itself; a left mode lets "
+    "its sum clear",
+    _bt_at.space_boosted == timedelta(0)
+    and _bt_before.space_boosted == 3 * _bt_20 + timedelta(minutes=10, milliseconds=500)
+    and (_bt_quiet_st.space_settle_until, _bt_quiet_st.space_boosted) == (None, timedelta(0))
+    and boost_mod._store_payload(_bt_quiet_st) == {}
+    and _bt_noexp.space_boosted == _bt_20
+    and (_bt_modeleft.mode_since, _bt_modeleft.space_settle_until) == (None, None),
+    f"{_bt_at} {_bt_before} {_bt_quiet_st} {_bt_noexp} {_bt_modeleft}",
+)
+
+# Restore at the boundaries: a tail ending at the restart's instant is spent,
+# and an overlay that ended more than a tail before the restart owes nothing.
+# Null control: ``_bt_down`` above, ended an hour before, owes its tail.
+_bt_r_now = boost_mod.BoostState()
+boost_mod._restore_settle(_bt_r_now, {"space_settle": {"until": NOW.isoformat(), "boosted_h": 1.0}}, NOW)
+_bt_r_old = boost_mod.BoostState()
+boost_mod._restore_settle(_bt_r_old, {"space": {"until": (NOW - timedelta(hours=13)).isoformat(),
+                                                "since": (NOW - timedelta(hours=14)).isoformat()}}, NOW)
+R.check(
+    "a restored tail ending now is spent; an overlay ended over a tail before the restart owes none",
+    (_bt_r_now.space_settle_until, _bt_r_now.space_boosted) == (None, timedelta(0))
+    and (_bt_r_old.space_settle_until, _bt_r_old.space_boosted) == (None, timedelta(0)),
+    f"{_bt_r_now} {_bt_r_old}",
+)
+
+# ``persist`` saves ``_store_payload`` through the boost store's own key and
+# version. Null control: the payload saved is the one a quiet state builds.
+_bt_saves = []
+
+
+class _BtSaveStore:
+    def __init__(self, real):
+        self.real = real
+
+    async def async_save(self, data):
+        _bt_saves.append((self.real._key, self.real._version, data))
+
+
+_bt_pc = _BtCoord()
+_bt_pc.hass, _bt_pc.entry = FakeHass(), type("_BtEntry", (), {"entry_id": "bt"})()
+boost_mod.held_for(_bt_pc).settle(NOW, NOW - _bt_20)
+_bt_real_store = boost_mod._store
+boost_mod._store = lambda c: _BtSaveStore(_bt_real_store(c))
+try:
+    _bt_asyncio.run(boost_mod.persist(_bt_pc))
+finally:
+    boost_mod._store = _bt_real_store
+R.check(
+    "persist saves the store payload under the boost store's key and version",
+    _bt_saves == [(f"{boost_mod.DOMAIN}_bt_boost", boost_mod.BOOST_STORE_VERSION,
+                   boost_mod._store_payload(boost_mod.held_for(_bt_pc)))]
+    and "space_settle" in _bt_saves[0][2],
+    f"{_bt_saves}",
+)
+
+# The coordinator's mode change reaches ``note_mode_change``: leaving the boost
+# mode through ``async_set_mode`` starts the tail and sums the mode's time.
+# Null control: entering it starts no tail.
+_bt_cc = _sr_coord()
+_bt_asyncio.run(_bt_cc.async_set_mode(boost_mod.MODE_BOOST, refresh=False))
+_bt_cc_in = (boost_mod.held_for(_bt_cc).mode_since is not None, boost_mod.held_for(_bt_cc).space_settle_until)
+_bt_asyncio.run(_bt_cc.async_set_mode(_fb_const.MODE_AUTO, refresh=False))
+_bt_cc_held = boost_mod.held_for(_bt_cc)
+R.check(
+    "async_set_mode into the boost mode marks its start, and out of it starts the tail",
+    _bt_cc_in == (True, None)
+    and _bt_cc_held.mode_since is None and _bt_cc_held.space_settle_until is not None
+    and _bt_cc_held.space_boosted is not None,
+    f"{_bt_cc_in} {_bt_cc_held}",
+)

+# #3420 part E (Bankaifan): a switch-on writes the step's mode first. A pass
+# writes nothing while the switch reads off, so the mode followed the
+# switch-on by up to a tick and a Luxtronik started in the last duty. The
+# cycle and the step tick both switch through ``write_supply``. Each null
+# control is the same run with ``_lead_mode`` replaced by a no-op (today's
+# order): where the lead owes nothing, the service calls and their order are
+# identical; where it owes the mode, the no-op run has no mode before the switch.
+from heatpump_optimizer import duty_switch as _mb_ds
+from dataclasses import replace as _mb_replace

+
+async def _mb_run(lead=True, duty="control", mode_entity=True, switch="off", via="cycle",
+                  select="Heating", fail=False, cut=False, optimizer="auto", space=False,
+                  disinfect=False, since=-60, after=0):
+    """Ordered (domain, service) calls of one switch write, through the real coordinator.
+
+    The plan is "-d": idle at 05:45, hot water only at 06:00 (``space``:
+    heating only, which a cut-off holds and hot water is exempt from). ``via`` cycle
+    runs ``_apply_action`` at 06:00; tick runs the cycle at 05:45 (OFF) and
+    the step tick at 06:00; direct calls ``write_supply(..., True)`` alone at
+    06:00 with the optimizer in ``optimizer`` (``released``: auto, the
+    entry unloaded). ``cut``: an early cut-off at
+    05:58 holds the switch-on (MIN_OFF). Also returns the contexts the
+    learner was told of, and the options the select was sent. ``disinfect``:
+    the pass reads a held disinfection. ``since``: minutes from 06:00 at which
+    the switch took its state (an hour back by default, so no minimum run or
+    pause holds the write; -2 holds a switch-on until 06:08). ``after``: the
+    step ticks then fire each minute to 06:00 + ``after``, and a fifth value
+    maps each such minute to its ordered calls.
+    """
+    ticks, told = [], []
+    armed, noted, owed = _sa_pa.async_track_time_interval, _mb_ds.note_mode_write, _sa_pa._lead_mode
+    _sa_pa.async_track_time_interval = lambda _h, fn, _i: (ticks.append(fn), (lambda: None))[1]
+    _mb_ds.note_mode_write = lambda rec, when, old, new, ctx: (told.append((rec, ctx)), noted(rec, when, old, new, ctx))
+    if not lead:
+        async def _none(_coord, _on):
+            return None
+        _sa_pa._lead_mode = _none
+    hass = FakeHass({
+        "switch.hp": FakeState(switch, last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=since)),
+        "select.pump_mode": FakeState(select, attributes={"options": list(_PA_TUYA)}),
+    })
+    if fail:

+    if mode_entity:

+    coord = Coord(hass, FakeEntry(data=data, entry_id=f"mb{next(_PA_IDS)}"))  # a fresh store each run
+    coord._mode = "auto"

+    t0 = _SA_T0 - timedelta(minutes=15)

+        timestamps=[t0, _SA_T0], power_schedule=[0.0, 1.5 if space else 0.0],
+        dhw_power_schedule=[0.0, 0.0 if space else 2.0],
+        optimal_setpoints=[21.0, 21.0],
+    )
+    try:
+        if via == "tick":
+            _sa_dt.freeze(t0)
+            coord._last_optimization = t0
+            _sa_boost.adopt_plan(coord, {"heat_pump_on": False, "power": 0.0})
+            await coord._apply_action()
+            hass.states.set("switch.hp", FakeState(switch, last_updated=t0))
+        hass.services.calls.clear()
+        _sa_dt.freeze(_SA_T0)
+        if cut:
+            _sa_ec.state_for(coord).cut_at = _SA_T0 - timedelta(minutes=2)
+        if via == "direct":
+            coord._mode = "auto" if optimizer == "released" else optimizer
+            coord._entry_released = optimizer == "released"
+            await _sa_pa.write_supply(coord, "switch.hp", True)
+        elif via == "tick":

+        else:
+            coord._last_optimization = _SA_T0
+            _sa_boost.adopt_plan(coord, {"heat_pump_on": True, "power": 2.0})
+            await coord._apply_action()
+        calls = [(d, s) for d, s, _d in hass.services.calls if d in ("select", "switch")]
+        options = [data["option"] for d, _s, data in hass.services.calls if d == "select"]
+        later = {}

+R.check(
+    "a cycle switch-on an early cut-off holds writes no mode ahead of the switch it holds back",
+    _mb_cut == [("switch", "turn_off")],
+    f"{_mb_cut}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: the same heating step with no cut on record writes the mode, then the switch",
+    _mb_uncut == [("select", "select_option"), ("switch", "turn_on")],
+    f"{_mb_uncut}",
+)
+# The same rows with the minimum pause engaged (``supply_hold.hold_supply``,
+# the switch off since 05:58): the hold sits ahead of ``write_supply`` in
+# ``_write_supply``, so a held switch-on writes no mode, and the step tick's
+# retry runs through the same gate, so the switch-on that lands at 06:08
+# writes the mode immediately before the switch, on that tick and no other.
+_mb_cut_held = _asyncio.run(_mb_run(cut=True, space=True, since=-2))[0]
+_mb_held = _asyncio.run(_mb_run(space=True, since=-2, after=12))
+R.check(
+    "with the minimum pause engaged too, a cycle switch-on an early cut-off holds writes no mode ahead of the switch it holds back",
+    _mb_cut_held == [("switch", "turn_off")],
+    f"{_mb_cut_held}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "a cycle switch-on the minimum pause holds back writes no mode and no switch",
+    _mb_held[0] == [],
+    f"{_mb_held[0]}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "a switch-on held on one tick and landing on a later one writes the mode immediately before the switch on that later tick",
+    {m: c for m, c in _mb_held[4].items() if c} == {8: [("select", "select_option"), ("switch", "turn_on")]},
+    f"{_mb_held[4]}",
+)
+_mb_direct = {
+    (sw, opt): _asyncio.run(_mb_run(via="direct", switch=sw, optimizer=opt))[0]
+    for sw, opt in (("off", "auto"), ("on", "auto"), ("off", "off"), ("off", "released"))
+}
+R.check(
+    "write_supply with the switch already on, the optimizer off or the entry released writes the switch alone",
+    all(_mb_direct[k] == [("switch", "turn_on")] for k in (("on", "auto"), ("off", "off"), ("off", "released"))),
+    f"{_mb_direct}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: write_supply with the switch off and the optimizer on writes the mode first",
+    _mb_direct[("off", "auto")] == [("select", "select_option"), ("switch", "turn_on")],
+    f"{_mb_direct}",
+)
+# The lead loads the persisted record before its write, as a pass does, so
+# the pass's own load cannot overwrite the record of the mode just written.
+_mb_loaded = {duty: _asyncio.run(_mb_run(via="direct", duty=duty))[3] for duty in ("control", "observe")}
+R.check(
+    "a lead write loads the persisted record before it writes",
+    _mb_loaded["control"] is True,
+    f"{_mb_loaded}",
+)
+R.check(

+    _mb_loaded["observe"] is False,
+    f"{_mb_loaded}",
+)
+_mb_dis = {dis: _asyncio.run(_mb_run(via="direct", space=True, disinfect=dis))[2] for dis in (True, False)}
+R.check(
+    "the mode written ahead of a switch-on for a heating step under a held disinfection is Heating + DHW",
+    _mb_dis[True] == ["Heating + DHW"],
+    f"{_mb_dis}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: the same heating step with no disinfection leads with Heating",
+    _mb_dis[False] == ["Heating"],
+    f"{_mb_dis}",
+)
+_mb_nulls = {
+    "no mode entity": {"mode_entity": False},
+    "duty mode observe": {"duty": "observe"},
+    "supply already on": {"switch": "on", "select": "Heating"},
+}
+for _mb_name, _mb_kw in _mb_nulls.items():
+    _mb_with = {via: _asyncio.run(_mb_run(via=via, **_mb_kw))[0] for via in ("cycle", "tick")}
+    _mb_without = {via: _asyncio.run(_mb_run(lead=False, via=via, **_mb_kw))[0] for via in ("cycle", "tick")}
+    R.check(
+        f"null control, {_mb_name}: the service calls and their order are today's",
+        _mb_with == _mb_without and any(("switch", "turn_on") in c for c in _mb_with.values()),
+        f"with {_mb_with}; without {_mb_without}",
+    )

 _sa_record = {"written": {
@@ -82183,6 +83042,472 @@ for _ms_name, _ms_kw, _ms_want in (
     )
 
 
+R.section("supply switch: minimum run and pause, restart")
+# A re-solve, a cycle or a step tick inside a step must neither stop the
+# compressor minutes after it started nor start it minutes after it stopped
+# (``supply_hold.hold_supply``): the gate holds the write back and the step
+# tick writes it once MIN_RUN / MIN_PAUSE has passed. Both are measured on the
+# switch's own ``last_changed``, whoever moved it. The real coordinator writes;
+# each tick fires every minute.
+import importlib
+import logging
+
+_sh = importlib.import_module(_sa_pa.__package__ + ".supply_hold")
+_sh_coord_mod = importlib.import_module(_sa_pa.__package__ + ".coordinator")
+
+_sh_off = lambda _held, _inputs, _boosts, value, now=None: value  # main: no gate
+
+
+async def _ms_run(duties, switch, events, until=20, off_at=None, entity="switch.hp",
+                  plan=True, sysid=False, gate=True, every=False):
+    """Switch writes by minute from 06:00 for a plan of ``duties`` (``s`` on).
+
+    ``switch`` is the switch's state and since-minute at 06:00 (negative is
+    before); ``events`` maps a minute to the action the cycle adopts there;
+    at ``off_at`` the optimizer is switched off. ``plan=False`` runs with no
+    plan, ``sysid`` under system identification, ``gate=False`` with main's
+    write (no gate); ``every`` returns every service call, not only the
+    switch's, and the learners' freeze reason at the end.
+    """
+    ticks = []
+    armed, real = _sa_pa.async_track_time_interval, _sh_coord_mod.supply_hold.hold_supply
+    _sa_pa.async_track_time_interval = lambda _h, fn, _i: (ticks.append(fn), (lambda: None))[1]
+    if not gate:
+        _sh_coord_mod.supply_hold.hold_supply = _sh_off
+    domain = entity.split(".", 1)[0] if entity else None
+    hass = FakeHass({} if not entity else {entity: FakeState(switch[0], last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=switch[1]))})
+    coord = Coord(hass, FakeEntry(data={**_LC_DATA, "heat_pump_switch_entity": entity, "pump_duty_mode": "observe"}))
+    coord._mode = "auto"
+    coord._optimization_result = SimpleNamespace(
+        timestamps=[_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=15 * i) for i in range(len(duties))],
+        power_schedule=[1.5 if c == "s" else 0.0 for c in duties],
+        dhw_power_schedule=[0.0] * len(duties), optimal_setpoints=[21.0] * len(duties)) if plan else None
+    writes, frozen = [], None
+    try:
+        for m in range(until + 1):
+            now = _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=m)
+            _sa_dt.freeze(now)
+            coord._last_optimization = now
+            coord._mode = "off" if off_at is not None and m >= off_at else coord._mode
+            if m in events:
+                _sa_boost.adopt_plan(coord, {"heat_pump_on": events[m], "power": 1.5 * events[m]})
+                if sysid:
+                    coord._current_action = {**coord._current_action, "mode": "system_identification"}
+                if plan:
+                    coord._optimization_result.power_schedule[m // 15] = 1.5 * events[m]
+                await coord._apply_action()
+            for tick in ([] if m in events else list(ticks)):
+                await tick(now)
+            for d, service, data in hass.services.calls:
+                if every:
+                    writes.append((m, d, service, dict(data)))
+                if d == domain and data.get("entity_id") == entity:
+                    writes.append((m, service)) if not every else None
+                    on = service == "turn_on"
+                    new = ("heat" if on else "off") if domain == "climate" else ("on" if on else "off")
+                    if hass.states.get(entity).state != new:  # async_set keeps last_changed
+                        hass.states.set(entity, FakeState(new, last_updated=now))
+            hass.services.calls.clear()
+        frozen = _sh_coord_mod._tail_freeze(coord)
+    finally:
+        _sa_dt.freeze(None)
+        _sa_pa.async_track_time_interval = armed
+        _sh_coord_mod.supply_hold.hold_supply = real
+    return (writes, frozen) if every else writes
+
+
+# The cycle at 06:00 switches on; a re-solve at 06:03 turns the step off.
+_ms_short = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 3: False}, until=14))
+_ms_long = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 12: False}, until=14))
+R.check(
+    "a re-solve three minutes into a run does not switch the supply off; the step tick does at MIN_RUN",
+    _ms_short == [(0, "turn_on"), (10, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_short}",
+)
+_ms_off = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 3: False}, until=14, off_at=5))
+R.check(
+    "a write held back is not retried once the optimizer is switched off",
+    _ms_off == [(0, "turn_on")],
+    f"{_ms_off}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: the same re-solve twelve minutes into the run switches it off at once",
+    _ms_long == [(0, "turn_on"), (12, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_long}",
+)
+# A re-solve at 06:12 switches the run off; one at 06:15 turns the next step on.
+_ms_pause = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("s-", ("off", -60), {0: True, 12: False, 15: True}, until=25))
+_ms_rest = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("s-", ("off", -60), {0: True, 12: False, 23: True}, until=25))
+R.check(
+    "a re-solve three minutes into a pause does not switch the supply on; the step tick does at MIN_PAUSE",
+    _ms_pause == [(0, "turn_on"), (12, "turn_off"), (22, "turn_on")],
+    f"{_ms_pause}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: the same re-solve eleven minutes into the pause switches it on at once",
+    _ms_rest == [(0, "turn_on"), (12, "turn_off"), (23, "turn_on")],
+    f"{_ms_rest}",
+)
+# One clock: a run or a pause the gate did not write (a boost, a fixed mode,
+# the user, the cut-off) is measured on the switch's own stamp like one it
+# wrote. The switch reads on, or off, since 05:57.
+_ms_user_run = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("on", -3), {0: False}, until=12))
+_ms_user_pause = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -3), {0: True}, until=12))
+R.check(
+    "a run someone else started three minutes ago is held on until MIN_RUN of the switch's own stamp",
+    _ms_user_run == [(7, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_user_run}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "a pause someone else started three minutes ago is held off until MIN_PAUSE of the switch's own stamp",
+    _ms_user_pause == [(7, "turn_on")],
+    f"{_ms_user_pause}",
+)
+# A restart of Home Assistant stamps the switch at the restart (the
+# ``StateMachine.async_set`` contract in tests/ha_contract.py): the pump reads
+# as a run started then and is held on for MIN_RUN. A reload of the
+# integration keeps the stamp: an hour-old run is switched off at once.
+_ms_boot = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("on", 0), {0: False}, until=12))
+_ms_reload = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("on", -60), {0: False}, until=12))
+R.check(
+    "after a Home Assistant restart a supply found on is held for MIN_RUN of its restart stamp, then switched off",
+    _ms_boot == [(10, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_boot}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: after a reload an hour-old run is switched off at once",
+    _ms_reload == [(0, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_reload}",
+)
+# A held write the plan gives no command for (no plan) is retried with the
+# action's own value at the minimum, not dropped until the next cycle.
+_ms_noplan = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("on", -3), {0: False}, until=12, plan=False))
+R.check(
+    "with no plan, an OFF held three minutes into a run lands at MIN_RUN",
+    _ms_noplan == [(7, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_noplan}",
+)
+# System identification passes the gate: a step-response edge is not delayed.
+_ms_sysid = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("on", -3), {0: False}, until=12, sysid=True))
+R.check(
+    "system identification: an OFF three minutes into a run is written at once",
+    _ms_sysid == [(0, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_sysid}",
+)
+# A climate target reads heat / off; its run is held like a switch's.
+_ms_clim = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("heat", -3), {0: False}, until=12, entity="climate.hp"))
+_ms_clim_old = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("--", ("heat", -60), {0: False}, until=12, entity="climate.hp"))
+R.check(
+    "a climate target reading heat three minutes is held on until MIN_RUN",
+    _ms_clim == [(7, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_clim}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: a climate target heating an hour is switched off at once",
+    _ms_clim_old == [(0, "turn_off")],
+    f"{_ms_clim_old}",
+)
+# The learners: an interval with a held write ran other than the plan, so
+# ``_learning_frozen`` names it (``supply_hold.FREEZE_HELD``); the null
+# control is the same run with no write held.
+_ms_fz_held = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 3: False}, until=14, every=True))[1]
+_ms_fz_free = _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 12: False}, until=14, every=True))[1]
+R.check(
+    "an interval in which the gate held a write freezes the learners with the supply_held reason",
+    _ms_fz_held == _sh.FREEZE_HELD,
+    f"{_ms_fz_held!r}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "null control: the same interval with no write held does not",
+    _ms_fz_free != _sh.FREEZE_HELD,
+    f"{_ms_fz_free!r}",
+)
+# Null control, owed: with every write on a step boundary and no restart, the
+# service calls and their order are identical to main's (the gate off); an
+# install with no supply switch is untouched by the gate.
+for _ms_name, _ms_args, _ms_kw in (
+    ("writes on step boundaries", ("s-s-", ("off", -60), {0: True, 15: False, 30: True, 45: False}), {"until": 59}),
+    ("a plan the step tick moves", ("s-ss", ("off", -60), {0: True}), {"until": 59}),
+    ("no supply switch", ("s-s-", ("off", -60), {0: True, 3: False, 15: False, 31: True}), {"until": 40, "entity": None}),
+):
+    _ms_a = _asyncio.run(_ms_run(*_ms_args, every=True, **_ms_kw))[0]
+    _ms_b = _asyncio.run(_ms_run(*_ms_args, every=True, gate=False, **_ms_kw))[0]
+    R.check(
+        f"null control: {_ms_name}, the gate issues main's service calls in main's order",
+        _ms_a == _ms_b and (_ms_kw.get("entity", 1) is None or _ms_a),
+        f"{_ms_a} != {_ms_b}",
+    )
+
+
+# Rule three: an ON that starts a run the plan ends within MIN_RUN is skipped,
+# except on a hot-water step whose tank is below its minimum or under a
+# disinfection hold (``supply_hold.tank_reason``, the early cut-off's own).
+def _sh_inputs(minute, *, dhw=False, cold=False, disinfecting=False, state="off", nodhw=False):
+    hass = FakeHass({"switch.hp": FakeState(state, last_updated=_SA_T0 - timedelta(hours=1))})
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(
+        timestamps=[_SA_T0, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=15)],
+        power_schedule=[0.0 if dhw else 1.5, 0.0], dhw_power_schedule=[1.5 if dhw else 0.0, 0.0])
+    return lambda: _sa_pa.ArbiterInputs(
+        hass=hass, config={"heat_pump_switch_entity": "switch.hp"}, mode="auto", plan=plan,
+        plan_stale=False, entry_released=False,
+        state=SimpleNamespace(dhw_temperature=40.0 if cold == "edge" else 35.0 if cold else 50.0),
+        thermal=None, params=SimpleNamespace(dhw_min_temp=40.0) if nodhw else SimpleNamespace(dhw_enabled=True, dhw_min_temp=40.0),
+        action={"heat_pump_on": True}, measured_power_kw=None, disinfecting=disinfecting)
+
+
+_sh_none = SimpleNamespace(active=lambda _c, _n: False)
+
+
+def _sh_start(minute, **kw):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState()
+    got = _sh.hold_supply(held, _sh_inputs(minute, **kw), _sh_none, True, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=minute))
+    return got, held.supply_held
+
+
+for _ms_name, _ms_min, _ms_kw, _ms_want in (
+    ("a space step, ON at minute 7 before an OFF step", 7, {}, (None, True)),
+    ("null control: the same ON at minute 5, MIN_RUN before the boundary", 5, {}, (True, False)),
+    ("a hot-water step with the tank warm", 7, {"dhw": True}, (None, True)),
+    ("a hot-water step with the tank below its minimum", 7, {"dhw": True, "cold": True}, (True, False)),
+    ("a hot-water step under a disinfection hold", 7, {"dhw": True, "disinfecting": True}, (True, False)),
+    ("a space step with the tank below its minimum", 7, {"cold": True}, (None, True)),
+    ("null control: the switch already on", 7, {"state": "on"}, (True, False)),
+    ("an unreadable switch", 7, {"state": "unavailable"}, (True, False)),
+    ("a hot-water step with the tank exactly at its minimum (not below)", 7, {"dhw": True, "cold": "edge"}, (None, True)),
+    ("a cold tank on params with no dhw_enabled field is not exempt", 7, {"dhw": True, "cold": True, "nodhw": True}, (None, True)),
+):
+    _ms_got = _sh_start(_ms_min, **_ms_kw)
+    R.check(f"rule three: {_ms_name} -> {_ms_want}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got}")
+
+
+# A write of None (cooling, both channels blocked) is passed and marks nothing
+# held, even on a run three minutes old.
+_sh_nheld = _sa_pa.ArbiterState()
+_sh_nin = _sh_inputs(7, state="on")
+_sh_nin().hass.states.set("switch.hp", FakeState("on", last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=4)))
+_sh_ngot = (_sh.hold_supply(_sh_nheld, _sh_nin, _sh_none, None, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7)), _sh_nheld.supply_held, _sh_nheld.held_until)
+R.check("a write of None passes and marks nothing held", _sh_ngot == (None, False, None), f"{_sh_ngot}")
+
+
+# A held write whose command is gone (the optimizer switched off) is dropped
+# by the step tick, flag and all; the null control keeps it in a plan mode.
+async def _sh_tick(mode):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState(supply=(_SA_T0, False), supply_held=True)
+    inp = _sh_inputs(3, state="on")()
+    inp = _sa_pa.ArbiterInputs(**{**vars(inp), "mode": mode, "plan": None, "action": {"heat_pump_on": False}})
+    wrote = []
+
+    async def _write(on):
+        wrote.append(on)
+
+    await _sa_pa.supply_tick(held, _sa_pa.SupplyWiring(lambda: inp, _sh_none, _write), _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=3))
+    return wrote, held.supply_held
+
+
+for _ms_name, _ms_mode, _ms_want in (
+    ("the optimizer switched off: no write, the hold dropped", "off", ([], False)),
+    ("null control: a plan mode with no plan retries the action's OFF", "auto", ([False], True)),
+):
+    _ms_got = _asyncio.run(_sh_tick(_ms_mode))
+    R.check(f"step tick, held write: {_ms_name}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got}")
+
+
+# An unreadable switch passes an OFF the gate would hold on a readable one;
+# a stamp ahead of the clock is an unknown age and holds nothing (#775).
+def _sh_stop(state, minutes_ago):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState()
+    inputs = _sh_inputs(7, state=state)
+    inputs().hass.states.set("switch.hp", FakeState(state, last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7 - minutes_ago)))
+    got = _sh.hold_supply(held, inputs, _sh_none, False, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7))
+    return got, held.supply_held
+
+
+for _ms_name, _ms_args, _ms_want in (
+    ("an OFF to a switch reading unavailable passes", ("unavailable", 3), (False, False)),
+    ("an OFF to a switch reading unknown passes", ("unknown", 3), (False, False)),
+    ("an OFF to a switch stamped ahead of the clock passes", ("on", -3), (False, False)),
+    ("null control: an OFF to a switch on three minutes is held", ("on", 3), (None, True)),
+    ("an OFF to a switch stamped this instant is held (age 0, not unknown)", ("on", 0), (None, True)),
+):
+    _ms_got = _sh_stop(*_ms_args)
+    R.check(f"stop: {_ms_name} -> {_ms_want}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got}")
+
+
+# The learners' freeze spans two plan intervals from the last held write,
+# fixed at the hold from its config; a config with no interval reads the default
+# interval, and nothing held reads nothing.
+def _sh_fz_hold(config):
+    held, inputs = _sa_pa.ArbiterState(), _sh_inputs(7, state="on")
+    inputs().hass.states.set("switch.hp", FakeState("on", last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=4)))
+    inp = _sa_pa.ArbiterInputs(**{**vars(inputs()), "config": config})
+    _sh.hold_supply(held, lambda: inp, _sh_none, False, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7))
+    return held
+
+
+_sh_fz = _sh_fz_hold({"heat_pump_switch_entity": "switch.hp", "optimization_interval": 30})
+_sh_fz_dflt = _sh_fz_hold({"heat_pump_switch_entity": "switch.hp"})
+_SH_FZ_AT = _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7)
+for _ms_name, _ms_got, _ms_want in (
+    ("nothing held reads nothing", _sh.freeze_reason(_sa_pa.ArbiterState(), _SA_T0), None),
+    ("a write held 59 minutes ago on a 30-minute interval is frozen", _sh.freeze_reason(_sh_fz, _SH_FZ_AT + timedelta(minutes=59)), _sh.FREEZE_HELD),
+    ("null control: 60 minutes ago is not", _sh.freeze_reason(_sh_fz, _SH_FZ_AT + timedelta(minutes=60)), None),
+    ("a config with no interval reads the default", _sh_fz_dflt.held_until - _SH_FZ_AT, 2 * timedelta(minutes=_sa_pa.EntryConfig.from_mapping({}).optimization_interval)),
+):
+    R.check(f"freeze_reason: {_ms_name}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got!r}")
+
+
+# A held write is not logged as the blocked-mode skip it is not.
+class _ShLog(logging.Handler):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__(logging.DEBUG)
+        self.seen = []
+
+    def emit(self, record):
+        self.seen.append(record.getMessage())
+
+
+_sh_log, _sh_level = _ShLog(), _sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.level
+_sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.addHandler(_sh_log)
+_sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
+try:
+    _asyncio.run(_ms_run("ss", ("off", -60), {0: True, 3: False}, until=14))
+finally:
+    _sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.removeHandler(_sh_log)
+    _sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.setLevel(_sh_level)
+_sh_skips = [m for m in _sh_log.seen if m.startswith("Not switching")]
+R.check(
+    "a held OFF is not logged as the cooling or blocked-mode skip",
+    _sh_skips == [],
+    f"{_sh_skips}",
+)
+
+
+
+async def _sh_blocked_write():
+    hass = FakeHass({"switch.hp": FakeState("on", last_updated=_SA_T0 - timedelta(hours=1))})
+    coord = Coord(hass, FakeEntry(data={**_LC_DATA, "heat_pump_switch_entity": "switch.hp", "pump_duty_mode": "observe"}))
+    coord._mode = "auto"
+    coord._pump_signals = SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(coord._pump_signals), "space_blocked": True, "dhw_blocked": True})
+    _sa_dt.freeze(_SA_T0)
+    try:
+        await coord._write_supply(False)
+    finally:
+        _sa_dt.freeze(None)
+    return [c for c in hass.services.calls if c[0] == "switch"]
+
+
+_sh_log.seen.clear()
+_sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.addHandler(_sh_log)
+_sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
+try:
+    _sh_bcalls = _asyncio.run(_sh_blocked_write())
+finally:
+    _sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.removeHandler(_sh_log)
+    _sh_coord_mod._LOGGER.setLevel(_sh_level)
+_sh_bskips = [m for m in _sh_log.seen if m.startswith("Not switching")]
+R.check(
+    "null control: an OFF both blocked channels skip writes nothing and is logged as the skip",
+    _sh_bcalls == [] and len(_sh_bskips) == 1,
+    f"{_sh_bcalls} {_sh_bskips}",
+)
+
+
+# Which writes the gate holds, one input changed at a time against a held
+# write: the plan modes and the boosts (``supply_hold._passes``), rule
+# three's window one tick inside it and its hot-water exemption on a "both"
+# step (``_ends_soon``), and the step tick's retry where the cycle would
+# write nothing (``supply_tick``, ``_action_supply``).
+def _sh_at(minute, value, since_min, state, mode="auto", boosts=None):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState()
+    base = _sh_inputs(minute, state=state)()
+    base.hass.states.set("switch.hp", FakeState(state, last_updated=_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=since_min)))
+    inp = _sa_pa.ArbiterInputs(**{**vars(base), "mode": mode})
+    got = _sh.hold_supply(held, lambda: inp, boosts or _sh_none, value, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=minute))
+    return got, held.supply_held
+
+
+def _sh_both(cold):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState()
+    inp = _sh_inputs(7, dhw=True, cold=cold)()
+    inp.plan.power_schedule[0] = 1.5
+    got = _sh.hold_supply(held, lambda: inp, _sh_none, True, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7))
+    return got, held.supply_held, _sa_pa.step_duty(inp.plan, _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=7))
+
+
+_sh_boost_mod = importlib.import_module(_sa_pa.__package__ + ".boost")
+_sh_boost = lambda ch: SimpleNamespace(active=lambda c, _n: c == ch)  # noqa: E731
+for _ms_name, _ms_got, _ms_want in (
+    ("economy is a plan mode: an OFF three minutes into a run is held", _sh_at(12, False, 9, "on", mode="economy"), (None, True)),
+    ("a fixed mode (comfort) passes an OFF three minutes into a run", _sh_at(12, False, 9, "on", mode="comfort"), (False, False)),
+    ("a live space boost passes an ON three minutes into a pause", _sh_at(2, True, -1, "off", boosts=_sh_boost(_sh_boost_mod.CHANNEL_SPACE)), (True, False)),
+    ("a live DHW boost passes an ON three minutes into a pause", _sh_at(2, True, -1, "off", boosts=_sh_boost(_sh_boost_mod.CHANNEL_DHW)), (True, False)),
+    ("null control: no boost holds that ON", _sh_at(2, True, -1, "off"), (None, True)),
+    ("rule three: an ON at minute 6, one tick inside MIN_RUN of an OFF step, is skipped", _sh_start(6), (None, True)),
+    ("rule three: a both step with the tank below its minimum is exempt", _sh_both(True), (True, False, "both")),
+    ("rule three: null control: a both step with the tank warm is skipped", _sh_both(False), (None, True, "both")),
+):
+    R.check(f"which writes are held: {_ms_name} -> {_ms_want}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got}")
+
+
+async def _sh_tick_over(**over):
+    held = _sa_pa.ArbiterState(supply=(_SA_T0, False), supply_held=True)
+    inp = _sh_inputs(3, state="on")()
+    inp = _sa_pa.ArbiterInputs(**{**vars(inp), "plan": None, "action": {"heat_pump_on": False}, **over})
+    wrote = []
+
+    async def _write(on):
+        wrote.append(on)
+
+    await _sa_pa.supply_tick(held, _sa_pa.SupplyWiring(lambda: inp, _sh_none, _write), _SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=3))
+    return wrote, held.supply_held
+
+
+for _ms_name, _ms_over, _ms_want in (
+    ("the entry released: no write, the hold dropped", {"entry_released": True}, ([], False)),
+    ("a stale plan: no write, the hold dropped", {"plan_stale": True}, ([], False)),
+    ("economy with no plan retries the action's OFF", {"mode": "economy"}, ([False], True)),
+):
+    _ms_got = _asyncio.run(_sh_tick_over(**_ms_over))
+    R.check(f"step tick, held write: {_ms_name}", _ms_got == _ms_want, f"{_ms_got}")
+
+
+# An install with no power switch: the gate reads no switch. Upstream's
+# ``StateMachine.get`` lowers a missed entity id, so ``get(None)`` raises
+# (tests/ha_contract.py, "StateMachine.get(None) raises"); FakeStates returns
+# None, so this install's states read as upstream's do.
+class _ShUpstreamStates:
+    def __init__(self, states):
+        self._states = dict(states)
+
+    def get(self, entity_id):
+        return self._states.get(entity_id) or self._states.get(entity_id.lower())
+
+    def set(self, entity_id, state):
+        self._states[entity_id] = state
+
+
+async def _sh_no_switch():
+    hass = FakeHass({})
+    hass.states = _ShUpstreamStates({})
+    coord = Coord(hass, FakeEntry(data=dict(_LC_DATA)))
+    coord._mode = "auto"
+    _sa_dt.freeze(_SA_T0 + timedelta(minutes=3))
+    try:
+        await coord._write_supply(True)
+        await coord._write_supply(False)
+    finally:
+        _sa_dt.freeze(None)
+    return [c for c in hass.services.calls if c[0] == "switch"], _sa_pa.state_for(coord).supply_held
+

+try:
+    _sh_ns = _asyncio.run(_sh_no_switch())
+except Exception as _sh_err:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the check reports what raised
+    _sh_ns = repr(_sh_err)
+R.check("an install with no power switch: the gate writes and holds nothing, and raises nothing",
+        _sh_ns == ([], False), f"{_sh_ns}")
+

+# ceiling raises a notice. The solve is not changed: the notice is the whole fix.
+def _vt_dhw_kwh(target):

+                                   buffer_tank_temperature=50.0, dhw_temperature=50.0,
+                                   outdoor_temperature=0.0),
+        prices=_CT_PRICES, outdoor_temps=np.full(96, 0.0), wind_speeds=np.zeros(96),
+        precipitation=np.zeros(96), solar_radiation=np.zeros(96),

diff --git a/tests/ha_contract.py b/tests/ha_contract.py
index 82635af2b1..74edeb0a0a 100644
--- a/tests/ha_contract.py
+++ b/tests/ha_contract.py
@@ -1094,6 +1094,64 @@ def _error_generated_message():
     assert err.args == ("k",)
 
 
+@contract(
+    "homeassistant.core.StateMachine",
+    "a restart's first write stamps last_changed anew, whatever state it restores",
+    cite="core.py StateMachine.async_set -- no last_changed parameter; a new state is stamped at the write",
+    expect="real",
+)
+def _restart_stamps_last_changed():
+    # supply_hold measures a run on the switch's last_changed: after a restart
+    # a pump found running reads as a run that started at the restart.
+    import asyncio
+    import tempfile
+    from datetime import timedelta
+
+    from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, State
+    from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+
+    async def main():
+        hass = HomeAssistant(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+        restored = State("switch.hp", "on", last_changed=dt_util.utcnow() - timedelta(hours=1))
+        before = dt_util.utcnow()
+        try:
+            hass.states.async_set("switch.hp", restored.state, restored.attributes)
+            written = hass.states.get("switch.hp")
+        finally:
+            await hass.async_stop(force=True)
+        assert written.state == "on"
+        assert written.last_changed >= before > restored.last_changed
+
+    asyncio.run(main())
+
+
+@contract(
+    "homeassistant.core.StateMachine",
+    "StateMachine.get(None) raises",
+    cite="core.py StateMachine.get -- a miss retries entity_id.lower()",
+    expect="real",
+)
+def _get_none_raises():
+    # pump_arbiter.supply_switch reads no switch on an install without one;
+    # tests/features.py's no-switch install reads states as upstream does.
+    import asyncio
+    import tempfile
+
+    from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+
+    async def main():
+        hass = HomeAssistant(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+        try:
+            hass.states.get(None)
+        except AttributeError:
+            return
+        finally:
+            await hass.async_stop(force=True)
+        raise AssertionError("StateMachine.get(None) returned")
+
+    asyncio.run(main())
+
+
 @contract(
     "homeassistant.exceptions.ServiceValidationError",
     "subclasses HomeAssistantError",

+
 def throwaway_git_env(base: dict | None = None) -> dict:
     """The environment for every git call into a throwaway repository."""

            if k not in LOCAL_ENV and not _INHERITED_PAIR.match(k)}
-    env.update(IDENTITY, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
+    env.update(IDENTITY, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=NO_GLOBAL_CONFIG, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
                GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=str(len(CONFIG)))

                                   capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()

+                             env=dict(throwaway_git_env(), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=str(junk)))

+                             env=throwaway_git_env())
+        check("a non-empty file as the global config fails git init (null control); the env's path inits",
+              old.returncode != 0 and new.returncode == 0, f"{old.returncode}/{new.returncode}")
         check("git reads auto-maintenance off, and gc.auto 0, through the env",

         bare = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("GIT_")}

         check("the shell twin's throwaway_git_env sets exactly the same GIT_ variables",

+              r.returncode == 0 and both_set and mine == theirs, f"py-only {set(mine.items()) - set(theirs.items())}, "
               f"sh-only {set(theirs.items()) - set(mine.items())}")
+        # The global config path is one no process can create or hold bytes at: its parent

+        homes = Path(td) / "home"

+        host = dict(bare, HOME=str(homes), XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(homes / ".config"))

+        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", '. ./throwaway_git.sh && cd "$1" && throwaway_git_env; '

+              and read("core.keep", inherited) == "1" and not created, created)
+        check("each side's GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is a path under its own regular file, which no process "

+        rs = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", '. "$1"; throwaway_git_env; throwaway_git_init "$2" -q',
+                             "_", str(twin), str(Path(td) / "rs")], env=fresh, capture_output=True, text=True)
+        check("a python and a shell process that built the env leave nothing in TMPDIR",
+              rp.returncode == 0 and rs.returncode == 0 and not any(scratch.iterdir()),
+              f"{rp.returncode}/{rs.returncode} {sorted(x.name for x in scratch.iterdir())} {rp.stderr}{rs.stderr}")

+def rollup_walk(fetch, head: str, max_pages: int = gh_read.MAX_PAGES):
+    """Every page of the rollup's contexts as ONE ROLLUP_Q-shaped payload
+    (R10-HOTFIX-TRAIN-CONTEXT-PAGES): a required context past the first 100 was
+    never seen, and platform_gate read such a head `unread`, a green approved
+    head refused. `fetch(cursor)` is one read (None for the first page) and
+    returns the parsed answer or raises ValueError/OSError; the walk follows
+    `endCursor` and stops on the first page whose answer carries no rollup or
+    is at another head, returning that payload for platform_gate to call
+    unread. A walk past <max_pages> returns the merge with hasNextPage still
+    true: refused as unread, never truncated. One read per page, so a head of
+    one page makes the one read it always did."""
+    merged, cursor = None, None
+    for _ in range(max_pages):
+        payload = fetch(cursor)
+        try:
+            commit = payload["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["commits"]["nodes"][0]["commit"]
+            ctx = commit["statusCheckRollup"]["contexts"]
+            more, cursor = ctx["pageInfo"]["hasNextPage"], ctx["pageInfo"].get("endCursor")
+        except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
+            return payload
+        if commit.get("oid") != head:
+            return payload
+        if merged is None:
+            merged = payload
+        else:
+            have = merged["data"]["repository"]["pullRequest"]["commits"]["nodes"][0]["commit"]["statusCheckRollup"]["contexts"]
+            have["nodes"] = list(have["nodes"]) + list(ctx["nodes"])
+            have["pageInfo"] = ctx["pageInfo"]
+        if not more or not cursor:
+            return merged
+    return merged

+def quiet_log(full: Path, out=print, tail: int = QUIET_TAIL):
+    """The train's quiet log (owner card 2026-10-24): every line goes to `full`;
+    stdout gets every line but the named chatter (QUIET_CHATTER), and a

diff --git a/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py b/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
index cac4c29228..f12d47539e 100644
--- a/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
+++ b/tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py
@@ -128,6 +128,40 @@ def sizes(durations: dict) -> tuple:
     except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
         raise SchemaError(f"{DURATIONS} carries no sizes_hours table: {e}")
 
+#: A group's owner-stated price (R10-HOTFIX-PLAN-OWNER-PRICE): minutes the
+#: owner ruled for the group, and the text of the ruling. The planner reads
+#: them (`replan.group_hours`), the editor writes them (`roster_edit set-price`),
+#: and both ask `owner_price_why` -- one definition of a writable price.
+OWNER_PRICE_MINUTES = "owner_price_minutes"
+OWNER_PRICE_CITE = "owner_price_cite"
+
+
+def owner_price_why(minutes, cite) -> str | None:
+    """Why (`minutes`, `cite`) is not an owner-stated price, or None. A price
+    is a positive number of minutes (a bool is no number) beside a non-blank
+    citation text: a price nobody can trace to the owner is a fabricated
+    measurement."""
+    if isinstance(minutes, bool) or not isinstance(minutes, (int, float)) \
+            or not minutes > 0 or minutes == float("inf"):
+        return f"an owner price is a positive number of minutes, not {minutes!r}"
+    if not isinstance(cite, str) or not cite.strip():
+        return "an owner price needs a citation text naming the owner's words"
+    return None
+
+
+def owner_price(group: dict) -> tuple[float, str] | None:
+    """(minutes, citation) of a group's owner-stated price, None when it has
+    none. One field without the other, or an invalid pair, is a SchemaError:
+    a half-written price is never read as no price."""
+    m, c = group.get(OWNER_PRICE_MINUTES), group.get(OWNER_PRICE_CITE)
+    if m is None and c is None:
+        return None
+    why = owner_price_why(m, c)
+    if why:
+        raise SchemaError(f"{group.get('group')}: {why}")
+    return float(m), c.strip()
+
+

+// The members are data, not source: tools/policy/legacy_control_files.json, which no check pins, so a
+// repair that delists a member is one pull request. The cap stays here. Fail-closed: an unreadable or
+// malformed file yields an empty set, so every listed carry is linted with the control rules.
+const LEGACY_CONTROL_DATA = path.join(HERE, 'legacy_control_files.json')
+function readLegacyControlFiles() {
+  try {
+    const d = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(LEGACY_CONTROL_DATA, 'utf8'))
+    return new Set(Array.isArray(d.files) ? d.files.filter((x) => typeof x === 'string') : [])

+  }

 export function lintCarryFile(file, { roster, legacy = LEGACY_CONTROL_FILES } = {}) {
   const findings = []
@@ -1453,6 +1461,17 @@ function assertCarryFixtures() {
 //    covers is refused by lintCarryFile with no roster handed in (a carry at 999999 is not: null control);
 //  - LEGACY_CONTROL_FILES only shrinks: its size is at most LEGACY_CONTROL_CAP, and every member still has a
 //    control error when linted without the exemption (a repaired file must be removed from the set).
+export function staleLegacyMembers(labels, files) {
+  const problems = []
+  for (const label of labels) {
+    const f = files.get(label)
+    if (!f) { problems.push(`${label} is in LEGACY_CONTROL_FILES and in no carry directory: remove it`); continue }
+    const errs = lintCarryFile(f, { roster: new Map(), legacy: new Set() }).filter((x) => x.severity === 'error' && / control/.test(x.group))
+    if (!errs.length) problems.push(`${label}: its controls lint clean without the exemption: remove it from LEGACY_CONTROL_FILES`)
+  }
+  return problems
+}

   return 0
 }
 
+// A listed-but-clean file is still refused (the data file's own guard): a carry whose controls lint
+// clean without the exemption is reported by staleLegacyMembers, a carry that still needs it is not
+// (null control), and a check that reports nothing -- the mutant -- is told apart by this arm.
+function assertLegacyListedClean() {
+  const problems = []
+  const clean = path.join(FIXTURES, 'carry-990001.json')
+  const tmp = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'legacyclean-'))
+  const bad = path.join(tmp, 'carry-990001.json')
+  const model = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(clean, 'utf8'))
+  fs.writeFileSync(bad, JSON.stringify({ ...model, carries: model.carries.map((c) => ({ ...c, control: 'a plain sentence that names no path at all' })) }))
+  const staleOf = (check, f) => check([path.posix.basename(f)], new Map([[path.posix.basename(f), f]]))
+  const mutant = () => []
+  const hit = (check) => staleOf(check, clean).length
+  if (!hit(staleLegacyMembers)) problems.push('a listed carry whose controls lint clean is not refused')
+  try {
+    if (staleOf(staleLegacyMembers, bad).length) problems.push('a listed carry that still needs the exemption is refused (null control)')
+  } finally {
+    fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true })
+  }
+  if (hit(mutant)) problems.push('the vacuous check is not told apart from the real one')
+  if (problems.length) {
+    console.log('\nLEGACY-LISTED-CLEAN VACUOUS:')
+    for (const m of problems) console.log(`  ${m}`)
+    return 1
+  }
+  console.log('\nLEGACY-LISTED-CLEAN ok: a listed carry that lints clean is refused, one that needs the exemption is not, and the vacuous check is told apart')
+  return 0
+}

+#: The ref a running stamp publishes (`STAMP_HOLD_REF` in merge_train.py): the
+#: train waits on it before a merge attempt, so main does not move under the gate.
+STAMP_HOLD_REF = "refs/heads/stamp-hold"

+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def stamp_hold(armed: bool, key: str | None = None, known_hosts: str | None = None, push=None, runner=None):
+    """Hold main while a pushing stamp runs: a commit made NOW (its committer date
+    is the hold's age, which the train reads) is force-pushed to STAMP_HOLD_REF
+    and deleted on exit, a refusal included. A refused take or release is a
+    warning, never a stop: the hold guards the train's merges, and the train
+    takes over a hold past its own age bound. `armed` False (no --push, a dry
+    run) touches nothing."""

+        return

+        commit = runner("git", "commit-tree", tree, "-p", "HEAD", "-m", f"stamp hold pid={os.getpid()}").strip()
+        push(f"+{commit}:{STAMP_HOLD_REF}", key, known_hosts)
+        print(f"STAMP HOLD {STAMP_HOLD_REF} {commit[:8]}: the train waits")
+    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError) as exc:
+        print(f"WARNING: stamp hold not taken ({exc}); the train is not held", file=sys.stderr)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        try:

+        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError) as exc:
